Full job description


Description

Apply Today Training Classes Begin in January 2027!

Looking for a career in insurance? Join our Inside Sales team and get free P&C license training with paid training time. Start your rewarding career today!

Key Date:

  • Licensed Class: January 11, 2027
  • Unlicensed Class: January 25, 2027

Start your journey with us and build a career where your talent and passion for helping others truly make an impact.

As an Inside Sales Representative at Liberty Mutual, youll have the tools, training and support you need to succeed from day one.

Plus, youll enjoy:

  • Generous earning potential
  • Paid licensing and training opportunities
  • Comprehensive benefits
  • Flexible work arrangements
  • Strong work-life balance
  • And more!

Why Liberty Mutual?

Pay Details:

  • Starting base salary is $45K with opportunity for growth.
  • Average earnings range from $55K-$75K through a combination of base salary and generouscommission.
  • Top Performing Agents in their second year and onward, can earn up to $85k+.

We are currently hiring quality Inbound sales professionals in the following states:AR, AZ, FL, GA, IA, ID, IN, KS, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MO, NC, NE, NH, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, andWV

Licensed only candidates based in ID, MT, WY, GA, TN, AL, OK, KS and KY. Applicants must reside within these specified locations to be considered for this role.

Positivity. Flexibility. Determination and a persuasive personality. Qualities like these cannot be taught. But they can be sharpened, strengthened, and appropriately compensated when you join Liberty Mutual Insurance as a part of our Contact Center Sales Organization. Bring your unique sales talent to our Fortune 100 company and receive paid-training, licensing in all 50 states, and a dynamic role that directs only warm leads your way (no cold calls) because we believe in supporting your success, not holding it back. Join our sales team and realize the rewards of a career with unlimited earning potential, generous commissions, and a portfolio of benefits that start on day one.

Job Details

As an Inside Sales Agent, you will be handling inbound calls and warm leads, consulting with customers on their insurance needs and match the correct coverages, products, and benefits to convert sales leads into policyholders.

Due to state licensing restrictions, employees must remain in their resident state for at least one year before relocating.

Youd be a great fit if you are:

A Passionate Seller:When a lead comes in, you skillfully pick up the phone and use your sales expertise to turn prospects into happy, confident Liberty Mutualpolicyholders.

A Front Lines Liaison:You rise to the role of representing the Liberty brand, you believe in what youre selling, and you enjoy connecting customers to the right products for their individual needs.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

Position Details:

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

  • Training extends over a period of 16 weeks for licensed hires and 18 weeks for unlicensed hires.
  • Comprehensive medical benefits from Day 1.
  • No cold calls, all incoming warm leads.
  • Opportunities for rewards and recognition.

  • Must be available to work a schedule of 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day. Standard shift is 11:30-8 EST, 12:30-9 CST, or 8:30-5 PST.

  • All computer equipment is provided. Youmust be able to maintain department.Work at home (W@H) requirements whichinclude a professional workspace/room with adedicated desk and wired (cable, fiber of DSLservice) high-speed internet connection with aminimum 100 MBps download speed and 20MBps upload speed. Liberty Mutual does notsupport satellite and mobile internet services.
Qualifications
  • 2-3 years sales experience preferred. 2 yearsof sales/service-related work experiencerequired.
  • Strong, engaging interpersonal and persuasion skills needed to close sales
  • Ability to communicate well to both prospects and customers
  • Excellent analytical, decision-making and organizational skills
  • Strong typing capabilities and PC proficiency
  • Property and Casualty License required afterhire.

About this job

Liberty Mutual seeks an Executive Underwriter to manage a Major Accounts Property portfolio of complex monoline accounts with minimum TIVs of $100m in the Central Region. The role involves analyzing property exposures, determining terms and conditions, collaborating with Risk Engineering, and mentoring other underwriters.

Full job description


Description

We are seeking an Executive Underwriter to manage and maintain a significant portion of our Major Accounts Property portfolio in the Central Region. In this role, you will be responsible for handling complex monoline Property accounts with minimum TIVs of $100m, analyzing the customer's property exposures, hazards, financial information, requested coverages, loss history, pricing targets and desired program structure to select business and determine appropriate terms and conditions. Will work closely with Risk Engineering to produce and manage a profitable book of business and manage producer/customer relationships. Maintains the highest level of skills/knowledge in the large property space with average account annual premium of around $1m. Shares underwriting expertise with other underwriters and stakeholders across all levels.

Responsibilities

  • Manages portfolio of brokers/agents & clients. Leverages market presence and expertise to develop and underwrite profitable business, acting as a representative for Liberty.
  • Has relationships with senior/market-leading brokers and/or key agents. Maintains a strong market presence, including established relationships with agents and brokers.
  • Looks to strengthen these relationships and develop new ones.
  • Articulates key coverage differences with a high degree of detail. Provides significant input into the business and marketing planning process, including advanced data-driven insights from portfolio analysis.
  • Participates in projects across departments designed to drive underwriting and process excellence (e.g., member of a working team).
  • Models effective collaboration across teams, stakeholders and partners (e.g., UW Support, Claims, Actuarial, Directors of Underwriting in North America).
  • Has strong knowledge of key legal cases, legislation and regulation impacting area(s) of underwriting expertise. Shares knowledge based on technical expertise, including providing external thought-leadership.
  • Mentors, coaches, and trains other underwriters and internal partners.
Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Prior single carrier property underwriting experience preferred.
  • Prior experience working with property risk engineering and/or loss prevention preferred.
  • Prior property facultative reinsurance or shared and layer property experience also will be considered.
  • Degree in Business or equivalent typically required
  • A minimum of 5 years expected, typically 7 years or more, of progressive underwriting experience and/or other related business experience
  • CPCU or professional insurance designation preferred
  • Proven analytical ability to evaluate and judge underwriting risks within scope of responsibility
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analyses and information in understandable written and/or oral directives to other persons in the organization for underwriting or training purposes
  • Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills in dealing with internal and external stakeholders
  • Must demonstrate comprehension of most complex technical underwriting issues and be capable of defining and implementing necessary underwriting and administrative processes/workflows to properly manage or administer those issues
  • Proven track record of developing and underwriting profitable business

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 3+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Senior Quantitative Analyst role in Liberty Mutual Investments' Global Liquid Markets unit, applying quantitative methods and machine learning to fixed-income strategy development. Work with Portfolio Managers and Traders on portfolio construction, performance analysis, and systematic strategy development.

Good fit if you have 3+ years in portfolio analysis or systematic fixed-income investing, with hands-on Python and SQL experience.

Full job description


Description

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) manages Liberty Mutual Insurance Groups (LMIG) global financial assets across public and private markets to build capital and generate income. With over $100 billion in assets under management and a team of more than 300 investment, finance, and operations professionals based in Boston, MA, LMI offers the best of both worlds: the entrepreneurial spirit of a boutique investment firm backed by the reputation and financial strength of a global leader.

LMI is on a transformational journey to foster innovation, build on our deep expertise, and further scale returns on our long-term capital through a one firm, one portfolio, one team approach. Our operating model is built on three pillars: centralized portfolio construction, asset management, and investment-enabling services. Teams are organized into Investment Business Units (IBUs): Strategy & Asset Allocation, Risk Management, Global Fixed Income, Global Private Investments, and Global Investment Solutions. Our portfolio spans a wide range of asset classes, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and toolkit to deliver on our mission.

We are seeking a Senior Quantitative Analyst to join the Investment Innovation, Integration & Trading (I3T) team within the Global Liquid Markets (GLM) unit. In this role, you will apply advanced quantitative methods, data modeling, and emerging technologies to enhance investment decision-making across various fixed-income strategies. You will collaborate with team members, Portfolio Managers, and Traders to tackle high-profile projects involving portfolio construction, performance assessment, and the development of new systematic fixed income strategies. This position is pivotal in advancing our teams expertise and helping LMI thrive in the constantly evolving global financial landscape. #LMI #LM-LMI

Responsibilities

  • Quantitative Model Development Systematic Alpha Research
    Design and implement quantitative methods and tools for portfolio construction, performance & attribution, and investment strategies in collaboration with Portfolio Managers, Traders, and Risk Managers.
  • Analytics & Visualization
    Build and refine analytic models, develop robust data pipelines and interactive dashboards, leveraging advanced Python, SQL, Dash and Power BI to translate complex data sets into actionable insights.
  • Machine Learning & AI
    Employ statistical techniques, machine learning algorithms, and GPT-based solutions to improve market analysis, develop investment strategies, and enhance decision-making processes.
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement
    Proactively identify opportunities to upgrade capabilities and stay at the forefront of fixed-income analytics. Monitor industry trends, market developments, and new analytical tools to maintain a competitive edge.
  • Project Coordination
    Oversee multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality results. Maintain meticulous attention to detail and effective communication throughout all stages of project execution.
Qualifications

Qualifications

Education

  • Numerate self-starter with a bachelors degree in finance, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field ( Masters degree preferred, CFA a plus.

Experience & Technical Skills

  • 3+ years of experience in portfolio analysis or investment management, with a strong preference for systematic fixed-income experience.
  • Must have hands-on experience with Python, SQL and familiarity with BI/visualization tools (Dash, Power BI, Jupyter Notebooks).
  • Nice-to-have, Practical knowledge of machine learning and AI (including GPT-based models) and their applications in financial analysis.

Tools & Systems

  • Preferred experience with BlackRocks Aladdin, Bloomberg, and Macrobond for data extraction, portfolio monitoring, and analytics.

Soft Skills

  • Tenacious problem-solving abilities with a focus on efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Strong attention to detail and passion for learning.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated interest in investments and a desire to delve into the intricacies of fixed-income markets.

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role has IN OFFICE requirements. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, youll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed no prior insurance experience required.

Description

What youll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

What We Offer:

  • Unlimited commission and renewal income potential for earnings growth over time.
  • Full-time employment with benefits from day one, including health insurance, generous 401(k) match, and paid time off.
  • Paid training, licensing support, and ongoing development.
  • Autonomy to embrace your entrepreneurial spirit and structure your time your way.
  • Flexible work structure (hybrid office, field, and remote based on what your day requires).
  • Supportive team culture with mentorship and long-term career paths.
Qualifications

Who Were Looking For:

Day One Skills & Traits

  • Self-motivated and accountable you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive you follow through and do what you say youll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Outgoing youre comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Tech savvy youre able to learn and use technology and digital tools with ease.
  • Calm under pressure you stay composed in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.

Build a career for yourself, not by yourself. Launch a rewarding insurance sales career today.

In 2022, Comparion Insurance Agency was created to transition former Liberty Mutual exclusive agents to an agency that delivers a unique value proposition to carriers with over 2,000 agents in approximately 180 cities in 44 states. We offer customers 50 insurance companies with product breadth including auto, home, life, pet, renters, umbrella, jewelry and much more. We use our scale to deliver a first-rate customer experience through consultative insurance experts located in their communities.

Our Leadership team has over 200 years of cumulative insurance experience. At Comparion, we have a philosophy of staying close to our customers and agents, so sales leadership is located throughout the country in our larger storefronts. Comparion is owned and backed by Liberty Mutual Group, a Fortune 100 company, founded in 1912

Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. About this job

Lead a team of insurance sales agents across Northern Ohio at Comparion Insurance Agency. Drive sales growth, coach your team, and manage branch operations while earning based on team performance.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, insurance sales experience, strong communication skills, and can obtain a state property and casualty license.

Full job description


Description

As a member of the Comparion Insurance Agency, you will lead a team of Insurance Sales Agents across Northern Ohio. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role, with the goal being to better meet the needs of our customers, help improve the sales process for our reps, and to support growth and profitability of the core business by influencing and mentoring sales representatives.

This position is responsible for providing strategic guidance and coaching support to drive the expansion and optimization of the agency, including the identification and evaluation of emerging opportunities for business growth. You determine how much you earn by how well you motivate and develop your team to sell and service customers.

This is a chance to play a key role in evolving the agency while developing and maintaining effective relationships with business partners and serving as a liaison between your branch and other business areas.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive sales team towards achieving/exceeding sales metrics.
  • Develop and coach the sales team.
  • Establish long-lasting relationships with customers in order to maintain high customer retention and satisfaction.
  • Oversee operational functions of the Branch.
  • Ensure exceptional customer satisfaction and high customer retention.
  • Generate strategic and innovative ideas in order to drive new business development.
  • Facilitate an engaging environment in which agents are inspired and feel supported.
  • Manage acquisition and service cost for Branch assignment.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor`s degree or equivalent experience required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of personal lines products and services; proven success with prior sales or related experience required.
  • Must possess highly effective oral and written communication skills, including group and individual presentation, persuasion, negotiation and customer service skills.
  • Requires excellent organizational skills, effective time management, strong leadership, interpersonal and analytical skills.
  • Incumbents must have, or be able to secure, a current state license, in property, casualty and life insurance.
  • Prior supervisory experience helpful

AXIS is seeking a US Renewable Energy Claims Associate to join our Global Markets Claims team. This developmental role supports the handling of renewable energy claims under the supervision of experienced claims professionals. The successful candidate will gain practical experience in claim investigation, coverage review, reserving, stakeholder communication, and claim resolution across first-party and third-party losses.

The role will help deliver the AXIS Global Markets Claims value proposition by working with clients, brokers, external adjusters, engineers, counsel, underwriters, actuaries, and operations colleagues. The trainee will support clear communication, accurate claim administration, and a premier claims service while developing the technical judgment required for progressively broader responsibility.

The successful candidate will:

• Support the handling of US Renewable Energy claims allocated to the trainee under the supervision of senior claims professionals.
• Assist with triage of first notification of loss and the timely engagement of appropriate adjusters, engineers, counsel, and other service providers.
• Review policy wordings and claim information to identify potential coverage considerations and escalate issues for senior review.
• Assist with claim investigations, exposure assessments, reserve recommendations, and resolution planning within delegated authority and supervision requirements.
• Maintain accurate, timely, and complete claim files in accordance with AXIS policies, procedures, and service standards.
• Monitor claim activity, document next steps, follow up on outstanding information, and escalate material developments promptly.
• Work closely with clients, brokers, independent adjusters, engineers, external legal advisors, and other experts to help maintain a premier claims service.
• Engage with underwriters, actuaries, operations, and other internal stakeholders in relation to claims, reporting, and management information.
• Support the review and validation of indemnity and expense payments to help ensure accurate and timely processing.
• Develop a working knowledge of renewable energy technologies, relevant legal frameworks, policy coverage, and claims handling practices.
• Meet agreed expectations for claim quality, productivity, diary management, and claims handling cycle time.
• Continue professional development through formal training, coaching, licensing, and practical claims experience.
• Demonstrate the AXIS behaviors that support and align with AXIS values: People, Decisiveness, Excellence, and Stronger Together.
 
KEY SKILLS & ABILITIES:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience preferred.
• One to three years of experience with a US insurer, broker, claims organization, renewable energy business, engineering firm, or related industry is preferred but not essential.
• Claims adjuster license preferred; willingness and ability to obtain and maintain licenses required by applicable states.
• Interest in commercial property, renewable energy, engineering, construction, or complex claims.
• Strong analytical, numerical, and solution-focused skills, with the ability to work accurately to deadlines.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly and concisely for the intended audience.
• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
• Effective organization, planning, time management, and attention to detail.
• Ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively in a hybrid and self-directed environment.
• Proficiency with Excel, Word, and PowerPoint preferred; familiarity with Outlook, OneNote, and other Microsoft Office products is desirable.
• Integrity, professionalism, curiosity, willingness to learn, and a collaborative team approach.

About this job

Report to the Head of North America General Casualty and Workers Compensation, AXIS Re, and contribute to portfolio strategy, client engagement, and disciplined cycle management across multiple casualty classes.

Good fit if you have casualty underwriting or reinsurance experience and understand North American casualty business, treaty structures, and actuarial pricing concepts.

Full job description

This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

North America Casualty Treaty Reinsurance Underwriter


Job Family Grouping

AXIS Re - Underwriting

Job Family

AXIS Re - Underwriting | Underwriters

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

Reporting to the Head of North America General Casualty and Workers Compensation, AXIS Re, the successful candidate will underwrite and manage a portfolio of North American General Casualty and Workers Compensation Treaty Reinsurance business. The role will contribute to Business Unit profit goals, portfolio strategy, client and broker engagement, and disciplined cycle management across General Liability, Workers Compensation, Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, and other casualty classes within the team's appetite.

What will you do in this role?

· Originate, analyze, price, structure, negotiate, and underwrite North America general casualty and workers compensation treaty business in accordance with underwriting guidelines, portfolio appetite, allocated authority, and established best practices.

· Manage assigned renewals and new-business opportunities across proportional and non-proportional treaty structures, including quota share, surplus share, working excess, and catastrophe or clash protections, as applicable.

· Assess cedent strategy, management, underwriting controls, distribution, claims practices, reserving, rate adequacy, exposure trends, and historical performance to develop a clear underwriting view.

· Partner with actuarial, claims, contract wording, finance, and legal colleagues to evaluate treaty economics, key assumptions, terms and conditions, and potential volatility.

· Build and maintain strong relationships with reinsurance intermediaries and cedent clients to support profitable business origination, retention, and long-term strategic partnerships.

· Contribute to casualty strategy and portfolio management, including appetite, guidelines, aggregate and limit management, concentration monitoring, and deployment of capacity.

· Monitor market conditions and casualty loss drivers, including social inflation, litigation trends, legal and regulatory developments, medical inflation, loss-cost trends, and changes in underlying policy terms.

· Prepare clear underwriting referrals, portfolio updates, and recommendations for senior leadership and governance forums.

· Participate in cedent underwriting audits, claims reviews, stewardship meetings, and ongoing monitoring of account performance.

· Maintain accurate and timely underwriting documentation, pricing records, exposure data, and internal system entries.

· Travel to service clients, meet brokers, conduct audits, and attend industry conferences and market events.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities, and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You

You are a hands-on casualty treaty underwriting professional with strong technical judgment and a record of building and managing a complex book of reinsurance business. You understand the treaty underwriting lifecycle, from submission review and portfolio analysis through pricing, structuring, negotiation, authorization, documentation, and post-bind monitoring. You bring professional presence, commercial judgment, and the ability to communicate, influence, and build relationships that add value to the AXIS Re portfolio and support longer-term strategic initiatives.

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While there are qualifications and experiences we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge may help you succeed in this role and contribute to our goals.

What you need to have

· Demonstrated casualty underwriting, reinsurance underwriting, broking, actuarial, or related experience with a strong understanding of North American casualty business.

· Knowledge of General Casualty and Workers Compensation, with familiarity across Commercial Auto Liability, Umbrella/Excess Liability, General Liability and related casualty classes.

· Working knowledge of actuarial and pricing concepts, including experience partnering with actuarial teams to evaluate and price reinsurance treaties.

· Ability to assess exposure and experience data, loss development, rate and exposure change, limits, retentions, attachment points, and treaty economics.

· Strong grasp of underlying policy forms, reinsurance contract wording, exclusions, claims issues, and the roles of claims, actuarial, legal, accounting, and finance in the underwriting process.

· Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to audiences at all levels, including executive leadership.

· Strong analytical, negotiation, marketing, and influencing skills, with sound judgment when faced with ambiguity or changing priorities.

· Client-focused approach and flexibility in developing solutions that meet client needs while maintaining underwriting discipline.

· Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple submissions, renewals, and peak-period workflows.

· Highly collaborative and versatile, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

· Ability to initiate and independently lead defined projects and portfolio initiatives.

· Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent industry experience.

What we prefer you to have

· CPCU, ARe, ACAS, FCAS, ARM, or other relevant industry designation.

· A minimum of five years of casualty insurance, reinsurance underwriting, actuarial, claims, or broking experience.

· Experience underwriting or analyzing both proportional and non-proportional casualty treaty structures.

· Established relationships with reinsurance brokers and North American casualty insurers.

· Effective strategic relationship management and portfolio management skills.

· Advanced Excel capability, including lookup functions, PivotTables, and analysis across multiple data sets.

· Experience building dashboards or data models using Power BI.

· Experience with AI Assistants a plus.

· Based in the New York City area or another approved AXIS office location.

Role Factors

· Travel to visit clients and brokers, conduct underwriting audits, and attend industry conferences.

· Be in the office, or visiting brokers or clients, three days per week.

· Attend broker and client events as required, including evenings and some weekend travel.

What we offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $185,000 - $250,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors, including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate performance and your individual performance. You will also be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and more.

This role is exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Job Description: North America Programs/MGA Cash and Receivable Lead Manager

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

This role will be part of the North America Insurance Premium Accounting team. The team is responsible for collection of all premium receivables and cash allocations for the Insurance premium written on US writing companies – including Canada. This team is instrumental in making sure premiums are paid timely and are key to the cash flow of the company overall.

What will you do in this role?

  • Lead the North America Insurance Premium Accounting team - providing guidance on how to resolve differences/issues on cash allocations and premium receivables and assist in escalation process if required.

  • Ensure the team is following up on premium receivables and cash variances as expected. Escalate items where internal/external contacts are not responding timely

  • Work in conjunction with the internal departments and external brokers to research and resolve any outstanding issues and/or inquiries.

  • Communicate with brokers and Axis internal customers on past due premium receivables.

  • Review the overdue receivables report produced by the BPO vendor and work with Axis internal departments and/or brokers to resolve discrepancies.

  • Track the entry of the cash receipts into the premium accounting system by the BPO vendor daily while ensuring adherence to established process and delivery standards. Ensuring controls are being followed by the BPO vendor for cash processing.

  • Month-end close processing for the legacy system

  • Review and approve bank reconciliations produced by the BPO vendor

  • Review and authorize disbursement requests.

  • Assist the BPO team in researching issues.

  • Conduct other duties as assigned.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You:

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table, so while there are some qualifications and experiences, we need you to have, we are open to discussing how your individual knowledge might lend itself to fulfilling this role and help us achieve our goals.

What you need to have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance or equivalent work experience.

  • Minimum of 5 years P&C insurance industry experience

  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of related automated financial systems.

  • Demonstration of strong software skills including Excel, Access, and Outlook.

About this job

Data Insights Lead role at AXIS Capital focused on turning complex reserving data into clear insights for decision-making. You will design dashboards and analytics tools, work across Reserving and Finance teams, and help modernize how reserving analysis is produced and used.

Good fit if you have data or analytics experience in insurance, can design business solutions, and communicate complex analysis clearly to non-technical users.

Full job description

This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How This Role Contributes to Our Collective Success?

This is an opportunity to use data and analytics to make a meaningful difference to one of the most important decision-making areas at AXIS: Reserving. In this role, you will help the Reserving team turn complex data into clear, trusted insight so they can better understand trends, explain movements, and make confident decisions.

In this role, you will help us:

  • Make reserving decisions easier to understand by improving access to consistent, timely, and well-defined data.

  • Bring important trends to the surface, helping the team understand what is changing, why it matters, and where more analysis may be needed.

  • Reduce manual effort and improve the way reserving analysis is produced, shared, and used across the business.


You will help shape how reserving analytics evolves at AXIS, building practical insight capabilities that make it easier to understand portfolio movements, compare views across business areas, monitor key indicators, and support high-quality discussions with senior stakeholders.

You will work closely with colleagues across Reserving, Finance, Actuarial, Claims, Underwriting, and Data & Analytics to understand what the Reserving team needs and turn those needs into useful dashboards, datasets, self-service tools, and repeatable insight products. You will also partner with technical teams to make sure reserving data is trusted, accessible, clearly defined, and fit for decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Be a Trusted Partner to the Reserving Team

  • Build strong relationships with the Reserving team and the wider teams that use reserving information, taking time to understand their processes, challenges, priorities, and decision-making needs.

  • Help define the reserving analytics roadmap, making sure the work we prioritise delivers clear value for the Reserving team and the business.


Create Better Data Products and Insight Tools

  • Design and deliver dashboards, datasets, and self-service tools that give the Reserving team clearer views of loss development, claims experience, exposure changes, prior-year development, and other important indicators.

  • Replace static, manual reporting with more interactive insight solutions that help users explore trends, compare results, test assumptions, and identify areas for deeper review.

  • Help identify, explain and monitor reserve signals, including AvE, PYD, claims emergence, large loss activity, exposure/mix changes and reserve diagnostics.


Explore Modern Analytics and AI

  • Work with actuarial, data science, and AI colleagues to explore where modern analytics can support reserving analysis, scenario exploration, anomaly detection, and clearer explanation of key drivers.

  • Promote practical and responsible use of AI and analytics, with a focus on improving speed, transparency, and confidence while maintaining strong governance and actuarial judgement.


Inspire Through Insight

  • Create clear, intuitive visualizations that help colleagues understand reserving movements, emerging trends, portfolio changes, and areas of uncertainty.

  • Help improve how reserving insights are communicated so they are concise, consistent, and useful for actuarial, finance, management, and business discussions.


Set Standards for Excellence

  • Help define clear standards for reserving metrics, data definitions, reporting, reconciliation, and interpretation of key indicators.

  • Support high-quality, governed outputs that align with enterprise data standards, actuarial controls, and financial reporting needs.


Collaborate Across D&A

  • Collaborate with architecture, engineering, governance, finance, actuarial, claims, and underwriting colleagues so reserving needs are considered from the data foundation through to the final insight experience.

  • Look for opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual data wrangling, and build reusable insight capabilities that teams can rely on over time.

You may also be asked to take on additional responsibilities aligned with the nature and scope of this role.


About You

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience in data, analytics, actuarial, finance, or a related insurance or reinsurance role.

  • Experience helping to design, improve, or deliver data and analytics solutions for business users.

  • A deep understanding of insurance or reinsurance data, including how claims, policy, exposure, premium, underwriting, finance, and actuarial information can be used to support analysis.

  • The ability to lead through influence, work with technical teams, and bring people together around a shared outcome.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to make complex data and analysis clear, practical, and actionable.

  • Experience creating dashboards, datasets, visualizations, or self-service tools that help business users understand performance, trends, and drivers.

  • Curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, and an interest in applying them to real business problems in a practical and responsible way.

  • Familiarity with data visualization tools such as Power BI, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with reserving, actuarial, finance, claims, underwriting, or performance reporting teams.

  • Some knowledge of reserving processes, actuarial triangles, loss development, claims trends, or financial close reporting.

  • Hands-on experience with Power BI and other visualization platforms.


What Really Sets You Apart

  • You enjoy turning complex data into insight that people can trust, understand, and use.

  • You are naturally curious and like asking how analysis could be faster, clearer, more consistent, and more useful.

  • You are excited by the chance to help modernize reserving analytics at AXIS and build tools that improve confidence, transparency, and business understanding.

Role Factors


In this role, you will typically be required to:

  • Attend your local office at least three (3) days per week to meet and build relationships with colleagues and the wider business.

  • Engage in company activities to grow your network and build a strong team culture.

As a Northland Claim Litigation Specialist, you will be responsible for managing and investigating moderate complexity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight.

In this technical role, you will leverage your expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution.

You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and stakeholders on claims that may involve significant litigation or span extended periods.

You will provide guidance and mentorship to Claim Reps and Associate Claim Reps, sharing knowledge and best practices to support their development.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims which may include coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Leverage resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Actively negotiate with multiple constituents (e.g., claimants, attorneys, contractors, representatives) and convey claim settlements within authority and issue payments timely and accurately.
  • Assist in coordinating with Counsel to support litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Three years of liability, bodily injury or comparable claim experience.
  • Two years of litigation claim experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to comprehend, synthesize, and clearly articulate complex information to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and make effective decisions independently.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers; ability to manage difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to handle complex or disputed claims, negotiate settlements, and manage litigation.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Thorough understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations, fair claims practices, and legal requirements applicable to claim handling.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and clearly articulate complex policy language, endorsements, exclusions to assess coverage and claim eligibility.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Two years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. $25.00 - $26.00

Target Openings

2

What Is the Opportunity?

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role. Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

As of the date of this posting, Travelers anticipates that this posting will remain open until March 1, 2027.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

What is a Must Have?

  • Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor's degree.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

We are committed to providing accommodation to persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation during the recruitment or interview process we will work with you to accommodate your needs.

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Manage Workers' Compensation claims with lost time to conclusion and negotiate settlements where appropriate to resolve claims. Coordinate medical and indemnity position of the claim with a Medical Case Manager. Independently handles assigned claims of low to moderate complexity where Wage loss and the expectation is a return to work to modified or full duty or obtain MMI with no RTW. There are no litigated issues or minor to moderate litigated issues. The claim may involve minor sprains/ minor to moderate surgery The injured worker is working modified duty and receiving ongoing medical treatment. The injured worker as returned to work, reached Maximum Medical Improvement (MMI) and is receiving PPD benefits. File will close as soon as the PPD is paid out. With close to moderate supervision, may handle claims of greater complexity where Injured worker (IW) remains out of work and unlikely to return to position. Employer is unable to accommodate the restrictions. The claim involves moderate to complex litigation issues IW has returned to work, reached Maximum Medical Improvement (MMI), and has PPD. File litigated to dispute the permanency rating and/or causality. IW has been released to work with permanent restrictions and there has been a change in the current position. IW is receiving Vocational Rehabilitation. Claims that have been reopened for additional medical treatment on more complex files. Injuries may involve one or multiple back, shoulder or knee surgeries, knee replacements, claims involving moderate to complex offsets, permanent restrictions and/or fatalities. Claims on which a settlement should be considered.

What Will You Do?

  • Conduct investigations, including, but not limited to assessing policy coverage, contacting insureds, injured workers, medical providers, and other parties in a timely manner to determine compensability
  • Establish and update reserves to reflect claim exposure and document rationale. Identify and set actuarial reserves. Apply knowledge to determine causal relatedness of medical conditions.
  • Manage files with an emphasis on file quality (including timely contact and proper documentation and proactive resolution of outstanding issues). Achieve a positive end result by returning injured party to work and coordinating the appropriate medical treatment.in collaboration with internal nurse resources where appropriate.
  • Work in collaboration with specialty resources (i.e. medical and legal) to proactively pursue claim resolution opportunities, (i.e. return to work, structured settlement, and discontinuation of benefits through litigation). Develop strategies to manage losses involving issues of statutory benefit entitlement, medical diagnoses, Medicare Set Aside to achieve resolution through the best possible outcome.
  • Collaborate with our internal nurse resources (Medical Case Manager) in order to integrate the delivery of medical services into the overall claim strategy. Prepare necessary letters and state filings within statutory limits.
  • Pursue all offset opportunities, including apportionment, contribution and subrogation. Evaluate claims for potential fraud.Proactively manage inventory with documented plans of action to ensure timely and appropriate file closing or reassignment.
  • Effectively manage litigation to drive files to an optimal outcome, including resolution of benefits. Understand and apply Medicare Set Asides and allocations.
  • Negotiate settlement of claims within designated authority. May use structured settlement/annuity as appropriate for the jurisdiction.
  • In order to perform the essential functions of this job, acquisition and maintenance of Insurance License(s) may be required to comply with state and Travelers requirements. Generally, license(s) must be obtained within three months of starting the job and obtain ongoing continuing education credits as mandated.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 2 years Workers Compensation claim handling experience.
  • Analytical Thinking: Identifies current or future problems or opportunities; analyzes, synthesizes and compares information to understand issues; identifies cause/effect relationships; and explores alternative solutions that support sound decision-making.
  • Communication: Expresses, summarizes and records thoughts clearly and concisely orally and in writing by applying proper content, format, sentence structure, grammar, language and terminology.
  • Ability to effectively present file resolution to internal and/or external stakeholders.
  • Negotiation: Intermediate ability to understand alternatives, influence stakeholders and reach a fair agreement through discussion and compromise.
  • General Insurance Contract Knowledge: Interprets policies and contracts, applies loss facts to policy conditions, and determines whether or not a loss comes within the scope of the insurance contract.
  • Principles of Investigation: Intermediate investigative skills including the ability to take statements.
  • Follows a logical sequence of inquiry with a goal of arriving at an accurate reconstruction of events related to the loss.
  • Value Determination: Intermediate ability to determine liability and assigns a dollar value based on damages claimed and estimates, sets and readjusts reserves.
  • Settlement Techniques: Intermediate ability to assess how a claim will be settled, when and when not to make an offer, and what should be included in the settlement offer package.
  • Legal Knowledge: General knowledge, understanding and application of state, federal and regulatory laws and statutes, rules of evidence, chain of custody, trial preparation and discovery, court proceedings, and other rules and regulations applicable to the insurance industry.
  • Medical knowledge: Intermediate knowledge of the nature and extent of injuries, periods of disability, and treatment needed.
  • WC Technical:
  • Intermediate ability to demonstrate understanding of WC Products and ability to apply available resources and technology to resolve claims.
  • Demonstrate a clear understanding and ability to work within jurisdictional parameters within their assigned state.
  • Intermediate knowledge, understanding and application of state, federal and regulatory laws and statutes, rules of evidence, chain of custody, trial preparation and discovery, court proceedings, and other rules and regulations applicable to the insurance industry.
  • Customer Service:
  • Advanced ability to build and maintain productive relationships with our insureds and deliver results with optimal outcomes.
  • Teamwork:
  • Advanced ability to work together in situations when actions are interdependent and a team is mutually responsible to produce a result.
  • Planning & Organizing:
  • Advanced ability to establish a plan/course of action and contingencies for self or others to meet current or future goals.
  • Maintain Continuing Education requirements as required or as mandated by state regulations.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • 1 year Workers Compensation claim handling experience or successful completion of the WC trainee program.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join a cross-functional, product-centric team helping Bond & Specialty Insurance (BSI) evolve through AI-native development. This role is a builder and the owner of technical vision, shaping product vision together with the product owner and designer, and identifying where AI agents and tooling create the most leverage for the users their product serves.
The successful candidate brings demonstrated experience shipping production AI agents and LLM-powered systems, proficiency with modern agent frameworks and orchestration tooling, and a track record of defining technical direction within a workstream or product area. The individual will complete advanced software engineering tasks end-to-end, including designing, developing, testing, debugging, documenting, monitoring, and shipping production AI agents and supporting tooling. What Is the Opportunity?

This position performs a variety of complex paralegal duties and has a solid understanding of complex legal issues. Assists attorneys and others in legal case preparation and file management for moderate to complex matters which may include moderate to complex legal research, conducting investigations, drafting routine to complex documents and obtaining, reviewing, summarizing and analyzing all relevant documents, reports, records and other sources of information.

What Will You Do?

  • May conduct moderate to complex legal research and analyzes to prepare legal documents.
  • Assists with projects as requested.
  • Compiles and/or drafts routine to complex legal documents for review and use by attorneys such as motions for summary judgment, discovery responses, subpoenas and/or privilege logs.
  • May prepare and execute affidavits.
  • Summarizes deposition transcripts and/or assists attorneys in deposition preparation of witnesses up to and including trial preparation.

  • Assists attorney in every aspect of trial strategy and preparation and shares in the responsibility of trial results.
  • Categorizes and interprets data; reviews and analyzes reports, responses and records.
  • Conducts investigations including interviews as needed and directed.
  • Coordinates requests between multiple parties involved in litigation.
  • Uses resources to identify and select subject matter experts and provides instruction on areas to address.
  • Prepares and publishes legal holds.
  • Prepares case summaries and/or case analysis reports
  • Subpoenas records.
  • Coordinates with Document Management to obtain underwriting files and certified policies.
  • May provide testimony at depositions or trial, including as a corporate designee regarding company practices and procedures.
  • Locates archived materials in a variety of formats such as microfilm and microfiche. Works with Claim and Underwriting Units to locate archived manuals and guidelines for all legacy companies.
  • May review and process bills for payment.
  • Captures time and records billable time in accordance with policies and procedures.
  • Utilizes technology to respond efficiently to discovery requests.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

PURPOSE OF THE JOB


The purpose of the Senior Accountant is to create and analyze financial information to provide accurate and useful information to Management for review and decision making. This position performs and coordinates accounting duties within the Accounting department. This position exists to ensure accounting processes are completed thoroughly and accurately, while aligning with Company standards.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Accounting Operations and Reconciliations

  • Performs reconciliations monthly and resolves all reconciliation issues timely and independently.
  • Reviews and verifies the accuracy of journal entries and accounting classifications assigned to various records and makes corrections as needed to ensure provision accuracy.
  • Assembles, creates, and reconciles month-end accounting entries resolving discrepancies.
  • Prepares all account entries by compiling and analyzing account information.
  • Investigates and resolves moderately complex accounting discrepancies by evaluating root causes and recommending corrective actions.
  • Supports month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes and tax processes.

Process Improvement and Governance

  • Proven ability to influence and collaborate with stakeholders through the effective communication of accounting concepts, policies, and practices.
  • Supports internal and external audits as well as regulatory examinations by coordinating requests, preparing documentation, and responding to inquiries
  • Leads and implements process improvement initiatives related to financial reporting, analysis, system functionality, internal controls, and operational efficiency.
  • Upholds financial security by following internal controls.
  • Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to tax provisional inquiries by teammates.

Financial Reporting & Analysis

  • Prepares key components of income and balance sheet statements, consolidated statements, and various other accounting statements and reports.
  • Maintains, records, and reconciles all accounting information across source systems.
  • Coordinates special projects, ensures integrity of accounting information, and develops new or improved methods and procedures.
  • Independently analyzes complex financial transactions and accounting issues, identifies trends and risks, and provides recommendations to management.
  • Research and interpret accounting standards, policies, and procedures to ensure appropriate accounting treatment and effectively communicates any changes
  • Leads assigned accounting projects and process improvement initiatives within the department.
  • Coordinates and leads assigned accounting projects and department initiatives, ensuring timely completion of objectives and deliverables.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university required with a major or emphasis in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
  • Minimum 5-7 years of related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience required.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required. Certified Public Accountant (CPA) preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Intermediate knowledge of General Accounting, A/P, A/R and/or in an accountant role required.
  • Experience with automated accounting and financial management systems.
  • Solid knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing and interact effectively with management, employees, and auditors.
  • Ability to convey complex financial issues to non-financial users.
  • Ability to work independently and meet stringent deadlines; detail-oriented and highly organized. Ability to collect, analyze, and summarize data and to prepare clear and concise reports.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite applications.
  • Ability to support effective partnerships with key groups and individuals and have good consultation and change management skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate accounting issues, identify root causes, and recommend solutions.
  • Ability to interpret accounting policies, procedures, and regulations and apply professional judgment to complex situations.

Full job description

*****NO RECRUITERS PLEASE*****

Assistant Controller (CPA Required) | Hybrid

Experienced Senior Accountants and Accounting Managers with an active CPA license are encouraged to apply. We are seeking professionals with expertise in budget preparation, leadership of month-end close processes, team management, and driving process improvement initiatives.

POSITION SUMMARY

Windward Risk Managers is seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Assistant Controller (CPA Required) to support the Controller in leading the organization's accounting and financial reporting functions. This highly visible leadership role is responsible for overseeing month-end close. financial reporting, budgeting, cost allocation, financial analysis, and accounting operations while providing guidance and mentorship to the accounting team.

The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in financial reporting, budgeting, and process improvement, along with a proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Hybrid Schedule: This position offers a hybrid schedule of four days in the office and one day remote following the initial training period. During training (up to six months), the position is fully onsite five days per week.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

General Ledger and Financial Reporting

  • Lead month-end closing and preparation of monthly internal financial statements and reporting packages.
  • Review journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and reports.
  • Work closely with the Commissions team to develop, analyze, and reconcile reports and statements.
  • Support Accounts Payable and Claims Billing functions as needed.
  • Train and mentor junior staff.
  • Assist with annual audit preparations.
  • Assist with system reviews and process improvements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Budgeting & Financial Analysis

  • Lead the annual operating budget process in coordination with department heads.
  • Maintain department-level budgets and support models.
  • Prepare monthly budget-to-actual variance analyses.
  • Partner with department leaders to review variances and support corrective actions.
  • Ensure budgets align with organizational objectives and cost structures.

Cost Allocation & Expense Management

  • Develop, document, and maintain cost allocation methodologies across departments, entities, and cost centers.
  • Ensure cost allocations are applied consistently, accurately, and in accordance with internal policies.
  • Collaborate with Accounting to reconcile allocated costs to the general ledger and resolve discrepancies.
  • Assesses allocation methodologies periodically to ensure continued appropriateness and transparency.

The Role at a Glance

The Compliance Consultant is responsible for supporting Lincoln's Funds Management business team by implementing and maintaining complex compliance programs for Lincoln Variable Insurance Products Trust (LVIP), Lincoln Retail Private Market Funds (PM Funds), Lincoln Financial Investments Corporation (LFI), and Lincoln National Life's managed separate accounts. The Funds Management compliance team primarily oversees compliance with federal securities regulations relating to these companies/accounts and many supporting service providers including investment sub-advisors, principal underwriters, administrators, transfer agents, consultants, and others. Additionally, the Compliance Consultant is responsible for effective implementation of these compliance programs, with emphasis on policies and procedure testing and service provider oversight, while supporting all duties and responsibilities of Funds Management.

What you'll be doing

• Developing and performing compliance reviews and analyses to assess compliance with policies and procedures and regulatory requirements for LVIP, PM Funds, LFI and its sub-advisers.
• Supporting quarterly and annual testing of compliance policies and procedures to ensure effective implementation, documents results, and develops action plans for remediation of findings.
• Collaborating with appropriate stakeholders to ensure action plans capture and remediate the issues found during testing.
• Supporting periodic review of all compliance policies and procedures and related updates.
• Assisting the Enterprise Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Compliance team with the administration of LVIP's, PM Funds' and LFI's AML programs, including assistance with reviewing issues and alerts escalated by service providers.
• Supporting investment guideline and restriction monitoring through a post-trade surveillance system.
• Supporting LVIP's, PM Funds', and LFI's risk management programs by performing risk assessments, recommending risk scores, and maintaining risk inventories.
• Supporting the tracking of service providers' compliance policies and procedures, communicated through quarterly compliance questionaries or otherwise, and updating policies and procedures inventories in a timely manner.
• Coordinating the review of sub-advisers' control reports, summarizing findings, and maintaining a calendar to ensure timely receipt and review.
• Supporting the administration of LVIP's, PM Funds', and LFI ‘s Code of Ethics programs including analyses of securities transactions and maintenance of required statements for those individuals subject to the Code.
• Preparing monthly, quarterly, and annual compliance reports to business partners and LVIP/PM Funds/LFI Board of Trustees/Directors.
• Establishing and maintaining effective relationships with business partners and service providers.
• Collaborating with colleagues on compliance projects as assigned.
• Identifying and recommending process improvements that may reduce workloads or improve quality.
• Championing and enhancing organizational initiatives by positively influencing and supporting change management and/or departmental/enterprise initiatives.
• Serving as a resource and consulting with internal/external stakeholders on a broad variety of compliance matters/issues.
• Obtaining input from management as appropriate before making internal/external statements or providing information that could impact the corporation.
• Providing effective and open communication with internal/external stakeholders to ensure transparency and consistency of compliance actions.

• 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) (Minimum Required)
• 3 - 5+ Years experience in compliance that directly aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position (Required)

Senior Underwriter managing an Excess Casualty portfolio for Berkley Edge, a wholesale-only carrier focused on hard-to-place risks. Responsible for underwriting decisions, broker relationships, pricing strategies, and mentoring junior underwriters.

Full job description

Company Details

Berkley Edge offers solutions for hard-to-place and distressed risks for both professional and casualty lines of business. Edge will focus on small to mid-sized risks through a wholesale only distribution model.

Founded in 1967, W. R. Berkley Corporation has grown from a small investment management firm into one of the largest commercial lines property and casualty insurers in the United States. Along the way, we have been listed on the New York Stock Exchange, seen our revenue soar well past $10 billion, and become a well-respected Fortune 500 Company.

The Company is an equal employment opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

Senior Underwriter, Excess Casualty

The Senior Underwriter is responsible for managing and growing an Excess Casualty book of business, driving profitability, underwriting excellence, and broker relationships. This role evaluates new and renewal business, determines risk acceptability, develops pricing strategies, and provides technical underwriting expertise. The position serves as a key partner to brokers, supports business development initiatives, and helps resolve service and coverage issues.

Key Responsibilities

  • Underwrite and manage a profitable Excess Casualty portfolio.
  • Evaluate submissions, renewals, pricing, endorsements, restrictions, and cancellations.
  • Analyze risks, assess rate adequacy, and identify exposure trends.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with wholesale brokers and distribution partners.
  • Develop and implement underwriting strategies to achieve growth and profitability goals.
  • Provide technical guidance on coverage, pricing, regulatory matters, and emerging risks.
  • Collaborate with claims, underwriting, and other internal teams to improve portfolio performance.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert and referral resource for complex underwriting decisions.
  • Mentor and train less experienced underwriters.
  • Support product development and coverage enhancements to address market needs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience (Risk Management preferred).
  • Minimum 5 years of Excess Casualty underwriting experience.
  • Strong background in Excess & Surplus (E&S) Lines and Wholesale Brokerage distribution.
  • Professional designations such as CPCU, ASLI, or AU preferred.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Excellent analytical, negotiation, relationship-building, and communication skills.

• Base Salary Range: $90,000K-125,000K
• Eligible to participate in annual discretionary bonus
