About this job

Conduct actuarial studies for auto, property and commercial insurance lines under the guidance of experienced staff. Present findings and proposals to management while learning data science techniques, tools, and actuarial analyst functions.

Good fit if you have completed sophomore year in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics or related field with a 3.0 GPA minimum

Full job description

At Erie Insurance, we believe in professional and personal development. With our Future Focus Internship Program, both are provided in abundance. Not only do we offer the opportunity to gain professional experience in a challenging and competitive setting, but we welcome you as part of the ERIE family. We ensure that our interns receive the best internship experience possible, which includes multiple educational, developmental, professional, social and networking opportunities. The esteem ERIE holds in its Future Focus Internship Program is evident at every level of the organization, defined even further by multiple opportunities for socializing with high level leaders, up to and including our President and CEO. Are you ready for the internship experience of a lifetime? Look no further.

2027 Future Focus Internship Program Start Dates: Monday, May 17th or Monday, May 24th, 2027

2027 Future Focus Internship Program End Date: Friday, August 6th, 2027

Position Summary

Working with experienced departmental staff conducts actuarial studies for auto, property and commercial lines of business. Presents findings and proposals to management. Supports the work of actuarial analysts while learning the actuarial analyst job function.

As a Data Science intern, you will focus on the following duties and responsibilites:

  • Works with experienced departmental staff to learn data science techniques, data sources, tools, and business applications to conduct analysis.
  • Assists in conducting detailed analysis to identify insights and opportunities to improve business performance and decision-making.
  • Assists with researching emerging trends, tools, and techniques relevant to data science and the insurance industry.
  • Communicates findings and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Works with experienced departmental staff to learn actuarial techniques, data sources, and spreadsheets to conduct reviews of rating factors.
  • Assists in conducting detailed analysis of The ERIE's insurance programs, profitability, rating factors, reserve studies, dynamic financial analysis, and experience exhibits. Typical projects have included: deductible studies, trend and forecasts of average paid losses and frequencies, effect of large losses on rate indications, and competitive analysis.
  • Creates exhibits, reports, and charts for actuarial and reserve studies, state insurance department filings, and rate recommendations. Determines appropriate presentation format.
  • Develops a basic knowledge of ratemaking procedures used by The ERIE, competitors, and rate bureaus. Writes programs in SAS and Visual Basic to extract data to spreadsheet format. Reviews data for reasonableness and accuracy.
  • Gathers ERIE and Industry information in response to requests. Presents rate, reserve and other analysis to management and communicates analysis impacts to other departments as required.


The first three duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.

Regular and predictable attendance is an essential job function. For certain positions at ERIE, including leadership roles, regular and predictable onsite presence may also be an essential job function based on business and operational needs.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Capabilities

  • Nimble Learning
  • Self-Development
  • Collaborates
  • Information Management Skills
  • Customer Focus

  • Job-Specific Knowledge

  • Pursuit of bachelor's degree with completion of sophomore year majoring in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics or related field required.


Additional Experience

  • Minimum 3.0 GPA required.
  • Candidates in their final year of undergraduate study, or pursuing graduate studies are also eligible.

Job.JobDescription:
Who We Are

For over 70 years, Glatfelter Insurance Group has believed in doing the right thing for our clients, agents, communities and associates. This founding principle has enabled Glatfelter to grow from the kitchen-table, one-man-operation as it began, to one of the largest managing general agencies in the U.S. with nearly 500 associates across the country, a distribution network of over 4,500 independent brokers and more than 30,000 clients. It is what drives us to innovate—the desire to deliver the best for our clients. Founded as The Glatfelter Agency, which is still in operation, the program basis of Glatfelter Insurance Group, Volunteer Firemen's Insurance Services (VFIS), was founded in 1969. Throughout the years, Glatfelter has expanded to include specialized program business inclusive of public entities, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and religious organizations. Glatfelter provides their insureds with comprehensive insurance solutions including property, casualty, life insurance, and more. In 2018, Glatfelter joined American International Group (AIG) and is now part of the AIG family.

About the Position

The Glatfelter Agency (TGA), a division of Glatfelter Insurance Group, is seeking an experienced Commercial Lines Account Manager to join our growing team. This individual will be assigned a book of business to maintain and service.


This position is required to be onsite at our Leader Heights, York, PA office.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and service an existing book of business with professionalism.
  • Ability to convey complex insurance information in a clear and understandable manner.
  • Serve as primary point of contact for Commercial client inquiries and requests.
  • Collaborate with Account Executive, where appropriate, on account activity.
  • Coordinate renewal quotes with incumbent carrier and alternative carriers if marketing, reconciling quotes to requested specifications.
  • Utilize carrier websites to quote, rate, bind, and various other functions.
  • Compiling materials for client renewal presentations, including preparation of the agency proposal document.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation within agency management system (Epic).
  • Review all carrier issued documents for accuracy.
  • Issue Certificates of Insurance & Prepare Auto ID Cards.
  • Process mid-year client change requests.
  • Ensure compliance with company procedures and workflows.

What We're Looking For

  • College degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience sufficient to perform the essential duties of the job required.
  • Commercial Lines retail insurance agency experience required.
  • Licensed Pennsylvania Property/Casualty Agent.
  • Strong Microsoft Word Skills.
  • CISR Designation preferred.
  • Applied Epic experience preferred.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively both orally and in writing with internal and external customers including but not limited to underwriters, clients, marketing representative, and service team members.
  • Must be capable of working independently under team concept with general supervision.
  • Should possess the ability to plan & prioritize, be detail oriented and able to handle multiple tasks.
  • Must possess problem solving capabilities.
  • Must possess strong customer service skills.
  • Should have the ability to adapt to changing and improving technologies, and able to function within various on-line company rating sites.

Why Choose Glatfelter?

Glatfelter is honored to have been named a Best Place to Work in PA since 2005. We are proud to offer a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most - your health care, savings, financial protection and wellbeing. In addition to 17 paid holidays, (which includes a personal holiday and mental health and wellness day) we provide a variety of leaves for personal, health, family, and volunteer needs.

We believe in fostering our associates' development and offer a range of learning opportunities for associates to hone their professional skills to position themselves for the next steps of their careers. We have a tuition reimbursement program for eligible associates to enhance their education, skills, and knowledge in areas that relate to their current position or future positions to which they may transfer or progress.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Key Responsibilities

  • Upholding the highest standards of customer satisfaction and service to insureds, agents, regional directors, and other interested parties while fulfilling obligations to protect our insured's interests and the company's assets.

This includes verbal communications, written correspondence, internal reports, and issuance of formal denial, disclaimer, and reservation of rights letters.

  • Secondary school diploma or equivalent, college degree, and Associate in Claims designation preferred.
  • Three to six (3-6) years of experience in first-party property insurance claims or appropriate transferable experience in a related field required.

Technical Qualifications:

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Efficient time management skills.
  • Proficient knowledge of insurance policy forms, pertinent coverages, and claims handling processes and procedures.
  • Proficient understanding of technical subject matter appropriate to assigned specialty/line(s) of business.
  • Must be proficient with the use of computer applications (standard Microsoft products), keyboard/typing, and telecommunication tools and technology.
  • Quality focus and attention to detail.
  • Ability to perform calculations, prepare reports, and maintain files.
  • Effective interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team.

Upon employment the Associate is required to:

  • Develop a working knowledge and understanding of GCM processes and procedures as well as GIG culture, products, and services within an appropriate period of time.
  • Develop functional proficiency in the use of GIG/GCM computer systems and applications.
  • Complete required training as assigned to enhance knowledge, expand technical understanding, and develop skills.
  • Obtain required adjuster licenses within an aggressive timeframe and maintain licensure renewals by obtaining required continuing education credits.
  • Demonstrate ability to take ownership of assigned tasks and complete tasks timely/accurately.

Job.JobDescription:
The Administrative Assistant Supervisor provides high-level administrative support to site and senior leadership while overseeing day-to-day administrative operations. This role serves as a key business partner, ensuring seamless coordination of schedules, communications, reporting, office operations, and employee engagement activities. As the primary point of contact for administrative and office-related matters, this individual drives organization, efficiency, and professionalism across the site while supporting business priorities and fostering a positive workplace experience.

This is an onsite role in our Mt Juliet TN facility.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • Lead and oversee administrative support activities, including workload prioritization, task delegation, process coordination, and quality assurance
  • Manage complex calendars, meetings, and events for site and senior leadership, including scheduling, logistics, travel arrangements, visitor coordination, technology needs, and follow-up actions
  • Coordinate leadership meetings, employee events, recognition programs, volunteer activities, and other site initiatives
  • Prepare reports, presentations, dashboards, spreadsheets, meeting materials, and executive communications
  • Maintain accurate records, trackers, documentation, and administrative systems to support operational efficiency and compliance
  • Assist with purchase orders, invoice processing, expense reporting, budget tracking, and other administrative finance activities
  • Serve as the primary contact for office administration, facility support, visitor management, and workplace-related inquiries
  • Coordinate office supplies, workspace organization, and interactions with internal departments and external vendors
  • Support cross-functional communication and collaboration with employees, leadership, and business partners
  • Maintain confidentiality while managing sensitive information, special projects, and other administrative initiatives

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 3+ years of administrative support experience, preferably supporting senior leaders or executives
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Strong calendar management, meeting coordination, and organizational skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interact professionally across all levels of the organization
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience preparing reports, presentations, meeting materials, and executive support documentation
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with discretion

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree
  • Experience supporting senior leaders within a manufacturing or industrial environment
  • Experience coordinating executive travel, conferences, off-site meetings, and large-scale events
  • Advanced PowerPoint and Excel skills, including reporting, data tracking, and presentation development
  • Experience with expense management, purchasing, and enterprise scheduling systems

Pay Range

$43,600.00 - $71,800.00

Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to serve as a litigation representative to attend hearings, depositions, and resolve disputes as it applies to aspects of workers' compensation claims. This position exists to reduce allocated loss adjustment expenses and improve results by proactively analyzing and resolving workers' compensation claims.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages litigation and claim disputes as they apply to workers' compensation claims.

  • Attends claim hearings representing ICW Group.

  • Appears at WCAB lien conferences and trials; may need to appear at status, priority, and mandatory settlement conferences on occasion.

  • Schedules and attends settlement walk-through hearings with claimants and/or counsel.

  • Reduces loss adjustment expenses by quickly and effectively resolving disputed claims and litigation, including liens.

  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured.

Prepares documentation necessary for assigned cases.

  • Prepares court pleadings, reports, and settlement documents in accordance with statutory and case law as well as pertinent regulations.

  • Prepares for and attends depositions; maintains notes and correspondence.

  • Prepares and submits timely Hearing Reports to claims personnel and claims management.

  • Reviews and analyzes the billed invoices and liens and compares with professional bill review analysis.

Provides subject matter expertise in the litigation aspect of workers' compensation claims.

  • Applies appropriate legal defenses and negotiates resolution or set for trial.

  • Provides guidance and expertise to other department's operations, including Underwriting and Risk Management Services.

  • Partners with Claims Examiner to determine solutions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university in Business Administration, Management or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum 2-5 years of experience in workers' compensation required, with claims examiner experience preferred.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Working knowledge of claims and insurance industry preferred. Familiarity with and ability to effectively utilize the CA Labor Code, CA Code of Regulations, and CA Schedule for Rating Permanent Disabilities to rate disability impairment. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical journals, financial reports, and/or legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from counsel, claimants, customers, regulatory agencies, and/or members of the business community. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups, and/or boards of directors. Strong ability to negotiate to resolution various legal issues before the WCAB with opposing counsel, proper claimants, and co-defendants. Strong oral skills to articulate company's position in contested legal matters to opposing side, Information Officers, and WCAB judges.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This position requires some travel – up to 20 hours per week. Works with computers and computer screens for multiple hours per day; must be able to lift and carry 25-40 pounds. Position is sedentary approximately 80% of time. Must be able to drive and be comfortable working independently.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is a hybrid field/office position. Field environment includes appearing at various WCAB district offices, driving to and from appointments/appearances, meeting with attorneys/judges, and use of cell phone/email. Office environment includes use of a computer, telephone, copier and other standard office equipment.

Job.JobDescription:
Assurant is looking for Licensed Insurance sales agents to join our dynamic team. Come build a career with our team or grow your portfolio of work before you set out in new directions. We are a fast-paced, energetic environment where you drive the results while having the opportunity to connect remotely and enjoy competitive monthly bonuses and working from the comforts of home.

You will serve as the point of contact in fulfilling the insurance needs of our clients by assisting them with their sales process via inbound calls.

Work Schedule:

Our sales center is open from 8AM to 10PM ET on weekdays and 10AM to 5 PM ET on Saturdays. Individuals will have the ability to earn earlier shifts through our quarterly, performance-based shift bid process. Need flexibility to work any shift.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • 90% Handle inbound calls for multiple products with no prospecting or cold calling

  • 10% outbound calls to follow up on existing quotes

  • Establish a good liaison with our client's customers while selling Renters Insurance products.

  • Adopt and develop strategies while meeting departmental monthly sales goals

  • Track and monitor personal results to meet monthly sales and key performance goals

  • Follow underwriting requirements and corporate policies while negotiating sales

  • Navigate a computerized data entry system, internet, and/or other relevant applications for tracking, information gathering, troubleshooting and transaction processing

  • Complete mandatory licensure continuing education and other training sessions as appropriate

  • Remain positioned and well informed of changes implemented that affect your work

  • Our sales center is open from 8AM to 10PM ET on weekdays and 10AM to 5PM ET on Saturdays. Individuals will have the ability to earn earlier shifts through our quarterly, performance-based shift bid process.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • High school diploma or GED

  • One (1) plus year of sales related experience

  • One (1) plus years of call center and/or insurance experience

  • Solid computer, grammar, and multi-tasking skills

  • Must have a Property & Casualty or Personal Lines insurance license.

  • Ability to become appointed/licensed as a non-resident agent in all applicable states.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Strong analytical, listening, problem-solving, and negotiating skills

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment

  • Detail-oriented with a commitment to excellence

  • Ability to prioritize tasks with shifting deadlines and work on multiple projects simultaneously

About this job

Lincoln Financial Group is building an AI Native Intelligence platform that enables conversational queries over enterprise data. This role is a hands-on technical position designing and shipping Bedrock agents, retrieval pipelines, and natural-language-to-analytics capabilities that power the platform.

Good fit if you have 8+ years in data analytics, 2+ years building production LLM systems, and hands-on expertise with AWS Bedrock, Lambda, Step Functions, Athena, and prompt engineering

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Requisition #: 76794

The Role at a Glance

Lincoln Financial Group is building an AI Native Intelligence platform that turns enterprise data into a conversational, agentic layer the business can query directly — and that continuously finds patterns, trends, and anomalies in that data on its own. The platform's architecture spans an AWS-native ingestion and extraction pipeline, a governed semantic layer and business knowledge graph, and an intelligence layer that answers questions in plain language and surfaces what's changing, instead of relying on static reports someone has to remember to check.

We're looking for a Lead, AI Native Analytics to be the hands-on builder of that conversational and analytical experience: the person who actually designs and ships the Bedrock agents, retrieval pipelines, pattern-detection logic, and natural-language-to-analytics capabilities that make the platform usable. This is an individual-contributor-heavy, deeply technical role — you'll spend most of your time in the architecture, the prompts, and the code, while partnering closely with the Senior Director on direction and with business stakeholders on what “useful” actually looks like.

What you'll be doing

  • Design and build the conversational AI experience end to end: Bedrock Agents (via AgentCore or MCP/API), retrieval-augmented generation over Bedrock Knowledge Bases / OpenSearch Serverless, natural-language-to-SQL over Athena, and relationship queries over a knowledge graph (Amazon Neptune / GraphRAG).
  • Build capabilities that continuously detect patterns, trends, and anomalies across enterprise data — surfacing what's notable proactively, rather than waiting for someone to know what question to ask.
  • Build and tune the AI extraction pipeline that turns raw unstructured data (documents, logs, notes, communications) into structured, query-ready facts — using Amazon Comprehend and/or LLM-based extraction via the Bedrock Converse API (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB for state).
  • Own prompt engineering and agent tool design: system instructions, tool/action-group definitions, structured-output schemas, and model selection/tiering to balance accuracy, latency, and cost.
  • Integrate the conversational layer with the platform's semantic layer and business ontology (KPI and metrics definitions, business rules glossary) so agent answers stay consistent with how the business already measures itself — never computing an ad hoc number that disagrees with a dashboard.
  • Build evaluation and quality processes for LLM-based systems: golden question sets, retrieval/accuracy scoring, hallucination and abstention testing, and regression checks before any change ships to users.
  • Implement guardrails in partnership with security/compliance: PII detection and redaction, Bedrock Guardrails configuration, access-controlled data zones, and audit logging for every AI-generated answer.
  • Partner directly with business stakeholders across the enterprise to translate real questions into working conversational and pattern-detection features, and iterate quickly based on usage and accuracy feedback.
  • Mentor and provide technical direction to engineers contributing to the conversational AI workstream, and represent this workstream in architecture reviews led by the Senior Director.
  • Stay current with the fast-moving AWS AI landscape — Bedrock model and AgentCore updates, new retrieval and evaluation tooling — and bring concrete recommendations back to the team.

What we're looking for

Must Haves:

  • 8+ years of experience in Data Analytics / Business Intelligence with at least 2+ years building production LLM-based Analytics systems (not just prototypes or proofs of concept).
  • Hands-on, production-level expertise with the AWS AI/data stack: Amazon Bedrock (Knowledge Bases, Agents/AgentCore), AWS Lambda, Step Functions, Amazon S3, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena; working experience with a vector store (OpenSearch Serverless or similar).
  • Strong, practical prompt-engineering and LLM application development skills: structured extraction, tool-calling/agentic patterns, retrieval design, and iterative evaluation against real questions.
  • Solid understanding of semantic layers, business ontologies, or metrics layers, and how to ground LLM outputs in governed, consistent business definitions rather than ad hoc computation.
  • Experience building or applying pattern-, trend-, or anomaly-detection techniques over enterprise data (statistical, ML-based, or LLM-assisted), and turning what's found into something a business user can act on.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript/Node.js for building extraction pipelines, agent tools, and integration code.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and cloud analytics engines (Athena, Redshift, or similar), sufficient to design and validate natural-language-to-SQL experiences.
  • Clear communicator who can demo a working system to engineers and explain its behavior and limitations to non-technical business stakeholders with equal clarity.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience with GraphRAG or other knowledge-graph-grounded retrieval patterns, and with a graph database such as Amazon Neptune.
  • Experience with a semantic-layer/metrics-layer tool (e.g., Cube.dev) used to serve consistent metrics to both BI and AI consumers.
  • Experience with NLP/document-processing pipelines (e.g., Amazon Comprehend) for extracting structure from varied unstructured enterprise data.
  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry, with a working understanding of PII handling and data privacy/compliance considerations.
  • Experience configuring LLM safety/evaluation tooling such as Bedrock Guardrails, or building your own evaluation harness for generative AI systems.
  • Familiarity with a range of enterprise data domains (financial, operational, customer, or workforce data) within a large organization.

The Role at a Glance

Lincoln Financial Group is seeking a detail-oriented and delivery-focused Product Owner to join our AI Product & Delivery organization. In this role, leading innovation squads, you will own the day-to-day execution of AI product features and capabilities within an assigned product domain, working hands-on with data science, engineering, and business domain teams to bring AI solutions from backlog to production. Reporting to the VP/AVP of AI Products, you will serve as the connective tissue between business process reimagination and technical delivery — writing clear user stories, managing sprint-level priorities, supporting model evaluations, and ensuring AI features meet quality, compliance, and user experience standards. This role is ideal for a practitioner who thrives in the details and is eager to grow their AI product career in a regulated financial services environment.

What you'll be doing

AI Feature Ownership & Delivery

  • Own and maintain the product backlog for assigned AI features or squads, ensuring stories are well-defined, prioritized, and ready for sprint execution.
  • Write detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and feature specifications for AI-driven capabilities in collaboration with engineering and data science teams.
  • Lead actively in agile ceremonies — sprint planning, standups, reviews, and retrospectives — keeping delivery on track and surfacing blockers early.
  • Coordinate UAT, QA, and launch readiness activities for AI feature releases, ensuring quality and compliance standards are met before go-live.
  • Support the AVP in managing timelines, dependencies, and risks across feature workstreams.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serve as the day-to-day product contact for business SMEs, engineering squads, and UX designers within assigned AI feature areas.
  • Communicate feature status, trade-offs, and delivery risks clearly to the AVP and relevant business partners.
  • Facilitate working sessions and backlog refinement meetings to drive team alignment and shared understanding of requirements.
  • Support change management by helping business partners understand, test, and adopt new AI-driven capabilities.

Responsible AI & Compliance

  • Apply responsible AI principles — fairness, transparency, explainability, and privacy — in the definition and acceptance of AI features.
  • Escalate potential compliance, bias, or safety concerns identified during model evaluation or feature review to the AVP and relevant risk partners.
  • Ensure AI feature documentation, testing evidence, and release artifacts meet Lincoln's internal governance and audit standards.
  • Collaborate with Trust & Safety, Legal, and Compliance teams as needed to support feature-level risk reviews.

Performance & Insights

  • Define and track feature-level success metrics including adoption, task completion, model accuracy, and user satisfaction.
  • Analyze usage data, model performance logs, and user feedback to identify improvement opportunities and inform backlog prioritization.
  • Contribute to sprint-level reporting and help maintain product dashboards that surface key delivery and quality metrics.
  • Share learnings from evals, user testing, and post-launch monitoring with the broader AI Product & Delivery team.

Data Science & Model Evaluation Support

  • Partner with data scientists and ML engineers to understand model capabilities, limitations, and evaluation results for assigned AI features.
  • Assist in designing and executing evaluations (evals) for LLM-powered features — assessing output quality, accuracy, relevance, and safety against defined benchmarks.
  • Review and annotate model outputs as part of human-in-the-loop feedback processes, identifying failure modes, edge cases, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support the creation of eval datasets, test case libraries, and regression frameworks to enable consistent model performance tracking.
  • Assist in prompt testing and iteration — running structured experiments to understand how prompt changes affect model behavior and output quality.
  • Help monitor model performance post-launch and flag regressions or unexpected behavior to the data science team.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:

  • 3–10 years of experience in product management, product ownership, or a closely related role.
  • Hands-on experience working on AI, ML, or data-driven products — including direct collaboration with data science or engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with LLM concepts such as prompt engineering, model evaluation, and output quality assessment.
  • Experience with agile methodologies and backlog management tools (e.g., Jira, Linear, Productboard).
  • Strong written communication skills — able to write clear, unambiguous user stories, PRDs, and feature specifications.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Business, or a related field.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Hands-on experience with LLM APIs or enterprise AI platforms (e.g., Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic Claude, Google Vertex AI).
  • Exposure to ML evaluation frameworks, annotation workflows, or AI observability tools (e.g., LangSmith, Weights & Biases).
  • Familiarity with responsible AI practices including bias detection, fairness evaluation, and model explainability.
  • Domain experience in life insurance, annuities, retirement planning, or employee benefits.
  • Product or AI-related certifications (Pragmatic, AIPMM, data science, or ML-related).

Lead actuary for Executive Benefits pricing, including COLI/BOLI and PPLI products. Responsibilities include pricing analysis, modeling, assumption setting, regulatory compliance, and presenting findings to stakeholders across business units.

Good fit if you have 6+ years of actuarial experience and familiarity with MG-ALFA modeling and product illustration software.

The Role at a Glance

The primary purpose of this role is pricing support for Lincoln's Executive Benefits (EB) products, including COLI/BOLI and PPLI. You will contribute to the design, modeling, assumption setting, analysis, and state filing/regulatory compliance for new products, as well as regular rate-setting (crediting rates) and profitability analysis for existing, inforce products. You will have the opportunity to present your work to various stakeholders, including product management, pricing review, risk management, and senior leadership. You will work on products developed in partnership with the EB distribution team and will work across business units and functions, including finance and enterprise risk management.

What you'll be doing

Pricing Analysis

  • Perform pricing analysis for new/redesigned Executive Benefits contracts and rider benefits, including COLI/BOLI and PPLI products.
  • Determine appropriate assumptions and how to model new product features.
  • Develop pricing strategies and provide consultation/clarification on actuarial models and risk issues.
  • Collaborate with the product development and distribution teams on product design to meet or exceed profitability and sales objectives.
  • Direct, develop, and/or run complex pricing models and analysis using MG-ALFA and product illustration software (Andesa) for EB contracts and rider benefits.
  • Present results of analysis to team members, key business partners, and management.

Risk Analysis

  • Analyze risk management strategies, and various reserve and capital requirements.
  • Evaluate the impact of potential product design changes on the reserve and/or capital requirement, profitability, and tail risks.

Actuarial/ Technical Support

  • Maintain existing actuarial pricing models and tools, and proactively identify and implement improvements. Develop tools and support product/relationship managers according to business needs.
  • Provide actuarial support for state filing, tax qualification, and regulatory compliance for EB products.

Pricing Documentation

  • Prepare reports and presentations summarizing pricing analysis and results, including crediting rates, and documentation of assumptions and methodology.

Special Projects

  • Participate in ad hoc projects related to product development, implementation, inforce management, and corporate risk management initiatives.

What we're looking for

  • 6+ years of experience in Actuarial positions
  • Preferred to have FSA credential
  • MG-ALFA modeling experience preferred; experience with product illustration software (e.g., Andesa) a plus
  • Strong technical skills
  • Comfort working with and communicating across various teams and levels of seniority
  • Capability to be productive in a dynamic environment with changing priorities and responsibilities

The Role at a Glance

An exciting opportunity to take a lead role on the RPS Pricing and Risk team responsible for product strategy, pricing, and actuarial risk management. You will serve as the lead analyst on strategic projects that support the business — building the analysis, developing the recommendation, and helping senior decision makers land on a path forward. You will also deliver the key reporting that informs how leadership manages product, pricing, and risk governance, including support for our stable value rate setting process. This position is built for someone who can work independently, communicate credibly with senior leaders, and turn complex analysis into recommendations that move the business forward.

What you'll be doing

  • Supporting strategic projects: Leading assigned workstreams on strategic initiatives from direction through implementation — developing the approach, managing timelines, coordinating with cross-functional partners, and carrying the work through to a recommendation with limited day-to-day oversight

  • Analyzing: Evaluating market dynamics, competitive positioning, profitability, and risk exposures to deliver actionable recommendations grounded in data
  • Reporting and rate setting support: Delivering monthly and quarterly reporting on product performance, pricing, and risk governance, including key metrics for RPS management and corporate stakeholders; supporting the stable value rate setting process in partnership with Product, Investments, and Finance; ensuring strong controls and minimizing operational risk
  • Innovating and automating: Identifying and implementing process improvements, automation, and enhanced data visualization that raise quality and efficiency across the team

What we're looking for

  • Executive presence — the ability to communicate clearly and credibly with senior leaders and influence outcomes through well-supported recommendations
  • Strong technical skills and understanding of actuarial, mathematical, and financial concepts
  • Proficiency in advanced Excel and at least one programming or analytics tool (e.g., VBA, Python, SQL, Dataiku, Power BI)
  • Demonstrated critical thinking and the ability to analyze data, identify trends, and draw valid conclusions
  • 4 Year/Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (e.g., actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, finance, economics, data science, computer science, or engineering)

About this job

Litigation Claims Adjuster for a Northeast property and casualty insurer, managing complex auto and liability claims including New York Labor Law and construction defect cases. Hybrid role in Bedford, New Hampshire requiring two office days weekly, with interaction across internal teams, policyholders, attorneys and service providers.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of commercial claims experience and strong negotiation and communication skills

Full job description

Description

Litigation Claims Adjuster

Hybrid Work Schedule

Bedford, New Hampshire

Merchants Insurance Group is a leading Property and Casualty Insurer in the Northeast and is looking for a Litigation Claims Adjuster to join our growing Claims Legal Team in our Bedford, New Hampshire office.

The Litigation Claims Adjuster will become part of a dedicated team focusing on auto and general liability claims, which includes New York Labor Law, construction defect, premises and/or third-party property damage claims. This position interacts extensively with internal colleagues as well as policyholders, agents, attorneys and a multitude of claim-related service providers.

Merchants Insurance Group is rated A- (Excellent) with a stable outlook by A.M. Best and is consistently recognized as a top employer and high-performing organization. Recent honors include:

  • Best Places to Work in Western New York (Buffalo Business First, 2023–2026)
  • Fast Track Company (2019–2025) and Top Private Company (2019–2025)
  • Ward's 50® top-performing property-casualty insurer (2021–2024)
  • Ivans Spark Award for Innovation (2024–2025)
  • Named to Newsweek and Statista's America's Most Reliable Companies list (2025), ranked among the top 300 of 1,500 B2B organizations evaluated

We offer a hybrid work schedule, requiring two full days per week in the office, with flexibility to work remotely or in office the remaining days. This model supports collaboration while providing flexibility and work-life balance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Cultivating relationships with claims and other internal staff, policyholders, attorneys, agents and a variety of service providers and experts all while working towards achieving the most optimal outcomes for Merchants and our policyholders.
  • Providing a high level of customer service while managing a portfolio of complex and high exposure litigated claims involving complex liability and damage issues.
  • Evaluating coverage by interpreting/applying policy language to claim facts and preparing appropriate and timely coverage position letters.
  • Conducting and directing timely and quality claim investigation, evaluation and equitable settlement of all assigned claims.
  • Ensuring timely and accurate reserves consistent with established reserving philosophy and practices.
  • Negotiating fair and equitable settlements directly with attorneys.
  • Identifying risk transfer opportunities through trade contracts and/or applicable law.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Qualified candidates will have a 4-year degree or equivalent work-related experience.
  • 5 plus years' experience handling commercial lines claims. Experience with New York Labor Law, construction defect and/or third-party property damage claims is a plus.
  • Candidates with JD and insurance defense experience looking for a new career path are encouraged to apply.
  • Ability to oversee and manage defense counsel, select and retain appropriate experts and develop appropriate resolution strategies.
  • Professional designations or working towards industry specific designations are a plus.
  • Exceptional organization, negotiation, verbal and written communication skills are required.

Merchants Insurance Group is a leading Property and Casualty Insurer in the Northeast and is looking for a Litigation Claims Adjuster to join our growing Claims Legal Team in our Melville, New York office.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Commercial Lines Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Underwriter
Job.JobDescription:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers' Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver's license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers' Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

The position may include other duties as assigned.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Quality Engineer II is an established, technical professional who serves as the Quality Engineering lead for their assigned delivery team. This role takes complete ownership of the test strategy, planning, and quality outcomes for the team, ensuring that quality is engineered into every stage of the software delivery lifecycle. Working independently with limited supervision, the QE II drives shift-left practices within the team, builds and maintains automated test solutions, and sets quality objectives that directly impact department results. The role requires practical depth in test engineering, the ability to solve difficult and moderately complex problems by drawing from prior experience, and the capacity to coordinate quality activities, delegate tasks, and coach junior team members.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the complete test strategy and test planning for the assigned Projects – defining scope, approach, risk assessment, entry/exit criteria, and test coverage targets for each release and sprint.

  • Act as the QE lead within the team and drive quality discussions during grooming, sprint planning, and design reviews; set quality objectives; and ensure the team delivers against them.

  • Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for functional, regression, integration, API, and exploratory testing.

  • Build, maintain, and extend automated test suites using frameworks such as Playwright for UI, Postman/Newman for API, following clean code practice.

  • Execute API-level testing including payload validation, error handling, and contract verification for in-house and third-party service integrations.

  • Contribute automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), supporting continuous testing across regression, smoke, and feature validation stages.

  • Validate data integrity across integrated systems including ETL pipelines, data transformations, and end-to-end data reconciliation.

  • Identify, record, and thoroughly document defects; perform root cause analysis by reviewing logs, stack traces, and database states to diagnose systemic issues.

  • Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.

  • Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.

  • Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.

  • Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.

  • Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.

  • Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.

  • Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.

  • Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.

  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.

  • Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.

  • Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.

  • Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.

  • Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.

  • Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.

  • Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).

  • Awareness of AI-assisted testing tools and willingness to adopt AI workflows for test generation and defect analysis.

  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum practices, shift-left testing, and the software development lifecycle.

  • Ability to work independently on moderately complex assignments with limited supervision; strong problem-solving skills drawing from prior experience and analysis.

  • Good communication skills; able to influence within the team and communicate with contacts within and occasionally outside the department.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate quality tasks, delegate work, and review the output of junior team members.

  • Preferred skills include strong Insurance domain background, specifically in Claims Management and/or Insurance Billing business workflows.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

About this job

Sales Development Manager supporting agencies in Broward and Miami-Dade Counties. Responsible for regional sales growth through agent contact, consultative selling, and tracking metrics including quotes, applications, profitability, and retention.

Good fit if you have 3+ years sales experience, a bachelor's degree, and reside in Broward or Miami-Dade County.

Full job description

This role supports Broward and Miami-Dade Counties. Candidates residing in Broward or Miami-Dade County are strongly preferred.

Position Summary:

The Sales Development Manager (SDM) will be responsible for continual contact with agencies in their region to provide assistance to the agents with the goal of superior customer service and increased sales.

Essential Functions:

The SDMs measure of success is broken into key annual objectives with specific metrics agreed upon with the Director of Sales:

  • Production
    • The SDM will be measure against metrics areas of Quotes, Applications, Profitability and Retention
  • Sales Card
    • This will measure the number of agents with the defined bands at the beginning and the end of the calendar year. The goal for the SDM is to move a % of agents into a higher premium ban while maintaining agents with existing premium.
  • Sales Call Quality
    • Works with team to implement a consultative selling approach in which we obtain an in-depth understanding of how our agents do business and what needs are important to them.
  • Functional and Administrative
    • Collecting Agency Profile Information goal is to have all profile fields completed for 90% of our full appointed agents
    • Contact Management implement and track the number of face-to-face visits and phone contact with agencies. All contact information to be entered in Sugar database
    • Competitive Intelligence Surface and comment any changes taken place in the marketplace by our competitors. Document information on weekly report that is submitted to Director
    • Weekly Reporting Update and document a weekly activity report that will be discussed on weekly departmental conference call
    • Territory reviews periodically meet with senior management to review regional goals per agent; strategies for contact management and competitive intelligence
    • Utilizing ISA

Why Windward Risk Managers:

  • Windward Risk Managers is proud to be recognized on Fortune's Best Medium Workplaces list, ranking #28 among the Top 100 companies
  • 100% employer paid health insurance for employees
  • Up to 6% 401(k) match with immediate vesting

  • Collaborative and growth focused culture

  • 3+ years sales experience
  • Excellent verbal and written communication and analytical skills necessary
  • Able to handle multiple tasks with varying deadlines

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1-3 years experience in P&C sales, preferably in Florida

Company Details

Carolina Casualty is a member company of W. R. Berkley Corporation, an insurance holding company that is among the largest commercial lines insurance writers in the United States. We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto markets including trucking, public transportation and others.

Join Carolina Casualty, where innovation meets purpose.

Carolina Casualty is a proud member of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the largest commercial lines insurers in the country. What sets us apart is not just our size, but how we work and who we are.

We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo, and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto market, including trucking and public transportation industries that keep America moving. Our team tackles real, complex challenges for the people and businesses that make that possible every day.

At CCIC, we live by three simple truths:

Always do right. Integrity is not just a slogan. It guides every decision we make.

Everything counts; everyone matters. Every role, every voice, and every contribution help shape who we are as an organization.

Embrace innovation and act responsibly. We are willing to challenge the status quo while remaining thoughtful and committed to our people, customers, and partners.

If you are looking for a place where your work makes an impact, your ideas are valued, and doing the right thing is expected, we would love to meet you.

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

The Product Compliance Analyst is a key role to ensure our policy forms are accurate, in compliance, producing effectively and supporting our company's goal to offer a competitive coverage product. The Product Analyst works closely with Actuarial, Underwriting, Marketing, and Claims to develop forms, product manuals, product comparisons and product communications.

Key Functions/Duties of Position: Describe the overall job responsibilities (including any decision-making authority) for this position.

· The Product Compliance Analyst is responsible to create and enhance the company's product including, but not limited to, forms, manuals, member policy package, implementation of forms, etc., to ensure competitiveness in the marketplace.

· The Product Compliance Analyst will draft and prepare filings and responses to negotiate approval for form and rule filings with the Department of Insurance (DOI) and Office of Insurance Regulation (OIR) through to completion.

· They will perform competitive research of primary competitors for opportunities for improvement.

· The Product Compliance Analyst interprets insurance forms, statutes, rules, regulations, develops conclusions, and makes recommendations.

· They perform analysis of existing forms and manuals on a regularly schedule basis for effectiveness.

· Research and analyze external information sources to provide updated, accurate competitive analysis including rates, guidelines, and forms coverage information.

· Compile, analyze and report on product market trends to assist in determining product strategy.

· They perform User Acceptance Testing for accuracy of enhancements and modifications of forms installations, identify, document and report discrepancies found.

· The Product Compliance Analyst works independently and manages projects and assignments and prioritizes workload to ensure deadlines are met.

· They perform all responsibilities using established department processes, quality control procedures and checklists.

· The Product Compliance Analyst effectively manages medium-large projects simultaneously to completion, while meeting deadlines.

· They perform program audits as needed and required.

· Other duties as assigned.

· This position is in office Monday-Thursday with Friday an optional work from home day.

Qualifications

Education Requirement

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Insurance Designations preferred

Qualifications: Include necessary skills/experience and core competencies required

  • 4+ years of experience working in the Property Casualty or Commercial Lines
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience in interpreting insurance forms, statutes, rules, regulations and performing analysis, developing conclusions, and recommendations.
  • Strong organizational, time management, attention to detail and analytical skills are essential.
  • Ability to organize and prioritize workload.
  • Ability to communicate effectively.
  • Self-motivated and results oriented.
  • Preferred knowledge in ISO rates/rules/forms.
  • Preferred experience in preparing and managing rate/rule form filings and implementation.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $93,408 to $133,440 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Jersey City, NJ
  • Experience: 8 to 10 years
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

About this job

Supervise environmental and professional liability claims at WR Berkley, overseeing investigation, evaluation, and negotiation of pollution and professional claims. Lead a team, provide technical guidance, analyze claims data for trends, and serve as subject matter expert for the specialty area.

Good fit if you have 8-10 years in environmental and professional liability claims plus 5 years management or team lead experience in insurance.

Full job description

Company Details

W. R. Berkley Corporation, founded in 1967, is one of the nation's premier commercial lines property casualty insurance providers. Founded in 2004, Berkley Environmental has underwriting and account executive units in seven regions. Berkley Environmental offers an array of coverages for virtually all classes traditionally known to have environmental liability exposures on both an admitted and non-admitted basis. We provide a comprehensive portfolio of commercial property casualty insurance, automobile liability and workers' compensation, along with claim services, providing expertise to meet the unique business needs of our customers.

Responsibilities

Provide the leadership to deliver superior results and develop strategies focused on attaining a "World Class" distinction in Environmental and Professional Liability Claims.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee and assist in your team's strategies to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and (if necessary) proceed to trial on pollution/professional claims.
  • Provide technical guidance, assistance and training as needed for claims staff and other departments.
  • Present high-level cases to upper management and other stakeholders in a committee review collaborative type environment.
  • Work with Corporate claims in reporting matters that have potential impact on other Operating Units within the W.R. Berkley Enterprise.
  • Analyze the incident data of claims to determine the root causes and trends.
  • Hold bi-monthly meetings with Pollution/Professional senior underwriters and product line managers to discuss recent loss developments.
  • Serve as a Claim Ambassador on account renewals and new business by supporting our Customer Service Director.
  • Work in concert with the Legal Service Coordinator by assisting in having our internal bill review process work seamlessly without interruption to claim examiners and their functions.
  • Respond to coverage inquiries from brokers and insureds in succinct communicative methods.
  • Assist examiners in recognizing potential subrogation opportunities that we handle in-house in the General Liability and Pollution/Professional disciplines.
  • Assist our Claim Operations Leader with the functioning of a Claims department (SOX controls, licensing requirements, etc.).
  • Provide weekly and monthly claims reports.
  • Assist underwriting in the drafting of non-admitted coverage forms and endorsements.
  • Coordinate with the Finance Department on claims associated costs.
  • Continuously exhibit and uphold Core Values of Integrity, Accountability, Communication and Teamwork, Innovation and Customer Service
  • Maintain a high level of communication with leadership.
  • Work within authority limits on assignments that reflect a high degree of technical complexity and coordination.
  • Will be recognized as the company consultant within specialty area.
  • Handle special projects related to specialty area as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Minimum 5 years management/team lead experience in the Insurance Industry.
  • Minimum 8-10 years insurance experience in Environmental and Professional Liability claims.
  • Demonstrates solid ability in presenting training programs.
  • Evidence of self-motivation and require minimal management direction.
  • Ability to establish, develop and maintain professional relationships with accounts and prospects.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Possesses analytical and creative problem-solving skills.

Kansas City, KS ~ Caledonia, MI ~ Oklahoma City, OK ~ Phoenix, AZ ~ St. Louis, MO

  • Department Hours of Operation: 7:00 am - 7:00 pm, Monday - Friday. You are expected to work 40 hours/week with flexibility, subject to business needs, geographic location, and Farmers Timekeeping Policy.

Compensation: The starting wage for this position is $26.01 per hour, plus you will be eligible for an annual bonus. Pay is dependent upon the candidate's geographic location and relevant claims experience.

    • Compensation will be evaluated based on related experience.
    • Candidates with Claims Auto Handling or related industry experience are highly encouraged to apply.

Job Summary

Utilizes working knowledge and skills developed through formal training to investigate, confirm coverage, determine liability, establish damages, and negotiate settlements of auto claims, which includes single and multi-vehicle losses with basic coverage and moderate complexity of liability.

Day in the Life of an Auto Claim Handler:

  • Utilizes a broad understanding of claims adjusting to apply skills and knowledge to investigate and determine liability for claims with basic coverage issues and moderate to complex liability issues. Performs in-depth investigation and analysis on losses such as multi-vehicle losses with comparative negligence. Completes investigation by securing recorded statements of the drivers, police reports vehicle photos and estimates, and scene investigations.
  • Makes same-day contact with customers. Explains the claims process to all customers. Explains all applicable coverage benefits to the policyholder. Confirms facts of loss. Determines vehicle location and if drivable. Offers vehicle repair and rental service options to customers. Coordinates auto physical damage estimate through the proper internal method of inspection and arranges for the release of vehicles that are accruing storage fees.
  • Proactively investigates and determines coverage for Auto policy claims with coverage issues requiring in-depth investigation including but not limited to if the policy is out of force for the date of loss, unlisted or permissive drivers, excluded drivers, vehicles not on the policy, rideshare involvement, material misrepresentation issues, and new business investigations.
  • Maintains ownership of the claim and completes work with a limited degree of supervision. Serves as the primary point of contact through resolution of all exposures. Communicates and collaborates with other claim specialists to facilitate claim resolution for customers. Provides verbal and written communication to customers to explain coverage issues and decisions.
  • Communicates policy risk issues to Underwriting to facilitate their evaluation of the policy risk and exposure. Escalates complex coverage issues to supervisor.
  • Demonstrates proficient knowledge and application of venue laws for all states handled in the Region. Analyzes duties owed and breached by all potentially responsible parties and determines liability percentage for each party. Escalates claims with exposures exceeding financial authority to supervisor. Communicates liability decisions to customers, claimants, claim specialists, and Underwriting. Recognizes subrogation potential and makes referrals to the Subrogation department when appropriate.
  • With limited supervision and support, investigates and recognizes all potential claim exposures. Recognizes and escalates non-auto property damage exposures and resolves auto physical damage claims proactively and accurately. Secures estimate of damages timely through appropriate repair channels. Writes, reviews, and adjusts auto physical damage estimates for repairable vehicles with minor to moderate damages. Issues and authorizes claim payments to customers and repair facilities and explains repair process and estimate to customers.
  • Manages rental claims through communication with customers, repair facilities, rental vendors, and claim specialists. Proactively manages and mitigates storage costs. Coordinates and collaborates with auto physical damage and total loss specialists to facilitate claim resolution for customers.
  • Maintains active diary and resolution plan on open files. Handles and documents files in compliance with regulatory requirements. Responsible for ensuring professional correspondence is sent to customers including claim status updates. Completes work with a limited degree of supervision. May act as an informal resource for colleagues with less experience.

Education Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
    • Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • An active All Lines Adjuster license is required, or the ability to obtain licensure.
    • If not currently licensed, obtaining and passing the All Lines Adjuster licensing requirements during training is a condition of employment.

  • Demonstrated customer service skills.
  • Effective conflict management skills. Identifies key issues and patterns from partial/conflicting data.
  • Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Strong written communication skills with the ability to convey critical decisions and information through written letters.
  • Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision-making skills.

  • Possesses flexibility to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment; uses discretion to modify work practices and processes to achieve results or improve efficiency.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills. Takes a broad perspective on problems and spots new, less obvious solutions.
  • Performs work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Possesses strong technical aptitude; Proficient in Microsoft Office products. Adaptable and flexible to new technology.

Physical Environment & Actions

  • Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping.

  • Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (e.g. others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction.
  • Visually verifies and reads information.
  • Visually locates material, resources and other objects.
  • Ability to continuously operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.
