Full job description


Description

Join a Growing Team and Tackle Some of the Industry's Most Complex Environmental Claims

Liberty Mutual is expanding our Environmental Claims team and seeking an experienced Environmental Claims Professional to manage high-exposure environmental, pollution, toxic tort, and mass litigation claims within our Commercial Specialty Lines portfolio! This is an excellent opportunity for a seasoned claims professional who thrives in complex coverage and liability analysis, enjoys collaborating with legal and industry experts, and is looking to make a meaningful impact at a Fortune 100 carrier known for its financial strength, innovation, and commitment to customer advocacy. In this role of Senior Technical Claims Specialist, you will exercise significant judgment and ownership throughout the entire claim lifecycle, from coverage analysis and investigation through litigation management, negotiation, and resolution. You'll partner closely with policyholders, brokers, reinsurers, underwriting, and defense counsel while helping shape outcomes on some of our most challenging and technically sophisticated claims.

Why this role

Youll own complex environmental casualty claims from first notice through resolution, with real authority to decide coverage, set reserves, negotiate, and settle. This is not a hand-off role. Youll make the calls, direct the strategy, and be recognized internally as a subject matter expert on pollution and specialty coverage issues.

What youll do

  • Own the claim end to end. Determine coverage, investigate, assess liability, set and adjust reserves, evaluate exposure, negotiate settlements, and authorize payment. Youll also have the authority to deny claims when the facts and policy language support it.
  • Drive litigation strategy. Review pleadings, claim files, and investigation materials, then set the plan to resolve each suit, including coverage positions, amounts owed, discovery plans, and negotiation approach.
  • Build the right team for each matter. Based on the allegations, assemble the working group of Home Office Legal, defense counsel, and Home Office Claims, and bring in technical resources such as environmental consultants where needed.
  • Manage outside counsel. Oversee defense counsels strategy, practices, and billing so spend stays aligned with outcomes.
  • Protect the claim and the data. Maintain the integrity of financial processing and the security of confidential information in claim files.
  • Mentor and partner. Coach colleagues and serve as the claims liaison to Underwriting, Reinsurance, and other business partners.
  • Stay ahead of the law. Track legislation, court decisions, and trends affecting pollution and other specialty coverages, and advise Claims Management on any impact to claims policies and procedures.
  • Contribute beyond your desk. Participate in special projects that shape how the team works.

What we offer

  • Meaningful settlement authority and ownership of your files
  • Complex, high-impact work with direct access to Legal, Underwriting, and Reinsurance
  • Opportunities to mentor others and grow into subject matter expert or leadership roles
  • Flexible work arrangements. Liberty Mutual follows hybrid work arrangements and team members within a 50-mile radius of one of our hub offices (Westborough, MA; Boston, MA; Weatogue, CT; Suwanee, GA; Plano, TX; Hoffman Estates, IL; Indianapolis, IN; Lake Oswego, OR; Las Vegas, NV; Chandler, AZ) are expected to work from the office approximately two times per month. We will also consider highly qualified remote candidates who do not reside near a hub location.
Qualifications

What you bring

Required

  • 5-7 years of commercial casualty claims experience, including environmental or pollution claims handling
  • Proven ability to handle complex, litigated matters independently, including coverage analysis, reserving, and settlement negotiation
  • Strong command of environmental coverage issues, such as pollution legal liability, CGL pollution exclusions, and third-party bodily injury and property damage from contamination
  • Experience managing defense counsel and consultants
  • Excellent analytical, negotiation, and communication skills
  • Advanced Environmental Claims and/or Pollution Claims experience preferred
  • Experience with mass litigation and/or toxic tort required
  • Ability to obtain/maintain All-Lines Adjuster License

Nice to have

  • Experience with Superfund/CERCLA, remediation oversight, or environmental site claims
  • Background in law, environmental science, engineering, or a related field, or a professional designation (e.g., CPCU, AIC)
  • Experience handling construction defect, toxic tort, or other complex specialty lines

Job.JobTitle: Senior Underwriter, Contractors Environmental & Professional Liability
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Philadelphia, PA
  • Experience: 3 to 5 years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Senior Underwriter role in Liberty Mutual's Environmental Construction Unit underwriting contractors pollution and professional liability policies. Responsibilities include reviewing submissions, analyzing exposures, pricing risk, managing broker relationships, and developing profitable business within underwriting authority.

Good fit if you have 3-5 years of contractors pollution or professional liability underwriting or brokerage experience and strong analytical skills.

Full job description


Description

Join a dynamic, collaborative team focused on helping contractors manage some of their most complex environmental and professional liability risks. In this role, youll evaluate unique exposures, develop thoughtful insurance solutions, and work closely with brokers, clients, claims partners, and internal stakeholders to deliver meaningful value. This is an opportunity to combine technical expertise with commercial judgment. Youll review submissions, analyze operations and contracts, assess pollution and professional liability exposures, evaluate loss history, and structure terms that support both customer needs and a strong, sustainable portfolio. Because every account is different, the work is varied and requires curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to think beyond standard solutions. Youll have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, contribute to important decisions, build trusted relationships while maintaining a strong focus on technical excellence and customer service.

The Environmental Division of Liberty Mutual is seeking a Sr. Underwriter to produce and maintain a profitable book of Contractors Environmental Legal Liability (CELL) and Designers & Contractors Professional Liability (DCPL) business in our Environmental Construction Unit (ECU). Responsibilities would include underwriting contractor pollution and professional policies within underwriting authority with limited guidance from leadership. As well as make decisions on whether to underwrite business by making analytical, data-driven decisions based on data and information provided, including pricing the risk.

Key Responsibilities

  • Leverage market presence and knowledge to develop and underwrite profitable business.
  • Handle a substantial environmental pollution book of business.
  • Gather underwriting information, review, analyze, price and document, new and assigned renewal Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional business subject to established Underwriting Guidelines.
  • Prepare quotes and binders and review policies and endorsements for accuracy.
  • Manage portfolio of brokers/agents and clients.
  • Develop and support marketing strategies to increase submission flow (will require limited travel)
  • Provide exceptional service to brokers by following workflow procedures on new and renewal business in order to achieve production goals and service goals (policy issuance and file documentation).
  • Drive new business submission and premium growth through strategic sales and marketing efforts with our broker partners and internal cross-sell initiatives with other profit centers

Qualifications
  • Bachelors degree required; environmental science or similar degree preferred
  • 3-5 years of Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional Liability underwriting experience with an environmental insurance company, or 3-5 years of brokerage experience placing Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional Liability policies.
  • Excellent analytical and quantitative skills.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Initiative and ability to work independently.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across teams, stakeholders, and partners.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Youll review submissions, analyze operations and contracts, assess pollution and professional liability exposures, evaluate loss history, and structure terms that support both customer needs and a strong, sustainable portfolio. Because every account is different, the work is varied and requires curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to think beyond standard solutions. Youll have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, contribute to important decisions, build trusted relationships while maintaining a strong focus on technical excellence and customer service.

The Environmental Division of Liberty Mutual is seeking a Sr. Underwriter to produce and maintain a profitable book of Contractors Environmental Legal Liability (CELL) and Designers & Contractors Professional Liability (DCPL) business in our Environmental Construction Unit (ECU). Responsibilities would include underwriting contractor pollution and professional policies within underwriting authority with limited guidance from leadership. As well as make decisions on whether to underwrite business by making analytical, data-driven decisions based on data and information provided, including pricing the risk.

Key Responsibilities

  • Leverage market presence and knowledge to develop and underwrite profitable business.
  • Handle a substantial environmental pollution book of business.
  • Gather underwriting information, review, analyze, price and document, new and assigned renewal Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional business subject to established Underwriting Guidelines.
  • Prepare quotes and binders and review policies and endorsements for accuracy.
  • Manage portfolio of brokers/agents and clients.
  • Develop and support marketing strategies to increase submission flow (will require limited travel)
  • Provide exceptional service to brokers by following workflow procedures on new and renewal business in order to achieve production goals and service goals (policy issuance and file documentation).
  • Drive new business submission and premium growth through strategic sales and marketing efforts with our broker partners and internal cross-sell initiatives with other profit centers

Qualifications
  • Bachelors degree required; environmental science or similar degree preferred
  • 3-5 years of Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional Liability underwriting experience with an environmental insurance company, or 3-5 years of brokerage experience placing Contractors Pollution Liability and combined form Pollution / Professional Liability policies.
  • Excellent analytical and quantitative skills.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Initiative and ability to work independently.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across teams, stakeholders, and partners.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Sterling Heights, MI
  • Experience: 1+ year

About this job

Field Property Claims Adjuster for Liberty Mutual in Sterling Heights, Michigan. You will investigate property damage claims, meet customers on-site, prepare repair estimates, and manage claims from initial report to closure. Travel locally within assigned territory. Comprehensive 5-month training program provided.

Good fit if you have at least 1 year of claims handling experience, strong customer service skills, knowledge of building construction, and can live near Sterling Heights.

Full job description


Description

Join us as a Field Property Claims Adjuster where youll be responsible for helping our customers navigate the claims process and get back on their feet following damage to the homeowners property. This is a role where people who love every day to be new, different and exciting, can thrive youll be traveling on the road to meet customers in person, providing hands-on assessment of damage and empathetic support.

The Field Property Claims Adjuster will be traveling locally to insured homes within Sterling Heights, MI (48310) and surrounding areas. To be successful within the role, candidates should live within or near this area.

Sign-On Bonus Available! Were offering a sign-on bonus for experienced and actively licensed new hires.

What youll do

  • Investigate and evaluate onsite to resolve complex coverage and damage issues to include preparing complete estimates of repair for the covered damages. This may include accessing roofs by ladder, inspecting attics, crawl spaces and basements in search of damage.
  • Handle moderate to complex claims independently while managing your workload, from first notice of loss to final closure.
  • Be expected to work in a vehicle in the field daily while occasionally handling assignments from the desk.
  • Explain coverage of loss, assist policyholders with itemization of damages, emergency repairs and additional living arrangements.
  • Work with and coordinate a few vendor services such as contractors, emergency repair, cleaning services and various replacement services.
  • May be called upon for catastrophe duty.

Position details

  • Territory-based work:Most workdays will be spent in the field within your assigned local territory, giving you the opportunity to work directly with customers and gain hands-on experience.

  • Training & support:To set you up for success, youll participate in a comprehensive 5-month training program, which includes:
    • Primarily virtual and on-the-job learning.
    • Two short in-person training sessions (Weeks 4 and 7) at our Lewisville, TX office.
    • Limited overnight travel for training and team meetings (typically less than 10%).

  • Mileage Reimbursement:This role offers mileage reimbursement. You may qualify for a company-provided vehicle once mileage requirements are met. Additional details will be provided if you advance in the selection process.
Qualifications
  • Working knowledge of claims handling procedures and operations.
  • Proven ability to provide exceptional customer service.
  • Effective negotiation skills.
  • Ability to effectively and independently manage workload while exhibiting good judgment.
  • Strong written/oral communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Computer skills with the ability to work with multi-faceted systems.
  • The capabilities, skills and knowledge required through a bachelors degree or equivalent experience and at least 1 year of directly related experience.
  • Ability to obtain proper licensing as required.
  • The ability to handle multiple competing priorities and organize your day.
  • Strong time management and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated understanding of building construction principles.

We are looking for an Insurance Sales Associate to join our team in our Peoria and Chandler offices. This is not a remote position.

Were Hiring Immediately!

As an Insurance Sales Associate, you will work alongside with and support a Comparion Insurance Sales Agent in profitable growth through new business sales and customer retention. Your ability to listen and empathize are key in being the initial contact for our customers. Success in this role will require building a strong local network and in-person relationship in the community.

Working for Comparion Insurance Agency, a Liberty Mutual company, means working for a company thats committed to advancing an inclusive environment. We do that through leadership development programs aimed at advancing, engaging, and retaining under-represented talent and our Employee Resource Groups, which strengthen our inclusive workplace, enhance personal development, and provide ways for employees to connect, learn and engage.

Ready to find out what it means to work for an agency that is backed by Liberty Mutuala Fortune 100 company thats committed to putting people first, acting responsibly and making things better?

  • Utilize consultative sales techniques to prospect and initiate new business sales.
  • Assists in the processing of new business, including contacting customers to finalize sales and service transactions.
  • Identifies cross selling opportunities for Sales Agent.
  • Contributes to and executes a marketing plan with the Sales Agent.
  • Identifies mass marketing prospects through existing book of business and community prospecting opportunities.
  • Meet monthly goals for new business sales.
  • Completes follow-ups on new policies in order to keep retention level high and capitalize cross-selling opportunities.
  • Coordinates activities with other departments to ensure quality customer service
  • Acts as initial contact in addressing customer concerns regarding establishment of policies and new account status.
  • Unlicensed candidates will be enrolled in a new hire training class once they begin working for Comparion. The training includes a licensing training program in which Comparion covers the cost of training materials and exam fees.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills

  • Professional business acumen, strong presence and confidence
  • Resourceful team player that can contribute and accept new ideas

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Personal Lines Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Underwriter
Job.JobDescription:
We are seeking a Personal Lines Underwriter who is responsible for making decisions on the acceptability of insurance risks through the application of various underwriting and risk selection techniques. This position also assists in the management of assigned agents.

This is a hybrid role reporting to the Harrisburg, PA office.

POSITION COMPETENCIES

  • Business Acumen
  • Negotiation
  • Results Oriented
  • Time & Priority Management
  • Decision Making

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Communicate underwriting decisions, techniques, and interpretation of policy forms and coverages with agents.
  • Document the underwriting file for all referred risks, including the actions taken, reasons for exception made, and any follow-up diary needed.
  • Communicate to the Underwriting Manager and Territory Manager any underwriting quality or integrity concerns with individual agents.
  • Provide input to the Branch Management team about individual agency underwriting performance. (i.e., Agency Review meeting, Quarterly Results Management meeting, etc.).
  • Provides underwriting and marketing philosophy or practices, to agents and assist with training issues within agency, making periodic physical visits.
  • Maintains documentation on risk exceptions and large losses based on certain agency-specific or policy specific information.
  • Identify product risks and recommend solutions to mitigate those risks. Advise Underwriting Manager on recommended risk reduction actions and solutions.
  • Exercise underwriting flexibility within the scope of authority in making appropriate exceptions, as warranted, based on agency relationships, results and Company strategies.
  • Leverage exceptions to achieve additional business opportunities from agencies.
  • Apply underwriting and risk selection techniques to determine the acceptability of new and renewal insurance risk referrals.
  • Conduct re-underwriting programs for selected agencies to improve the profitability of their books of business.
  • Complete Claim referrals.
  • Communicate underwriting and marketing philosophy or practices, to agents and assist with training issues within agency, making periodic physical visits.
  • Conduct special re-underwriting programs in conjunction with Branch and/or Home Office Management team[s] for selected agencies to improve the profitability of their books of business.
  • Provide support for prospective book transfers, including the gathering of policy, product, and underwriting information about a book transfer opportunity.
  • Ensure the proper risk placement and/or classification for referrals, to obtain adequate premium for the exposure.
  • Visits agents as necessary independently or jointly with other PNAT staff members.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Applies data to solve common business problems.
  • Compiles, manipulates and analyses data of varying complexity.
  • Knowledgeable and proficient about what tools are available for data analysis and when they are appropriate to use.
  • Contribute to the training/mentoring of the Underwriter Trainee.
  • Contribute to the development of company underwriting policy, procedures and guidelines to assure they reflect current market conditions and contribute to the attainment of Division goals.
  • Work independently within established standards.
  • Respond to Insurance Department complaints and attend periodic hearings.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Personal Lines Underwriting Manager.

SPECIAL RELATIONSHIPS

  • Daily contact with agents and periodic physical visits to agency. Develop and maintain ongoing strong positive relationships with agents.
  • Maintain a strong communication with Territory Manager to keep them abreast of agency interactions. Contributes to the development of unit and agency plans, enforcement of the objectives and monitoring of results to assure they reflect attainment of goals and current market conditions.
  • Interacts with internal customers, external customers and insurance related entities, ie., Department of Insurance.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Credentials

  • 4 - year degree preferred.
  • Continuing education in specialized insurance courses such as IIA & AU preferred

Experience

  • Completion of Underwriter Trainee curriculum; or a minimum of 1 year experience in a property/casualty underwriting position such as a Personal Lines Assistant Underwriter.

Technical/Professional Knowledge

  • Good working knowledge of underwriting and pricing risks
  • Good working knowledge of company underwriting standards and philosophy
  • Good working knowledge of all insurance coverages
  • Good math aptitude
  • Excellent research, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Good PC skills, with an emphasis on Microsoft Office Suite; along with demonstrated proficiency in all supplied desktop tools, including the automated underwriting and email systems

The compensation has been carefully determined by considering a variety of important factors, including skill sets, experience, training, and certifications. With these considerations in mind, the estimated hiring range is $60,000 - $83,000. Additionally, you may be able to participate in our annual incentive program, depending on eligibility under the plan.

JOB REQUIREMENTS (as required by ADA - Americans with Disabilities Act)

  • This position is primarily a sedentary position that requires occasional standing and walking throughout the office environment.
  • Must be able to perform computer-based tasks and access digital information necessary for job duties, including through the use of assistive technologies.
  • Must be able to complete computer-based tasks and utilize office equipment as needed to perform essential job functions.
  • Must be able to access and enter information accurately using automated systems.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively with internal and external clients using telephone, electronic, or other communication systems.
  • Must be able to present information to individuals and groups.
  • Must be able to interpret and apply concepts that may or may not be based upon established guidelines.
  • Must be able to maintain acceptable attendance and adhere to scheduled work hours.
  • Must have a valid driver's license and be able to operate a motor vehicle.
  • Must be able to travel, with overnight stays required.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Workers' Compensation Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $75,000 to $103,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Harrisburg, PA
  • Experience: 5+ years
  • License: Valid driver's license

About this job

Investigate and manage complex workers' compensation claims from assignment to settlement, including evidence gathering, reserve establishment, and coordination with legal counsel and medical providers. Role requires independent caseload management with hybrid work available across Pennsylvania and Wisconsin offices.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of workers' compensation claims experience and understand state statutes, policy provisions, and negotiation.

Full job description

These positions investigate, evaluate and dispose of assigned claims in a timely manner in order to achieve best practices type settlements within legal statutes, policy provisions and Company and/or client guidelines.

Candidates may reside in any of the approved hiring markets, provided they can report to our Harrisburg, PA, Pittsburgh, PA or Waukesha, WI office on a hybrid basis.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Coordinate with defense counsel, handle hearing/mediation representation, negotiate settlements, and manage Medicare Set-Asides (MSAs) or liens.

  • Serve as a primary liaison between injured workers, employers, policyholders, medical providers, and agents.

  • Develops claims files from initial assignment to disposition.

  • Achieves a best practices type settlement in the disposition of claims.
  • Completes actions on a timely basis, such as verifying coverages, setting or adjusting reserves, making appropriate contacts.
  • Collaborates with Team Leader, Manager and Home Office as necessary to develop case strategy, moving the investigation along and disposing of the claim, in order to keep management, claimants, insureds and other interested parties satisfied that effective efforts are being made toward claim settlement.

The Commercial Lines Territory Manager utilizes assigned position authorities to favorably impact agent, team, and branch commercial lines results. We are seeking an Enterprise Test & Quality Lead to provide end-to-end ownership of testing across development, QA, UAT, and release activities. This role is accountable for defining and governing the test strategy, coordinating testing across multiple concurrent delivery teams, improving environment and test data readiness, and ensuring that releases meet agreed quality and business acceptance criteria. The role is particularly important in a delivery context where shared environments, constrained non-production data, and cross-team dependencies require disciplined planning, strong stakeholder management, and clear operational control.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end test management lifecycle across Unit Testing, System Integration Testing, QA, UAT, regression testing, and release readiness.

  • Define and drive a Quality Engineering strategy embedding automated testing across the SDLC including “shift-left” and “shift-right” practices.

  • Define and maintain the overall test strategy, test plans, phase entry and exit criteria, acceptance thresholds, and defect management approach. Work and align with incumbent vendor to align QA to this overall strategy.

  • Define and enforce automated quality gates within CI/CD pipelines.

  • Coordinate testing across multiple concurrent scrum teams, ensuring alignment of delivery schedules, dependencies, and release milestones.

  • Define an environment strategy that enables parallel team execution, minimizes contention, and supports continuous testing.

  • Ownership of Test Data Governance Framework

  • o Ensure adherence and support from DPO / IRM / Privacy

  • Own the approach to Test Data Management, including data readiness, lineage, masking or obfuscation controls, and interim solutions required to support testing safely and effectively.

  • Partner with QA leads to define test scenarios, test cases, regression coverage, and the appropriate level of automation, including use of tools such as Tosca to deliver ROI driven automation, decisions on what to automate and coverage targets.

  • KPI Management of QA vendor

  • SLA tracking

  • Capability and skill matrix optimization.

  • Trend analysis of defect origin (code, data, environment, design) leading to systemic issue elimination

  • Work with Product Owners and business stakeholders to secure UAT participation, define UAT scripts and acceptance criteria, and manage UAT execution to completion.

  • The Test Manager should be a critical input into the release management go / no go stage gate decisions.

  • Manage defect triage, retest cycles, and regression planning to ensure efficient resolution and minimal disruption to completed testing.

  • Provide decision grade insights on test progress, risks, defect trends, environment readiness, and overall release confidence to project and executive stakeholders.

  • Drive continuous improvement in test practices, with a focus on moving from reactive or waterfall-like testing toward a more agile, disciplined, and scalable operating model.

  • Define and oversee post release validation strategies, including observability, monitoring, and production quality feedback loops.

  • Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience in Test Management, QA leadership, or quality engineering leadership within complex technology delivery environments.

  • Strong understanding of end-to-end software testing practices across unit, integration, system, regression, data lineage and user acceptance testing.

  • Experience managing testing in agile delivery environments with multiple concurrent teams and shared environments.

  • Practical knowledge of test automation and engineering led strategy and tooling, ideally including Tosca or comparable platforms, especially AI driven technologies and processes.

  • Strong understanding of environment management and test data management, including handling of sensitive data in non-production environments.

  • Ability to define quality gates, release readiness criteria, and structured defect management processes.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across engineering, QA, product, operations, and business teams.

  • Excellent planning, coordination, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and delivery risk.

  • Experience in regulated or control-conscious environments is highly desirable.

  • Experience of integrating testing into DevOps pipelines and familiarity with release orchestration and production validation techniques.

  • Experience of operating in SAFe (scaled agile) frameworks


Success Measures

  • Improved coordination and predictability across QA and UAT cycles including continuous validation and early user involvement.

  • Reduction in defects caused by environment or data issues rather than true functional failures.

  • Clear and consistently applied phase entry, exit, and acceptance criteria.

  • Increased confidence in release readiness and reduced rework or defect recycling.

  • Greater use of automation and regression coverage to support faster retest cycles.

  • Stronger governance, visibility, and accountability for end-to-end testing outcomes.


Key Interfaces
This role will work closely with Development Leads, QA Leads, Product Owners, Business UAT representatives, Environment and Release Management teams, Data and Privacy stakeholders, and senior programme or technology leadership.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Relevant testing or quality certifications such as ISTQB Advanced Test Manager or equivalent are desirable.

  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or other highly regulated delivery environments would be advantageous.

Responsibilities include vendor management, resource onboarding, risk monitoring, stakeholder engagement, and process optimization for Travelers' global sourcing portfolio.

Good fit if you have experience in sourcing, vendor management, supplier performance tracking, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$101,600.00 - $167,600.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Member of the Sourcing and Supplier Management team within Tech & Ops Finance responsible for enterprise-wide sourcing and supplier strategies, governance, performance management, risk and operational processes for Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships.

As a Manager, Sourcing Strategy, Management and Governance, you will play a critical role in executing work order processes across assigned business lines and area-specific strategic sourcing strategies, including sourcing model design, supplier selection, and alignment of suppliers to business needs across our professional services and outsourcing partner portfolio. You will serve as a key point of contact on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance across assigned lines, partnering closely with business stakeholders to track activity, resolve issues, and identify opportunities to improve how the team operates. This position does not manage others.

What Will You Do?

  • Work Order/Vendor Management and Sourcing Strategy: Manage a defined set of supplier work orders or portfolio activities across multiple assigned lines, including intake, modifications, closures, data-driven analysis, and process and tool optimization. Serve as a proactive sourcing advisor to LOB stakeholders, providing counsel on sourcing model selection, supplier performance, and workforce demand planning. Apply enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures to work being requested, advising stakeholders on right model, right supplier, right rate.*      
  • Onboarding and Team Support: Oversee resource onboarding and monitor engaged resources for quality, progress, and team dynamics. Own resource onboarding end-to-end, including understanding the skills required for the work being engaged, validating skill requirements with LOB stakeholders, and driving Technical Assessments. Cultivate ongoing, trusted relationships with the owners of the work, including engagement managers and LOB stakeholders, staying close enough to the business to anticipate needs, flag risks early, and bring forward solutions before issues escalate. Partner with Circle Leads on resource and team alignment needs.     
  • Proactivity and Risk Management: Monitor assigned vendor performance data and flag early indicators of risk or control gaps, addressing delivery issues as they arise and escalating when appropriate. Analyze work order data, supplier capability changes, and sourcing market conditions to identify business continuity risks, surface insights, and deliver proactive recommendations to leadership. Maintain deep understanding of assigned business lines to anticipate workforce needs, monitor internal demands, and inform sourcing strategy.    
  • Internal and External Stakeholder Engagement: Build and sustain trusted relationships with business stakeholders, finance partners, and assigned supplier contacts to surface risks, resolve delivery concerns and budget variances, and support governance interactions, performance discussions, and sourcing process coordination. Provide data and updates supporting ELT visibility for assigned lines on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance.      
  • Work Transition and Migration: Own the operational execution of work transitions when sourcing decisions result in a change of supplier, sourcing model, or workforce composition. This includes coordinating the migration of work from internal resources to external suppliers, managing supplier transitions, supporting onboarding of new supplier teams, and ensuring continuity of delivery throughout the transition period. Partner closely with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and the S&SM Strategy team to sequence and execute transitions in alignment with enterprise sourcing strategy and workforce plans.      
  • Process Optimization: Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities, including AI-enabled workflow enhancements. Optimize like work across assigned lines, standardizing repeatable processes, eliminating redundancy, and driving consistency across the Sourcing Delivery and Execution team. Champion the use of Travelers' AI tooling to streamline reporting, automate recurring workflows, and improve the quality and speed of work.      
  • Rate Card Adherence: Ensure compliance with established enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures. Partner with the S&SM Strategy team to validate that work being requested aligns to the appropriate rate card, role designation, and sourcing model, and assist stakeholders in understanding and adhering to rate card guidelines.
  • Track and report on sourcing footprint, role utilization, team composition, and premium role usage across assigned lines. 
  • Manage sourcing activity across multiple assigned lines or areas. Bring cross-line perspective to sourcing decisions, identify patterns and efficiencies across the portfolio, and ensure consistent application of enterprise sourcing strategy regardless of line-specific variation. 
  • Monitor work order alignment to budget; proactively flag variances and partner with DFRs to resolve. 
  • Contribute to the preparation of Business Review materials and Monthly Operating Review (MOR) data for assigned lines, supporting leadership visibility into supplier performance, workforce trends, and sourcing activity across the portfolio. 
  • Partner cross-functionally with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and Procurement to support sourcing and contracting activity, ensure alignment on budget and resource plans, and facilitate resolution of issues that span organizational boundaries. 
  • Engage with and learn Travelers' AI tooling, applying these capabilities to improve the speed and quality of recurring work such as reporting, data analysis, and workflow management. 

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience required.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in sourcing, workforce strategy, supplier management, or a related field.
  • Experience with Fieldglass, ACS, and workforce planning tools strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting or managing work transitions, supplier migrations, or sourcing model changes preferred.
  • Familiarity with rate card structures, role modernization concepts, and supplier performance principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior LOB or technology leaders.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements or automation opportunities.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and large language models (e.g., Claude); demonstrated ability or willingness to integrate AI capabilities into day-to-day work processes preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, including Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong working knowledge of sourcing models: managed services, staff augmentation, GSO, POD/catalog models, and rate card structures.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, ambiguous situations and drive to resolution with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to evaluate sourcing data, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable recommendations for business partners.
  • Process improvement and automation orientation, with experience identifying and implementing operational efficiencies.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with senior LOB leaders and building trusted advisor relationships.
  • Demonstrated initiative in identifying and adopting tools, technology, and process improvements that increase team efficiency and output quality, including AI-enabled solutions.
  • Demonstrated proficiency or willingness to actively develop proficiency with AI-powered tools, including large language models such as Claude; ability to apply these tools to sourcing workflows, reporting, and operational tasks to improve efficiency and output quality.
  • Ability to operate effectively through change and ambiguity, adapting approaches as the function evolves.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present information clearly to stakeholders at all levels.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, multiple workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously in a fast-moving environment.

What is a Must Have?

Full job description

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers Insurance is seeking a highly skilled and knowledgeable Claim Counsel to join our Bond & Specialty Insurance team. Bond & Specialty Insurance (BSI) provides management and professional liability, cyber, crime insurance, and surety bonds to or on behalf of businesses and/or nonprofits of all sizes. The BSI Claim Counsel team conducts thorough investigation, analysis, evaluation, and disposition of claims and claim litigation to achieve superior customer service and to optimize claim results. As a Claim Counsel, you will effectively manage all assigned BSI claims, typically of lower to moderate severity and complexity within our organization and with moderate guidance from management. You will manage outside counsel relationships, negotiate settlements, and ensure stakeholders are supported throughout the claims process. In addition to comprehensive claim and risk management, you also will provide legal advice and/or insight to our underwriting colleagues and non-attorney claim colleagues and contribute to BSI claim strategic initiatives.

What Will You Do?

  • Analyze, investigate, and resolve Bond & Specialty claims of predominantly lower to moderate severity and complexity, with moderate supervision, following operational policies.
  • Retain, monitor, and manage outside counsel (and other vendors as applicable) by actively utilizing incident response and/or litigation management plans and budgets, and negotiate settlements when appropriate to ensure effective legal and/or claim outcomes, involving litigation matters of lower to moderate severity and complexity.
  • Prepare management reports on loss development, financial exposure, and resolution strategies with general guidance from management.
  • Develop and coordinate recovery efforts with the Recovery Management Unit to optimize loss mitigation opportunities, as needed.
  • Attend mediations, settlement conferences, trials, depositions to support claim resolution, and may attend other internal/external business meetings.
  • With moderate oversight, provide a variety of legal and business support to underwriting colleagues which varies by business unit and may include negotiating indemnity documentation, drafting product forms and endorsements, reviewing contracts and bond forms, all involving matters of lower to moderate complexity, and supporting marketing and/or risk management efforts through broker visits and seminars.
  • Monitor industry trends and market dynamics, and proactively communicate key insights and strategic initiatives to relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure stakeholders/customers feel 'secure, respected, and cared for' throughout the duration of the claims process.
  • Ensure compliance with BSI Claims processes, procedures, and best practices.
  • Maintain thorough documentation of claim activities, decisions, and communications, adhering to record-keeping standards and confidentiality protocols.
  • To perform the essential functions of this job, acquisition and maintenance of Insurance Adjuster License(s) is required to comply with state and Travelers' requirements. Generally, license(s) must be obtained within three months of starting the job and must obtain ongoing continuing education credits as mandated. Additionally, the maintenance of an active legal license in the state of your principal office location and remaining current with all Continuing Legal Education (CLE) is required to perform this role.
  • Prepare timely and thorough coverage evaluations and correspondence to Insureds.
  • Maintain and note claim files pursuant to company best practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Five or more years of relevant legal or claim handling work experience.

  • Strong time management skills with the ability to proactively manage multiple priorities with an attention to detail, data and analytics.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on an Excel/VBA Annuity Modeling Specialist to join our Retail Solutions organization in a hybrid work environment. We are open to candidates in the following key city locations: Charlotte (NC), Fort Wayne (IN), Greensboro (NC), Hartford (CT), Omaha (NE) and Radnor (PA).

Background Details

As the Excel/VBA Annuity Modeling Specialist, you will contribute to the development of benchmark test tools for our annuity illustration, administration, and other product platforms. Working under general supervision and following established guidelines, you will apply working knowledge of Excel and VBA to build and maintain spreadsheet models that verify the accuracy of our systems. This position supports analysis for stakeholders across the Annuities group while delivering on routine assignments within its assigned area. The incumbent also serves as a resource for annuity product technical questions and supports other ad hoc annuity analytical initiatives as needed.

What you'll be doing

  • You will support the development and implementation of Excel-based testing models for Variable, Fixed, Indexed, Immediate and Deferred Income Annuities to ensure the accuracy of our illustration system(s), digital platform(s), administration system(s), and any other supporting system(s), including but not limited to: adding new products to existing spreadsheet models, creating new spreadsheets for new products, and updating existing spreadsheets for product changes.
  • You will work collaboratively with fellow team members to meet shared goals and deadlines.
  • You will leverage AI tools to enhance and accelerate spreadsheet modeling, testing, and analysis workflows.
  • You will assist in debugging systems and help determine the sources of differences from the benchmark tool.
  • You will respond to straightforward queries from distribution regarding product illustrations and projections.
  • You will work with Operations and the Product Implementation team to support production-related calculation issues.
  • You will maintain working knowledge of current developments and trends for assigned area(s) of responsibility.
  • You will support and positively contribute to departmental and enterprise change management initiatives within assigned area(s) of responsibility.
  • You will perform and deliver on routine assignments/projects while applying working knowledge of assigned area(s) of responsibility.
  • You will serve as a resource for ad hoc annuity product analysis assignments as needed.

What we're looking for

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's Degree, preferably in mathematics, computer science, or a similar technical field.
  • 1–3+ Years of experience in Excel modeling that directly aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position.
  • Working knowledge of spreadsheets and programming experience with VBA.
  • Experience using AI platforms (i.e., CoPilot, Claude).
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills; detail-oriented, motivated, and eager to learn.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret both internal and external documents.
  • Ability to apply mathematical concepts such as probability, statistics, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical solutions.
  • Ability to solve challenging but noncomplex problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables where guidelines exist.
  • Ability to collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
  • Ability to evaluate trends in data or information.
  • Understanding of annuity products and markets preferred, or a willingness to develop it.
  • Ability to work with others in a collaborative team environment under general supervision.
  • Demonstrated relationship management skills with internal clients (e.g., management, peers, and colleagues).
  • Demonstrates strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and multi-task while maintaining attention to detail.

Position Summary

With limited supervision, translates near-term and long-term business needs of moderate to high complexity into (technical) initiative solution options across multiple portfolios. Provides enterprise-level context to the architecture team to enable team members to focus, mature domains, and create future-state architectures. Provides leadership visibility on complex initiatives by facilitating discussions, leading conceptual and high level design sessions, capturing the results in artifacts, and ensuring the architectural design is realized through delivery for multiple enterprise stakeholders.


What You'll Do

As a Senior Solutions Architect – Data, you'll play a key role in shaping ERIE's enterprise data strategy. You'll design and implement scalable, modern data architectures that ensure accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across the organization. You'll collaborate closely with data engineering, analytics, and business partners to align data initiatives with enterprise goals and deliver trusted, high-quality data solutions that power decision-making.

Your expertise will guide the design and integration of enterprise data systems—connecting traditional on-premises environments with modern, cloud-based ecosystems that support ERIE.


Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing enterprise data architectures that promote data quality and consistency.
  • Proficiency with Master Data Management (MDM) tools such as Informatica MDM, Reltio, SAP MDG, or IBM InfoSphere.
  • Strong understanding of data integration, governance, metadata management, and data stewardship principles.
  • Experience with data modeling, APIs, ETL design, and modern cloud data platforms (AWS, Azure, or similar).
  • Proven ability to collaborate across disciplines to define strategy and deliver scalable data solutions.
  • Familiarity with AWS services such as S3, Glue, or Redshift is a plus.


What Makes You Stand Out

You're a strategic thinker with a builder's mindset. You connect architecture vision with practical delivery—creating data systems that drive measurable business value. You balance innovation and structure, ensuring ERIE's data assets are both trusted and transformative.

You stand out because you:

  • Combine deep MDM expertise with practical cloud architecture experience.
  • Have a track record of integrating on-premises and cloud data environments.
  • Foster strong partnerships between IT and business, translating data strategy into real outcomes.
  • Bring curiosity, adaptability, and a continuous improvement mindset to every challenge.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Serves as the single point of accountability for architecture function to portfolio owner customers and technology leadership.
  • Provides architectural guidance on initiatives of moderate to high complexity across multiple enterprise portfolios, while managing multiple customers with differing priorities on the organization's most strategic initiatives.
  • Provides full-stack architectural options that enable business objectives while ensuring long-term technology goals for all aspects of a solution.
  • Collaborates with team members for technical validation during design and planning phases.
  • Informs aspects of portfolio maturity regarding technology and ability to achieve target technology alignment, while facilitating a minimum viable architecture.
  • Monitors large-scale project execution and considers and interprets architectural tradeoffs occurring during delivery. Escalates for appropriate context sharing and decision making, as necessary.
  • Proactively enables portfolio owners to see technical debt clearly, provides appropriate context to inform plans to achieve elimination of technical debt in a comprehensive plan across multiple portfolios, delivery teams, programs, or projects.
  • Serves as a mentor for other members of the team, builds an environment for analysts, engineers, architects, and other technology leaders to grow and have high impact.
  • Directs and drives closure on investment decisions within the enterprise while also identifying cross-portfolio impacts on significant delivery initiatives.
  • Serves as a subject matter expert for multiple portfolios, providing actionable recommendations via consultation services, adapted to stakeholder context, to technology leadership and organizational stakeholders.
  • Collaborates with architects, portfolio owners, and other job families to achieve an enterprise view; provides project and program level views to project and program teams in context of enterprise strategies and directions with light supervision.
  • Supports business agility through agile engagement across multiple delivery operations.
  • Interprets business needs, assesses solution choices, applies technology, and provides project guidance within a long-term enterprise lens.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Product Owner plays a pivotal role in driving the successful development and delivery of innovative products that meet the needs of our customers and aligns with the company's strategic goals. This role acts as the bridge between business stakeholders, development teams and end-users, ensuring clear communication and effective prioritization of features and enhancements throughout the product lifecycle.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Maximizes the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum team.

  • Defines and communicates product vision, overall strategy and growth opportunities to business and IT stakeholders, with guidance from leadership and other Product team members.

  • Drives the continuous refinement of the product vision, roadmap, and strategy to drive optimum business value.

  • Works closely with business stakeholders across the organization to convert product ideas into a prioritized backlog according to business value or return on investment (ROI).

  • Participates in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, iteration reviews, and retrospectives to ensure continuous improvement and iterative development.

  • Facilitates Product Grooming Backlog sessions to align priority & strategy for better cross functional collaboration.

  • Validates roadmap items prior to starting development work with guidance from business stakeholders as needed.

  • Remains accountable for each stage of the development process and the final product, evaluating progress and performance at each iteration and deciding whether the team can move on to the next steps.

  • Works closely with Technical Product Managers and Scrum master to ensure the successful execution of the product roadmap.

  • Anticipates product's future needs by maintaining user personas and journey maps.

  • Owns and drives user-centric product outcomes collaboratively with business and IT leadership.

  • Researches and analyzes market trends and user needs to develop and shape the roadmap for the product.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university is required with a major or emphasis in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field. Minimum 6 years of related experience inclusive of leading technical teams, collecting business needs, and translating requirements to a technical audience. Experience in the insurance industry highly desired. Minimum 3 years of experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar role, with a track record of successfully launching and managing products or platforms.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Certified Product Owner (CPO) required, SAFe preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Knowledge of Agile processes and principles. Understanding of the Insurance industry. Ability to map value stream across business lines. Possess technical expertise and understanding of product development practices. Ability to balance technical constraints and a differentiated product that meets the needs of the marketplace. Knowledge of mobile and web platform design conventions and technology limitations and opportunities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience working with cross-functional teams, and presenting to leadership. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Word, Visio, Excel, Project, and PowerPoint. Excellent organizational and time management skills. Advanced analytical, qualitative, quantitative, and problem-solving skills. Ability to apply critical thinking and analytical skills to recommend creative solutions to business and technical challenges. Strong attention to detail. Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

Company Details

As an elite Excess and Surplus Lines market, Nautilus Insurance Group offers commercial property and casualty insurance solutions to appointed wholesale surplus lines producers countrywide. We have specialized in providing these solutions for more than 35 years.

We have more flexible policy terms and premium rates on a non-admitted basis. Our focus is small to medium Property and Casualty risks on both an admitted and a non-admitted basis.

  • Can you hear us now? Employees are eligible for special cell phone service discounts with Verizon and AT&T. We've got a plum position for you! We participate in the Plum Benefits program offering employees cost-free access to thousands of exclusive travel and entertainment discounts.

Responsibilities

The Litigation Specialist's job function includes efficiently and effectively handling advanced-level, primarily litigated, commercial third-party general liability losses in a “paperless” environment. An ability to communicate both verbally and in written form in a prompt, courteous and professional manner is essential.

This role can be located in our Scottsdale AZ office, or remotely for a highly qualified candidate.

  • Reviews and sets up new loss assignments in a timely manner in compliance with Department guidelines and best practices.
  • Establishes appropriate initial loss and expense reserves and continues to regularly evaluate the file for adequacy, accuracy and adherence to reserving guidelines.
  • Analyzes and interprets policy language in conjunction with specific loss facts to reach appropriate coverage decisions.
  • Drafts frequent and complex coverage correspondence, including reservation of rights and coverage disclaimers in compliance with various state statutes and regulations.
  • Composes a variety of other detailed correspondence to insureds, claimants, attorneys, agents and Regulatory agencies.
  • Proactively manages primarily litigated claim files from inception to closure, including identification and investigation of coverage, liability and damage issues, determination and efficient execution of an appropriate plan of action, and prompt, economical file resolution, in compliance with Department guidelines and best practices.
  • Appropriately and clearly documents all claim file activity, including current strategy, plan of action and exit plan in file notes.
  • Consistently demonstrates comprehensive coverage analysis, investigation, evaluation and negotiation skills at an advanced level.
  • Directs and controls the activities and costs of numerous outside vendors including defense counsel and coverage counsel, experts and independent adjusters.
  • Effectively presents and discusses loss facts and issues in roundtable discussions to peers and members of management at all levels.
  • Composes and transmits on a regular and timely basis frequent Large Loss Reports and other detailed reporting documents as appropriate.
  • Manages and monitors file caseload through the use of various resources.
  • Obtains all required state adjuster licenses and maintains them as required via compliance with mandatory continuing education requirements.
  • Other duties may be assigned.
  • Serves as a technical resource within the Department through mentoring and knowledge-sharing, whether one-on-one, in small groups, or presentations to larger groups.
  • Meets with intern personnel and others as needed to provide job function overview and/or specific subject-matter training.
  • Occasional participation in projects and initiatives led by other departments and/or W. R. Berkley companies, including audits, workshops, focus groups, task forces, etc.
  • Initiates appropriate communication with members of management and other Departments.
  • Attends internal and external seminars and other training events and provides feedback to peers and/or members of management.

Job Description

Broker I, National Casualty

The National Casualty Practice is a premier team of casualty brokerage professionals with extensive experience in representing buyers of primary and umbrella/excess liability. We are looking to add a broker to our Primary Casualty team!

We are considering applicants in Dallas and Houston, Texas!

This is a hybrid role with at least three days a week in the office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

How this opportunity is different

Our primary brokers are experts in their field and handle a variety of clients and program structures. You'll work closely with a diverse team of seasoned brokers, accounts executives, and risk analysts, each bringing a wealth of knowledge and experience to the table. This position offers you a unique opportunity to develop professionally, expand your expertise, and make an impact in the world of primary casualty. Thank you for your time and consideration.

What the day will look like

  • Thorough analysis of current risk transfer programs to include coverage and cost analysis and a graphical representation of the program.
  • Insurance program structure planning and design of alternatives.
  • Provide benchmarking analysis related to limits and coverage terms.
  • Prepare all marketplace insurance submissions, coordinate and conduct market meetings and negotiations as appropriate in coordination with Account Executives. May include some travel.
  • Finalize all quotes and complete a thorough comparison of program options as part of the client proposal presentation. Comparison to include changes in exposures, losses, collateral, coverage terms and conditions and cost of risk.
  • Serve as a primary or secondary market contact as assigned and in accordance with established policy.
  • As part of a team, you are expected to educate and advise fellow team members on coverage issues, markets, and related developments.
  • Serve as team member for Aon's broking library and periodically contribute to the library and related best practices.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Casualty broker with 2+ years of experience working in primary placements and/or in casualty. Will be asked to work directly with clients as lead broker or secondary broker to build primary casualty programs, as well as participate on new business opportunities.
  • Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions.
  • An experienced primary casualty broker or underwriter with a solid understanding of and relationships with insurance company management and underwriting teams/personnel.
  • Strong written and communication skills necessary to communicate in a professional manner with clients and the marketplace.
  • A strong team player who understands the roles and responsibilities of other Aon professionals on the team, assumes responsibility for the timely delivery of a professional work product in accordance with assigned roles, and facilitates communication among team members.
  • Promote creativity in presenting new ideas and approaches for clients or prospects; promote a positive attitude in always trying to improve a program.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of industry experience.
  • Property and Casualty Brokers License is required (can be attained on the job)

Job Description

Executive Benefits Specialist - Nonqualified Deferred Compensation (NQDC)

Are you looking to join an industry-leading team and deliver high-quality service in a client-focused environment? If so, consider our Executive Benefits Specialist role.

Aon is seeking a detail-oriented benefits or financial services professional to support the administration of nonqualified deferred compensation (NQDC) plans and related executive benefit programs. You will work with corporate plan sponsors, executive-level participants, recordkeeping and administrative systems, and internal partners to deliver accurate, timely, and high-touch service.

The strongest candidates will have direct NQDC experience or transferable experience in retirement plan administration, pension administration, executive compensation, stock plan administration, trust or recordkeeping operations, payroll administration, or another regulated financial-services environment involving participant accounts, plan provisions, transactions, and reconciliations.

This hybrid position offers flexibility to work both virtually and from our Atlanta, GA, Dallas, TX, or Radnor, PA offices. Although we would prefer candidates to work hybrid in one of above offices, we would be willing to consider a virtual work arrangement for a strong candidate.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Administer recurring NQDC plan activities, including annual enrollment, deferral elections, company contributions, vesting, investment allocations, distributions, and participant data changes.
  • Interpret plan provisions and established administrative procedures to respond to plan sponsor and participant questions accurately.
  • Coordinate data and transaction activity with clients, payroll teams, recordkeepers, trustees, carriers, and internal partners.
  • Reconcile participant and plan-level data, investigate discrepancies, document findings, and drive issues to resolution.
  • Prepare client reports, participant communications, enrollment materials, transaction files, and administrative calendars.
  • Maintain accurate plan documentation, participant records, procedures, and audit support materials.
  • Use Excel and database tools to validate data, analyze activity, and support recurring and ad hoc reporting.
  • Manage multiple client deliverables and deadlines while maintaining strong quality controls and confidentiality.
  • Identify process improvements that strengthen accuracy, efficiency, consistency, and the client and participant experience.
  • Build knowledge of NQDC plan mechanics, Internal Revenue Code Section 409A, corporate-owned life insurance (COLI), and related executive benefit arrangements.

How this opportunity is different

Aon's Executive Benefits team specializes in programs designed for executives and other select employees. This role offers exposure to the administration, participant experience, financial data, and operational controls associated with nonqualified deferred compensation and related executive benefit programs. It is a focused opportunity for someone who wants to build deeper expertise in the retirement and executive compensation space rather than broad-based health and welfare benefits.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 2-5 years of experience in at least one of the following areas:
    • Nonqualified deferred compensation or executive benefit plan administration;
    • Qualified retirement or pension plan administration, recordkeeping, or participant services;
    • Executive compensation, equity or stock plan administration;
    • Trust, custody, payroll, accounting, or financial-services operations involving participant accounts, transactions, reconciliations, and plan or contract provisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with detailed plan, financial, payroll, or participant data and reconcile discrepancies.
  • Intermediate Excel capability, including formulas, lookups, filters, sorting, conditional logic, and data validation, or the ability to demonstrate comparable analytical skills.
  • Ability to read and apply plan provisions, procedures, or other technical documentation.
  • Strong client service, written communication, problem-solving, organization, and follow-through.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines and deliver accurate work in a controlled environment.

Preferred skills and experience:

  • Direct experience administering NQDC plans, 409A plans, SERPs, excess or restoration plans, or executive retirement arrangements.
  • Experience with annual enrollment, deferral elections, distributions, vesting, participant statements, payroll files, or plan-level reconciliation.
  • Familiarity with Section 409A, COLI, rabbi trusts, nonqualified plan recordkeeping, or executive benefit funding concepts.
  • Experience supporting corporate clients or executive-level participants in a consultative service environment.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related field (or equivalent experience)

Pay Transparency

The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $50,000 - $85,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant's education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. Full job description

Job Description

Surety Account Manager III

Are you a surety professional who thrives at the intersection of client service, underwriting strategy, and operational execution? Join a high-performing team and take on a meaningful role managing and delivering surety bond solutions for many clients!

This hybrid position requires working 3 days a week from an Aon office.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Provides analytical and operational services for a portfolio of surety bond clients, with an emphasis on accuracy, client interaction, underwriting pricing rigor & negotiation, and execution quality. Partners closely with clients to facilitate timely issuance of surety obligations. Reports to the regional Surety Operations leader. (Director or Team Lead).

  • Operates with a high degree of autonomy and judgment across complex or strategically significant accounts and in dealing with markets.
  • Takes primary accountability for handling selected key accounts, including coordination of large bond programs and sophisticated underwriting submissions.
  • Possesses strong, in-depth knowledge of surety bonds, including contract and commercial surety, indemnity structures, and market dynamics.
  • Serves as a technical lead within the team; assists in training, mentoring, and developing internal team, and contributes to improvement in execution initiatives.
  • Collaborates daily with carriers on complex needs. Prepares and processes a broad range of surety instruments, including but not limited to bid, final, miscellaneous, and court bonds, ensuring alignment with underwriting parameters and client requirements.
  • Collaborates daily with clients on complex needs. Completes Consents of Surety, Prequalification Letters, Riders, and other client required obligations per State requirements. Determines appropriate documentation to finalize issuance, i.e. power-of-attorney, resident license, etc. with attention to contractual, legal, and financial implications.
  • Prepares General Indemnity Agreements and bond applications, coordinating with and advising clients to obtain complete, accurate financial and corporate information for underwriting review – including any other nuanced client needs or requirements.
  • Maintains and facilitates data integrity and enabling proactive management of bond programs in AonBondLink (ABL).
  • Works closely with internal collaborators to build and maintain accurate, complete electronic bond files in AonBondLink (ABL). It also confirms and manages client financial and underwriting records while following internal controls and audit requirements to avoid E&O.
  • Manages countersignature requirements and related jurisdictional nuances to support compliant bond issuance across multiple states and territories.
  • Provides technical surety guidance and support to non-surety colleagues, helping interpret bond forms, indemnity requirements, and program structures for internal stakeholders.
  • Coordinates receipt and organization of pertinent client related underwriting information (e.g., financial statements, work-in-progress schedules, bank information, organizational documents) to support timely carrier decisions.
  • Verifies that all bonds are issued within established surety lines of credit and brokerage authority; assists in structuring and negotiating approvals for bond requests that exceed standard limits or fall outside delegated authority.

How this opportunity is different

Unlike many surety operations roles focused mainly on transaction processing, this position combines technical surety expertise with client advisory duties and meaningful market involvement. You will work directly with complex bonding programs, underwriting negotiations, and carrier relationships while acting as a trusted resource for clients and internal colleagues. The role also allows for broader influence through mentoring, participation in operational improvement, and responsibility for critical compliance and underwriting workflows. For professionals wanting to move beyond administrative bond issuance and act as a strategic partner in the surety process, this is an outstanding chance to increase visibility, expand impact, and grow within a leading organization.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Is able to effectively interpret a wide range of technical instructions and documentation involving abstract and concrete variables, including financial analyses, contractual provisions, and underwriting guidelines.
  • Possesses experience or formal education in Risk Management, Insurance, and/or Surety, and applies this background to enhance client and market outcomes.
  • Demonstrates strong organizational, time-management, and multi-tasking skills, consistently managing high-volume and complex workloads.
  • Maintains Notary Public designation.
  • Maintains Power of Attorney appointments with major surety markets and is regarded as a trusted signatory.
  • Maintains appropriate Producer license
  • Is proficient in all required technology platforms, including AonBondLink, Bridge, and Outlook, and utilizes these systems to manage data, analyze bond portfolios, and support decision-making.

Education and licensing requirements: A Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is preferred for this position. Maintain Notary Public designation and hold the appropriate Property and Casualty license.
