About this job

Senior Compensation Analyst at Assurant supporting competitive pay decisions through market pricing, job evaluation, and data analysis. Works independently managing compensation programs and develops insights for leaders across functions and geographies.

Good fit if you have 5+ years in compensation, human resources, finance or data analytics with market pricing and survey experience.

Full job description

Overview of Position

The Senior Compensation Analyst serves as a key analytical and consultative partner within Assurant's Global Compensation team. This role transforms complex compensation and workforce data into meaningful insights and recommendations that support competitive, equitable, and financially responsible pay decisions.


Working with compensation leaders, People Business Partners, Finance, and business stakeholders, the Senior Compensation Analyst independently manages market pricing, job evaluation, annual compensation programs, data analysis, reporting, and complex stakeholder requests. The role applies compensation expertise, analytical judgment, and knowledge of internal practices and external market trends to identify risks, evaluate alternatives, and recommend practical solutions.


The Senior Compensation Analyst will also help advance the function's future-state capabilities by identifying opportunities to improve compensation processes through automation, AI-enabled tools, enhanced reporting, and process augmentation.


What will my duties and responsibilities be in this job?


  • Independently manage recurring compensation programs, processes, analyses, and complex stakeholder requests.
  • Conduct job evaluations, market pricing, benchmarking, and salary survey activities; interpret findings and develop well-supported recommendations.
  • Evaluate job responsibilities, organizational context, internal compensation relationships, and external market practices to assess role scope, level, and competitive positioning.
  • Analyze compensation trends, salary movement, incentive outcomes, pay equity, and other workforce compensation matters.
  • Build market-pricing analyses, financial and scenario models, dashboards, recurring and ad hoc reports, and executive-ready presentations.
  • Support the design, planning, testing, execution, and evaluation of annual compensation programs, including merit, promotion, salary-planning, and incentive processes.
  • Review compensation requests and transactions, identify exceptions and risks, and recommend solutions consistent with compensation philosophy, guidelines, and governance.
  • Translate complex compensation data and technical concepts into clear, practical guidance for People Business Partners, managers, and business leaders.
  • Perform data-quality reviews, audits, modeling, testing, and reconciliation; identify trends, discrepancies, and opportunities for corrective action.
  • Lead or contribute to compensation projects and continuous-improvement initiatives, including requirements gathering, analysis, documentation, implementation, and change support.
  • Identify opportunities to improve compensation workflows through automation, AI, digital tools, standardized reporting, and stronger quality controls.
  • Monitor external market trends, regulatory developments, and evolving compensation practices to inform program decisions.
  • Maintain accurate job descriptions, market matches, compensation records, analytical methodologies, and process documentation.
  • Share technical knowledge, tools, and effective practices with junior team members.

Location & Work Arrangement

  • This position is based in the United States and follows the work arrangement established for the selected location. The role collaborates regularly with stakeholders across functions and geographies. Occasional meetings outside standard local business hours may be required to support global stakeholders or annual compensation processes.

What are the requirements needed for this position?


  • Minimum of 5 years of progressive professional experience in Compensation, Total Rewards, Human Resources, Finance, data analytics, or a related field, including meaningful experience supporting compensation programs and analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience with market pricing, job evaluation, salary surveys, compensation analysis, and annual compensation processes.
  • Experience using AI-enabled tools to augment processes, improve data analysis, or enhance stakeholder service.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel proficiency, including the ability to analyze, reconcile, model, and clearly present complex datasets.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to identify trends and risks, evaluate alternatives, and develop practical recommendations.
  • Ability to translate technical compensation concepts and analytical findings into clear guidance for varied audiences.
  • Strong project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver accurate work within established deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy, consistency, and quality.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, work independently, and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Ability to handle sensitive employee and compensation information with discretion and confidentiality.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across functions, geographies, and organizational levels.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?


  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Professional compensation certification or progress toward certification, such as Certified Compensation Professional, or CCP.
  • Experience supporting global compensation programs or working within a multinational organization.
  • Experience with Workday or another human resources information system and compensation-planning platform.
  • Experience with compensation surveys and market-data platforms, job architecture, salary structures, incentive plans, or pay-equity analysis.
  • Experience developing dashboards, data visualizations, automated reporting, or other technology-enabled compensation solutions.
  • Demonstrated success partnering with People Business Partners, business leaders, Finance, Legal, or other cross-functional stakeholders.

Why Join Us?

Join a collaborative Global Compensation team where you will have meaningful ownership of compensation analyses, programs, and stakeholder support. You will have the opportunity to deepen your technical expertise, influence compensation decisions, lead process improvements, and help shape the continued evolution of Assurant's global Compensation and Total Rewards practices.


This role is well suited for a compensation professional who enjoys turning complex data into practical recommendations and wants to help advance the function through stronger analytics, automation, AI adoption, and technology-enabled solutions.

This is an onsite role in our Mt. Juliet TN facility with a schedule of Friday - Sunday, 5AM – 5:30PM.

  • Monitors tableau/Oracle reporting to ensure dashboards are current, investigating and resolving the issues
  • Research and resolve issues preventing devices, shipments, materials, authorizations from moving through respective department/processes
  • Communicates with established representative to rectify problems related to order cancelations, materials transactions, call center support, shortages, damage, nonconformances

  • As a SME Train and/or cross trains associates as needed

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Talent Acquisition Specialist, Human Resources & Training
Job.JobDescription:
The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth. This program offers students meaningful, real-world experience while building foundational technical and business skills in a Fortune 500 organization.


Assurant is seeking a motivated People Organization (HR) Intern to support strategic initiatives within the Talent Acquisition (TA) organization. This role will focus on enhancing the hiring manager experience through survey development, process documentation, content creation, analytics support and change management.


This internship offers hands-on exposure to People Organization operations, instructional design, people analytics, and cross-functional project work. You will be part of a dynamic team (Talent Acquisition Optimization) that is at the forefront of driving large scale technology change for the Talent Acquisition function.


Key Responsibilities

The Intern will support multiple TA projects and will:

  • Partner with TA Leaders to define requirements, goals, and content for hiring manager experience initiatives
  • Partner with TA Leaders to outline key TA process points and expectations for recruiters
  • Assist in designing a comprehensive survey including question development, survey cadence, and delivery plan
  • Collaborate with analysts to build the survey infrastructure and reporting through tools such as SurveyMonkey
  • Support the development of dashboards and insights by partnering with the People Analytics team (e.g., PowerBI)
  • Gather information and create content for process guides, including workflow overviews, roles and responsibilities, and service-level expectations
  • Work with Learning & Development teams to transform content into visually appealing, easy-to-understand materials
  • Support communications planning and change management for rollout of new tools, resources, and processes
  • Contribute to clear, user-friendly outputs such as finalized guides and launched surveys, ensuring hiring managers have consistent and accessible resources

What You Will Learn

This internship provides hands-on learning in areas including

  • HR project and program management
  • Talent Acquisition processes
  • Survey design and analysis
  • People Analytics dashboards
  • Instructional design and content creation
  • Change management and communications
  • Cross-functional collaboration within HR

Preferred Qualifications :

  • Strong interest in Human Resources or Talent Acquisition
  • Excellent communication and writing skills
  • Proactive and strong initiative – see a need and support it
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through
  • Curiosity around emerging technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI)
  • Experience managing multiple priorities and projects in school, extra curriculars or past employment
  • Experience creating visual presentations. Solid proficiency in Microsoft Office tools
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment
  • Enrolled in an accredited US based University (working towards a Bachelor's degree) with an expected graduation date of December 2027 to Spring 2028

Remote Opportunity: Atlanta

Paid Internship: $20-22/hour

Start Date: 5/17/2027
End Date: 8/7/2027

Note: You must be work authorized in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future. The Company cannot offer employment to F-1 (student) visa holders who require employer sponsorship in the future or cannot work now on a full time basis.

Job.JobTitle: Business Development Underwriter - Dallas Metro Region
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $90,560 to $152,723 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Dallas, TX
  • Experience: 1+ year
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Business Development Underwriter for ICW Group's Dallas Metro region, responsible for underwriting, pricing, and managing a profitable book of business while building agency relationships and driving production. This remote/field role combines underwriting authority with business development and cross-sell responsibilities across Commercial Lines products.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree in business or related field, at least one year of underwriting or insurance experience, a current driver's license, and knowledge of commercial insurance products.

Full job description

Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop and manage a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while building and maintaining strong agency relationships and driving production results. Business Development Underwriters are assigned primary underwriting responsibility for specific line(s) of business (e.g., Workers' Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages). In addition, this role supports broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities and actively marketing all Company products in coordination with other underwriting partners. This role exists to ensure the Company achieves its underwriting profitability and distribution objectives through disciplined risk selection, pricing, and agency engagement.


Location: This is a remote/field role. Candidates ideally will reside in or near Dallas, Texas or the surrounding metro area or other nearby communities.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines
  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio
  • Evaluate risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history to determine acceptability
  • Apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, and underwriting judgment to achieve target returns
  • Accept or reject risks within delegated authority while ensuring alignment with underwriting guidelines and profitability objectives
  • Monitor book performance and take corrective action as needed
  • Utilize underwriting authority to effectively price and manage business within assigned line(s)
  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS) impacting assigned line(s) of business

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution
  • Develop, manage, and maintain a producer force capable of generating profitable business
  • Monitor production, quality, and profitability of assigned producers and hold producers accountable to expectations
  • Drive profitable sales of all Company products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions
  • Actively identify and pursue cross-sell opportunities across all Commercial Lines products, regardless of primary underwriting assignment
  • Promote all Company Commercial Lines offerings in agency interactions, supporting a total account approach
  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers aligned with Company strategy
  • Set, communicate, and monitor production expectations with agency partners
  • Maintain thorough knowledge of assigned territory, including production sources, competitor activity, and market trends
  • Identify opportunities for growth, new distribution, and market expansion and provide feedback to leadership

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary Company contact and representative for assigned and prospective producers
  • Build and maintain collaborative relationships through regular agency visits, meetings, and presentations
  • Provide underwriting and production support, including participation in account strategy and marketing discussions
  • Provide responsive, high-quality service to agents and insureds, resolving inquiries and coverage decisions promptly
  • Maintain consistent communication through in-person visits, calls, and Company technology
  • Present agency performance insights, opportunities, and agency management strategies to internal stakeholders and agency partners

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university with a major or emphasis in Business, Accounting, Statistics, or related field or equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum 1 year of related experience and/or training required.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver's license required.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong relationships with agents and brokers while delivering high-quality customer service
  • Ability to apply fundamental underwriting principles, concepts, and guidelines within assigned line(s) of business
  • Ability to evaluate and interpret submissions, financial information, loss control reports, and policy forms/endorsements
  • Working knowledge of commercial insurance products, including Workers' Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages (e.g., General Liability, Property, Commercial Auto, Inland Marine)
  • Ability to balance underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with business development, production, and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and relationship management skills
  • Ability to analyze risk, identify exposures, and make sound underwriting decisions aligned with Company objectives

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.
  • Role requires 40%-50% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.
  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.
  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • This position operates in a home office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier and other standard office equipment.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities.

The position may include other duties as assigned.

$90,559.93 - $152,723.07

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off

Job Description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Claims Specialist to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims


Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair, and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

Picture yourself building a successful career at AIG working alongside other talented, highly motivated individuals committed to reaching our goal of becoming the world's leading insurance provider. We believe that our success depends on building a world class team. If you would like to be a part of our team, we invite you to consider putting your talents to work with the AIG Claims department.


We are seeking an experienced Casualty Claims Adjuster to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and resolve Commercial Auto Liability and Commercial General Liability claims. The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in liability analysis, injury evaluation, coverage interpretation, and litigation management, with the ability to independently handle a moderate to complex caseload from initial notice through resolution. This role requires sound judgment, strong analytical skills, and the ability to balance customer service, financial stewardship, and technical claim expertise. The adjuster will work closely with insureds, claimants, attorneys, brokers, and internal business partners to deliver timely, fair, and compliant claim outcomes. You'll be responsible for:


Claim Investigation, Evaluation and Negotiation

  • Conduct prompt, thorough investigations to determine coverage, liability, damages, and compensability.
  • Gather and evaluate evidence, including statements, police reports, medical records, expert reports, and other relevant documentation.
  • Analyze coverage issues and prepare reservation of rights, denial, and other coverage correspondence as appropriate.
  • Evaluate bodily injury, property damage, and exposure-related claims to determine appropriate resolution strategies.
  • Independently negotiate settlements within established authority levels.
  • Develop and execute proactive claim resolution strategies that achieve timely and cost-effective outcomes.
  • Identify and mitigate claim exposure through effective investigation, evaluation, and negotiation.
  • Ensure accurate claim documentation supporting all decisions and actions taken throughout the life of the claim.

Litigation Management

  • Manage litigated files and coordinate with defense counsel to develop case strategies.
  • Review pleadings, discovery responses, deposition summaries, and legal evaluations.
  • Monitor litigation budgets and legal expenses to ensure efficient claim handling.
  • Participate in mediations, settlement conferences, and other dispute resolution proceedings as necessary.

Financial and Regulatory Stewardship

  • Establish and maintain accurate indemnity and expense reserves with documented rationale.
  • Continuously evaluate reserve adequacy throughout the life cycle of the claim.
  • Ensure compliance with company guidelines, statutory requirements, and regulatory standards across all applicable jurisdictions.
  • Maintain diary and workload management systems to effectively prioritize and resolve assigned inventory.

Customer and Stakeholder Management

  • Deliver exceptional customer service through professional, timely, and empathetic communication.
  • Build strong working relationships with insureds, brokers, claimants, attorneys, and internal stakeholders.
  • Communicate claim status, strategy, and exposure effectively to management and business partners.

What you'll need to succeed:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 4+ years of Commercial Auto Liability and/or Commercial General Liability claims handling experience.
  • Demonstrated experience handling bodily injury claims involving moderate to significant exposure.
  • Experience interpreting policy coverage and drafting coverage position letters, reservation of rights letters, and denial letters.
  • Experience managing both litigated and non-litigated claims.
  • Excellent analytical, investigative, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Active Property & Casualty Adjuster License preferred; must obtain required state licensing within six months of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Litigation management experience.
  • Multi-state claims handling experience.
  • Experience handling serious bodily injury claims.
  • Professional designations such as AIC, CPCU, ARM, or SCLA.
  • Prior experience with commercial insurance carriers handling middle-market or large commercial accounts.

Company Details

Operating from offices in New York, Atlanta and San Francisco, Berkley Specialty Property is a recently established underwriting platform that writes a nationwide portfolio of specialty property business across a broad range of occupancy classes.

Responsibilities

Assistant Vice President, Underwriting - Builders Risk & Construction

Shape the future of complex construction risk while driving profitable growth.

Berkley Specialty Property is seeking an experienced and relationship-driven Assistant Vice President, Underwriting to join our Engineering & Construction team. This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic underwriter with deep Builders Risk expertise to play a key role in expanding a high-performing portfolio while partnering with brokers, clients, and colleagues across our global platform.

In this role, you will lead the underwriting and management of both new and renewal business, evaluating complex risks, crafting tailored solutions, and making sound underwriting decisions that balance growth with profitability. You'll have a direct impact on the development and execution of our Engineering & Construction underwriting strategy while building strong market relationships nationwide.

What You'll Do

  • Underwrite and manage a portfolio of project-specific Builders Risk and Construction All Risks business across the United States.
  • Assess exposures, determine pricing, analyze coverage, and structure profitable insurance solutions.
  • Develop and strengthen relationships with retail and wholesale broker partners.
  • Contribute to the growth and evolution of the Engineering & Construction portfolio through disciplined underwriting and market insight.
  • Collaborate closely with underwriting, actuarial, claims, and portfolio management teams in London to support consistent, profitable growth across the broader platform.
  • Monitor portfolio performance and apply sound judgment to manage risk while identifying new business opportunities.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

We're seeking a motivated underwriting professional who combines technical expertise with strong market relationships and a commercial mindset.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 5+ years of Builders Risk and/or Construction Property underwriting experience.
  • Established broker relationships within the retail and/or wholesale market.
  • Strong knowledge of construction and engineering risks, policy coverages, and underwriting principles.
  • Proven track record of underwriting profitability and effective risk selection.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex risks and make informed, business-focused decisions.
  • Exceptional communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing multiple priorities.
  • Self-starter who works independently, takes initiative, and collaborates effectively across teams.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent industry experience.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to join a growing specialty platform where your expertise, relationships, and underwriting judgment will directly influence business results. You'll work alongside highly respected industry professionals, gain exposure to complex and challenging risks, and help shape the future direction of a nationally focused Builders Risk portfolio.

If you're passionate about construction underwriting, value strong broker partnerships, and are ready to make a meaningful impact, we'd love to hear from you.

The Workers' Compensation Claims Specialist manages within company best practices lower-level, non-complex and non-problematic workers' compensation claims within delegated limited authority to best possible outcome, under the direct supervision of a senior claims professional, supporting the goals of claims department and of CorVel.

This is a remote position.

  • Establishes reserves and authorizes payments within reserving authority limits

  • Communicates claim status with the customer, claimant and client
  • Adheres to client and carrier guidelines and participates in claims review as needed
  • Assists other claims professionals with more complex or problematic claims as necessary

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location. Pay rates are established taking into account the following factors: federal, state, and local minimum wage requirements, the geographic location differential, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, internal employee equity, and market conditions. Our ranges may be modified at any time.

ABOUT CORVEL:

CorVel, a certified Great Place to Work® Company, is a national provider of industry-leading risk management solutions for the workers' compensation, auto, health and disability management industries. CorVel was founded in 1987 and has been publicly traded on the NASDAQ stock exchange since 1991. Our continual investment in human capital and technology enable us to deliver the most innovative and integrated solutions to our clients.   • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders' residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days.

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

We are seeking an experienced attorney with experience handling habitability, landlord-tenant, and HOA matters to join our Southern California staff counsel team! Our attorneys work from home and handle in-person appearances and trials as required. We offer developmental opportunities, and a comprehensive benefits package including annual bonus potential up to 20% of the salary, generous 401k, auto allowance, PTO, medical/dental/vision, paid parental leave, and much more all without the stress of billable hours!

Job Summary

This position is responsible for representing clients in all areas of insurance defense practice, handling cases that are primarily moderate to high complexity and exposure and/or involve unique insurance defense issues. Manages all phases of cases from intake to resolution.

Essential Job Functions

  • Litigates moderate to high complexity and exposure cases and/or cases involving unique legal or procedural issues and performs duties necessary from intake to trial and/or settlement. This includes but is not limited to preparation of pleadings, motions, discovery, and briefs.
  • Acts as the lead attorney at hearings, conferences, interviews, mediations, arbitrations, and/or trials.
  • Develops strategies and arguments to thoroughly prepare for trial.
  • Utilizes knowledge of legal precedents to analyze the probable outcomes of a case.
  • Identifies the strengths and weaknesses of approaches to a case.
  • Performs or ensures completion of any other tasks or duties necessary for the proper representation of clients.
  • Consults with Claims Executive team and renders legal strategy recommendations regarding the legal aspects of the handling of personal injury claims.
  • Provides guidance to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards.
  • Interprets applicable industry laws, rulings and regulations.
  • Functionally supervises attorneys who are assisting in the handling of cases as development opportunities.
  • Provides guidance and mentorship with the autonomy to learn.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice Law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Seven years of litigation experience required. Insurance defense, personal injury, and/or jury trial experience required. First and second chair trial experience in bodily injury litigation strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Special Skill Requirement

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Additional Qualification

Effective leadership skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to command the attention of an audience. Demonstrated problem solving skills. Possesses a genuine interest in the defense of Insurance regulations. Ability to represent the company with external constituents. Handles conflict effectively with the ability to quickly interpret and respond to new information. Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills. Ability to work within tight timeframes and meet strict deadlines. Excellent time management and priority setting skills. Articulate and responsive to colleagues. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Adept and proficient at using technology to maximize efficiency in virtual, paperless environment.

Full job description

Job Summary

Workplace: MEXICO - Remote ( #LI-Remote )

We are looking for a Predictive Analytics Manager to join a newly established, high-impact team focused on transforming enterprise decision-making. This team is at the forefront of delivering timely, accurate, and forward-looking financial and operational insights by combining advanced analytics, actuarial concepts, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities.

In this role, you will help build predictive analytics capabilities from the ground up in a fast-paced, “startup-like” environment within a large organization. You will play a key role in designing and implementing data-driven solutions that drive profitable growth, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen business intelligence across the enterprise.

This is an excellent opportunity for a data-driven professional who enjoys autonomy, thrives in ambiguous environments, and wants to influence how analytics is built and scaled.

Requirements

  • Years of experience in predictive analytics, data science, or related field
  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, or related field
  • Professional experience in insurance or pricing analytics is a strong plus
  • Strong experience with:
  • Python, R, and SQL
  • Experience with SAS is a plus
  • Advanced knowledge of:
    • Predictive modeling and machine learning techniques
    • Statistical analysis and data mining
    • Data preparation and feature engineering
  • Strong understanding of data ecosystems and ability to navigate complex data environments
  • Ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present analytical findings to diverse audiences
  • Problem-solving mindset with the ability to work independently in a fast-evolving environment
  • Experience contributing to or building analytics capabilities from scratch is highly valued
  • Collaborative and proactive approach, with a willingness to share knowledge and mentor others
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams in data-driven environments

Essential Job Functions

  • Develop and implement predictive models using advanced statistical and machine learning techniques (e.g., regression, clustering, decision trees, neural networks)
  • Build and maintain programs for predictor and response variables, ensuring model accuracy and scalability
  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand needs, translate them into analytical solutions, and communicate actionable insights clearly
  • Present analytical findings to non-technical audiences, explaining methodologies, data sources, and business impact
  • Explore, prepare, and structure large datasets (internal and external) to support model development and enhancement
  • Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of modeling frameworks, processes, and best practices
  • Ensure data quality and model integrity through rigorous validation and review processes
  • Develop a strong understanding of the data landscape, including sourcing, mapping, and integrating data across systems
  • Support enterprise data initiatives (e.g., data migration and transformation programs)
  • Collaborate with and mentor junior analysts, sharing knowledge and promoting best practices
  • Stay current on industry trends, particularly within insurance analytics and predictive modeling

Benefits

This position offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and work–life balance. Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

The Specialty Operations Senior Consultant plays a critical role in shaping successful outcomes for highly complex reinsurance claims. In this position, you will lead the resolution and settlement of high exposure assumed reinsurance mattersincluding asbestos, pharmaceutical, toxic tort, environmental, sexual abuse and molestation, and other mass tort claims.
You will join a collaborative and knowledgeable Specialty Operations team where independent judgment, analytical skill, and strategic decision making are valued. This is an opportunity to influence meaningful outcomes, work with challenging and evolving legal issues, and contribute to our continued success within a highly specialized claims environment

Key Responsibilities:


Independently manage a portfolio of complex reinsurance claims involving asbestos, environmental, and other latent injury exposuresanalyzing liability, damages, and contractual obligations to drive informed and strategic claim outcomes.

Interpret and apply facultative and treaty reinsurance contracts, as well as CGL, umbrella, and excess policies, to determine coverage, using underlying facts and relevant case law.
Establish accurate case reserves, leveraging cedent reporting, internal assessment, and designated authority levels; seek management approval for exposures exceeding authority.
Develop and execute action plans for the evaluation, negotiation, and resolution of reported claims.
Maintain thorough and timely documentation, ensuring claim files reflect clear reasoning, compliance with internal guidelines, and proactive communication with management.
Stay current on emerging legal trends, industry developments, and significant case law, applying this knowledge to enhance claims strategy and decisionmaking.
Serve as a corporate witness or representative in litigation, arbitration, and other disputeresolution settings when required.

This position does not include supervisory responsibilities.


Preferred Qualifications


Experience:

5+ years of relevant experience preferred; 3+ years will be considered for strong candidates with demonstrated capability.


Functional Skills

Strong knowledge of reinsurance contracts, insurance coverage principles, claim processes, and relevant case law. This role focuses on Property & Casualty reinsurance.
Proven experience evaluating and resolving complex bodily injury and property damage reinsurance claims involving masstort exposures.
Ability to collaborate effectively in both virtual and inperson settings with internal teams, management, external cedents, and brokers.
Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, and Copilot; aptitude for learning new technology and claims systems.
Exceptional written communication skills with the ability to produce clear, concise, and wellreasoned documentation.

Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Join the legal frontline and champion the defense for both the insured and the Company! As a Senior Trial Attorney, you'll handle bodily injury, property damage lawsuits, and more, with mediations, arbitrations, and occasional trials. Beyond the courtroom, you'll provide vital counsel to business clients and coordinate between legal teams. Stay ahead of the game by monitoring new laws and regulations, ensuring our strategies remain sharp. Embrace the excitement of constant challenges and victories in this dynamic role!

Applicants must be licensed to practice in the state of California

Applicants can reside in the following states: CA, WA, AZ, NV, OR


This position is eligible for a $10,000 sign-on bonus, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Represents insured individuals and the Company in the defense of bodily injury and property damage lawsuits, subrogation, and Allstate Financial cases.
  • Prepares thoroughly for and conducts hearings, trials, arbitrations, mediations, and depositions.
  • Prepares and presents pre- and post-trial motions effectively.
  • Assists colleagues in resolving calendar conflicts in a collaborative manner.
  • Offers counsel to business clients on day-to-day legal matters.
  • Manages projects efficiently, fostering coordination and collaboration among legal teams.
  • Keeps abreast of and evaluates new laws, regulations, and case law; identifies and summarizes relevant issues; collaborates with other areas of the Law and Regulation (L&R) department; provides proactive advice and counsel to business units on the impact of new laws; monitors legal representation.

Education

  • Juris Doctorate and active membership in good standing with the California State Bar required.

Minimum Requirements

  • 4+ years of proven litigation experience or strong litigation-type skills, such as case strategy development, legal research, and advocacy, with the ability to manage complex disputes and work effectively under pressure.
  • First or second chair jury trial experience
  • Proven experience with insurance defense is preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, LexisNexis, and internet research.
  • Strong teamwork skills, able to collaborate effectively with attorneys, paralegals, and administrative assistants under the guidance of Lead Counsel.
  • Capacity to manage a substantial case load.

Job.JobTitle: Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster - Remote - PST/MST/CST
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster your focus will be investigating automobile accidents involving single or multiple vehicles, which result in property damage and bodily injury with attorney/litigation involved. You will have the convenience of working remotely from your home while efficiently handling your responsibilities. You will assess coverage, liability, and damages while providing exceptional customer service throughout your day. Customer and attorney communication will take place through different channels, including voice calls, email, and text messages. Through the utilization of innovative platforms and tools, you will engage in negotiation processes to reach fair injury settlements with all parties involved.

In this role, candidates must demonstrate a high level of adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced and continuously evolving environment. Success requires the ability to manage multiple, diverse venues simultaneously, each with its own unique operational demands and stakeholder expectations.

As the claim owner, you are the primary point of contact for the customer for their claim. While otherssuch as field adjusters or repair shopsmay assist with the claim, the insured will look to you for guidance throughout the process.

Excellent customer service is essential. For many customers, this may be their first experience filing a claim. It's your responsibility to support them through what can be a stressful situation by providing clear communication and empathetic guidance.

Additionally, the role involves close collaboration with internal partners to assess and drive value across initiatives. This cross-functional engagement is key to aligning strategic goals and delivering impactful outcomes.

Candidates for this role must reside in the Pacific, Mountain or Central time zones. This position is not available to residents of California, Washington, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico.

The work schedule varies depending on your local time zone:

  • Pacific Time Zone: Monday-Friday, 8:00am - 5:00pm PST
  • Mountain Time Zones: MondayFriday, 8:00am 5:00pm MST
  • Central Time Zones: MondayFriday, 8:00am 5:00pm CST

The first approximately 6-9 weeks of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.

Allstate Benefits

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, youll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:

The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each casualty claim. You lead with empathy, always.

The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate casualty claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.

The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and text with customers and others to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a

specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.

  • Proficient communication skills, especially over the phone, to establish rapport and assess claims accurately.
  • Ability to work independently and remotely, while managing time efficiently.

Quick facts

About this job

Senior Trial Attorney representing insured individuals and Allstate in bodily injury, property damage, and subrogation lawsuits. Role includes trials, arbitrations, mediations, depositions, and counsel to business clients on legal matters.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of litigation experience, first or second chair jury trial experience, and are licensed to practice in California.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Join the legal frontline and champion the defense for both the insured and the Company! As a Senior Trial Attorney, you'll handle bodily injury, property damage lawsuits, and more, with mediations, arbitrations, and occasional trials. Beyond the courtroom, you'll provide vital counsel to business clients and coordinate between legal teams. Stay ahead of the game by monitoring new laws and regulations, ensuring our strategies remain sharp. Embrace the excitement of constant challenges and victories in this dynamic role!

Applicants must be licensed to practice in the state of California

Applicants must reside in the following states: CA, WA, AZ, NV, OR

This position is eligible for a $10,000 sign-on bonus, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Represents insured individuals and the Company in the defense of bodily injury and property damage lawsuits, subrogation, and Allstate Financial cases.
  • Prepares thoroughly for and conducts hearings, trials, arbitrations, mediations, and depositions.
  • Prepares and presents pre- and post-trial motions effectively.
  • Assists colleagues in resolving calendar conflicts in a collaborative manner.
  • Offers counsel to business clients on day-to-day legal matters.
  • Manages projects efficiently, fostering coordination and collaboration among legal teams.
  • Keeps abreast of and evaluates new laws, regulations, and case law; identifies and summarizes relevant issues; collaborates with other areas of the Law and Regulation (L&R) department; provides proactive advice and counsel to business units on the impact of new laws; monitors legal representation.

Education

  • Juris Doctorate and active membership in good standing with the California State Bar required.

Minimum Requirements

  • 4+ years of proven litigation experience or strong litigation-type skills, such as case strategy development, legal research, and advocacy, with the ability to manage complex disputes and work effectively under pressure.
  • First or second chair jury trial experience
  • Proven experience with insurance defense is preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, LexisNexis, and internet research.
  • Strong teamwork skills, able to collaborate effectively with attorneys, paralegals, and administrative assistants under the guidance of Lead Counsel.
  • Capacity to manage a substantial case load.
  • Comfortable working in a remote environment and willing to travel throughout California for trials & court appearances on an as needed basis.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Trial Attorney, Remote (Sacramento / San Francisco, CA)
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Los Angeles, CA
  • Experience: 4+ years

About this job

Senior Trial Attorney handling bodily injury and property damage lawsuits for Allstate, including mediations, arbitrations, and trials. Role involves trial work, legal counsel to business clients, and monitoring regulatory changes.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of litigation experience, first or second chair jury trial experience, and are licensed to practice in California.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Join the legal frontline and champion the defense for both the insured and the Company! As a Senior Trial Attorney, you'll handle bodily injury, property damage lawsuits, and more, with mediations, arbitrations, and occasional trials. Beyond the courtroom, you'll provide vital counsel to business clients and coordinate between legal teams. Stay ahead of the game by monitoring new laws and regulations, ensuring our strategies remain sharp. Embrace the excitement of constant challenges and victories in this dynamic role!

Applicants must be licensed to practice in the state of California

Applicants must reside in the following states: CA, WA, AZ, NV, OR

This position is eligible for a $10,000 sign-on bonus, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Represents insured individuals and the Company in the defense of bodily injury and property damage lawsuits, subrogation, and Allstate Financial cases.
  • Prepares thoroughly for and conducts hearings, trials, arbitrations, mediations, and depositions.
  • Prepares and presents pre- and post-trial motions effectively.
  • Assists colleagues in resolving calendar conflicts in a collaborative manner.
  • Offers counsel to business clients on day-to-day legal matters.
  • Manages projects efficiently, fostering coordination and collaboration among legal teams.
  • Keeps abreast of and evaluates new laws, regulations, and case law; identifies and summarizes relevant issues; collaborates with other areas of the Law and Regulation (L&R) department; provides proactive advice and counsel to business units on the impact of new laws; monitors legal representation.

Education

  • Juris Doctorate and active membership in good standing with the California State Bar required.

Minimum Requirements

  • 4+ years of proven litigation experience or strong litigation-type skills, such as case strategy development, legal research, and advocacy, with the ability to manage complex disputes and work effectively under pressure.
  • First or second chair jury trial experience
  • Proven experience with insurance defense is preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, LexisNexis, and internet research.
  • Strong teamwork skills, able to collaborate effectively with attorneys, paralegals, and administrative assistants under the guidance of Lead Counsel.
  • Capacity to manage a substantial case load.
  • Comfortable working in a remote environment and willing to travel throughout California for trials & court appearances on an as needed basis.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. Job Description

The Software Engineer Senior Manager is the direct leader of more critical groups with significant responsibilities. These groups may sometimes be more heavily resourced with more senior staff or more staff in general or be responsible for more technically complex or strategically important parts of the architecture or product. Software Engineer Senior Manager are expected to build relationships throughout the organization to ensure whole-company alignment and support for their goals, and vice-versa. The Software Engineer Senior Manager architects and designs their digital products using modern tools, technologies, frameworks, and systems. They apply a systematic application of scientific and technological knowledge, methods, and experience to the design, implementation, testing, and documentation of software. They own and manage running their application in production, and ultimately becomes accountable for the success of their digital products through achieving KPIs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Frequently advise others on complex engineering matters

  • Build foundation to translate strategy into challenging and meaningful goals

  • Manage teams that are responsible for strategic and critical pieces of architecture or provide functions that are of key strategic value to the business

  • Act as an authority in software best practices and be relied upon to propagate these in the broader organization, beyond their individual team

  • Expert ability to view the organization as a whole

  • Leverage and influence key stakeholders

Experience

  • 10 or more years of experience Java and Cobol

  • Experience and knowledge in developing REST APIs using Java Spring boot, including tooling for documentation (swagger, REST-docs, OpenAPI spec), versioning, service discovery/registration, testing and management; experience using API gateways a plus.

  • Experience and knowledge in web and API security including authentication, authorization, OAuth, OWASP, OpenID, and SAML.

  • Experience in backend development design and implementation, database (MongoDB, caching) and Kafka messaging.

  • Knowledge and experience using distributed version control systems (git), artifact management systems, build and packaging systems (maven, gradle, npm, artifactory, etc ) and Jenkins or similar Continuous Integration tools .

  • Experience of working in an Agile environment or paired programming/engineering model.

  • Experience with Python is a plus..

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job has supervisory duties of up to 5 people

National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

The Direct Sales Agent Specialist is responsible for driving profitable growth by generating new business, cross-selling existing customers, and building lasting relationships. This role focuses on understanding customer needs, delivering tailored solutions, and maintaining a strong book of business.

This role sells to local customers both in person and over the phone, while driving growth through community involvement, relationship building, and outside marketing efforts.

If you are ready to start working in a fun & exciting environment while making a difference, then apply to join our team today!

As a Direct Sales Agent Specialist, you will:

  • Achieve sales goals through new business, cross-sell, and retention
  • Build and maintain a consistent pipeline, including local lead generation and referrals
  • Develop relationships within the community (e.g., dealerships, events, local partners) to support business growth
  • Conduct outbound prospecting and follow-ups to convert opportunities into sales
  • Partner with leadership to support sales and local marketing initiatives
  • Stay informed on products, underwriting guidelines, and market competition
  • Deliver results aligned with performance standards, compliance requirements, and customer experience expectations

What makes Direct Auto Insurance unique?

  • Ability to sell a multitude of industry-leading products through retail stores and phone
  • Entrepreneurial, performance-based, and results-focused culture

Job.JobTitle: Litigation Attorney - Special Investigations Unit (Remote - New York)
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: New York, NY

About this job

Litigation attorney role at Allstate's Special Investigations Unit handling insurance fraud cases, including RICO-based affirmative actions. Remote position in New York requiring 4+ years of litigation experience and active New York State Bar membership.

Good fit if you have 4+ years of litigation experience, New York State Bar membership, and federal court admission or ability to seek it.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Join the legal frontline and put your litigation and investigative skills to work protecting The Allstate Company against insurance fraud. The ideal candidate for this role will have a passion for combatting fraud against the insurance industry. In this role, you will utilize your litigation and investigative experience to help defend the company against medical and other types of fraud. The successful candidate will be responsible for bringing affirmative actions, including RICO-based litigation, on behalf of the Company. You will apply your well-developed legal writing skills and negotiate a variety of complex matters within the state of New York. This role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact by pursuing innovative legal strategies and helping protect the Company from fraudulent activity.

Key Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with the Claims/Special Investigation Unit (SIU) to combat fraudulent claims in No-Fault and other cases.

  • Research, prepare, file, and litigate fraud cases, including RICO and other Affirmative Actions.

  • Develop litigation strategies on legal matters.

  • Review case files and plan resolutions.

  • Draft discovery requests, motions, memorandums, and legal briefs.

  • Prepare for and conduct Depositions and Examinations Under Oath (EUOs).

  • Attend arbitrations, mediations, and trials.

  • Work with expert witnesses in the preparation of, or defense of litigation.

  • Represent the company in court appearances (conferences, hearings) in State and Federal courts.

  • Draft pre-trial and post-trial motions.

  • Negotiate settlements and prepare related documentation.

Education and Licensing

  • Juris Doctorate and active membership in good standing with the New York State Bar

  • Federal Court Admission or the ability to seek admission upon selection for this role

Experience

  • 4 or more years of experience

  • Ability to manage and oversee intermediate-level litigation matters.

  • Legal research and writing skills

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office and related computer applications

  • Exercises discretion and maintains confidentiality

  • Demonstrates ethics and integrity

  • Knowledge of legal holds and discovery processes

  • A team player who enjoys collaborating with colleagues on a daily basis

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job does not have supervisory duties

Explore the Benefits of Joining Allstate's Client Legal Services:

    • Exceptional Work-Life Balance:At Allstate, we understand the importance of achieving harmony between work and personal life. Our in-house litigation roles provide more predictable schedules and flexibility, allowing you to excel professionally while enjoying a fulfilling personal life.

    • Holistic Understanding of the Business:As part of the Allstate legal team, you'll gain invaluable insight into our diverse business operations, objectives, and culture. This comprehensive understanding enables you to align legal strategies closely with the company's goals, fostering impactful contributions and strategic partnerships across departments.

    • Direct Client Collaboration:Working in-house at Allstate means collaborating directly with internal stakeholders and business units. This close partnership cultivates deeper client relationships, facilitating a nuanced understanding of their needs and priorities. By providing proactive legal guidance and support, you'll play a pivotal role in driving the company's success.

    • Strategic Influence and Impact:As an integral member of our legal team, you'll have the opportunity to shape strategic decisions and risk management initiatives. Your insights and expertise will inform key business decisions, empowering you to mitigate risks effectively and drive positive outcomes that directly impact Allstate's bottom line.

    • Diverse Legal Challenges:In-house litigation roles at Allstate encompass a broad spectrum of legal work beyond traditional litigation, including regulatory compliance, risk assessment, and dispute resolution. This diversity of challenges ensures continuous professional growth and development, expanding your skill set and enhancing your career trajectory.

    • Professional Growth Opportunities:With ample opportunities for advancement and professional development, you'll have the support and resources you need to reach new heights in your legal career.

#LI-PC1

Skills

Cross-Team Collaboration, Defense Litigation, Insurance, Insurance Defense, Investigative Skills, Legal Document Preparation, Legal Investigation, Legal Research, Legal Writing, Litigation, Litigation Strategy, Microsoft Windows Office, Researching, Team Collaboration, Time Management, Torts

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is $130,000 - 158,000 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Quick facts

  • Pay: $65,400 to $108,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Greensboro, NC
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • License: Valid driver's license
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

About this job

Inspect damaged vehicles, estimate repair costs, and settle claims for Travelers Insurance. This remote-based role requires technical expertise in vehicle damage assessment and strong customer service skills while working with repair facilities and customers.

Good fit if you have two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience, an active adjuster license, and a valid driver's license.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$65,400.00 - $108,000.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Outside Auto Appraiser, you are responsible for physically inspecting damaged vehicles, estimating repair costs, working closely with repair facilities, and determining and settling the actual cash value of total loss vehicles to ensure accurate and timely claim settlements. In this customer-facing role, you will need to have a high level of technical expertise in vehicle damage assessment, strong customer service skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment. This position will serve as a technical resource for auto claim staff and will provide advice and direction to claim professionals on claim damages to achieve optimal outcomes. This position is based remotely with work at residential and/or commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office.

What Will You Do?

  • Inspect and assess vehicle damage resulting from accidents, weather events, or other covered losses by conducting thorough virtual or on-site inspections at body shops or customer locations.
  • Perform estimate review work, conduct virtual inspections, and collaborate with repair facilities to ensure accuracy, consistency, and quality across claims.
  • Prepare accurate repair estimates using industry-standard estimating software to determine the cost of parts, labor, and materials required to restore vehicles to pre-loss condition.
  • Evaluate and settle vehicle total losses by determining actual cash value (ACV) through market research, comparable vehicle analysis, and application of appropriate valuation tools and methodologies.
  • Negotiate repair costs and settlements with body shops, customers, and third-party claimants to reach fair and timely resolutions while maintaining quality repair standards.
  • Identify and document pre-existing damage, prior repairs, and potential fraud indicators to ensure accurate claim evaluation and protect company interests.
  • Collaborate with claim representatives, body shops, and vendors to coordinate repairs, authorize supplements, and resolve coverage or repair-related issues.
  • Provide exceptional customer service by explaining the appraisal process, answering questions, assisting in moving claims towards timely resolution, and keeping vehicle owners informed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Active adjuster license, where applicable.
  • Two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience.
  • Proficient in claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers throughout the claim process.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated conflict resolution skills; ability to facilitate productive discussions and reach equitable outcomes.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations and claim handling requirements.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • One year of auto physical damage appraisal or comparable claim related experience or successful completion of required Travelers Claim Representative training program.
  • Valid driver's license.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.
