Job.JobTitle: VP, Operational Excellence - Investment Operations - Liberty Mutual Investments
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 10+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

VP of Operational Excellence for Liberty Mutual Investments' Investment Operations function, a newly created role focused on assessing and strengthening operational health across seven operating teams. Responsibilities include designing risk and control self-assessments, testing control effectiveness, identifying gaps, owning operational metrics and reporting, and partnering with transformation teams to drive durable fixes.

Good fit if you have experience in operations and controls, understand operational risk assessment, and can influence peer teams without direct authority.

Full job description


Description

The Company

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is the investment firm for Liberty Mutual Group (Liberty) andis responsible forpowering Libertys strategy amid profound change in global capital markets. With deep expertise in fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies,LMI invests $120+ billion (as of 12/31/2025) of capital globally,taking a long-term approach across its integrated platform and has a team of over 350 investment, finance, and operations professionals located in Boston, MA, and New York, NY.

LMI has a clear purpose: build enduring businesses side-by-side with our partners, drive economic growth, and generate superior risk-adjusted returns that power Libertys strategy and secure its promises.Weoffer the best of both worlds the look and feel of a boutique investment firm with the reputation and financial strength of a global leader. As the investment firm of a mutual with long-term capital, LMI has a single client mandate. This gives us the freedom to focus on what we do best.

Our portfolio spans a broad spectrum of public and private investments, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and our toolkit in support of our mission. We invest across diverse asset classes, financial structures, and industries, including real estate, digital infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy, and technologywith the aim of creating value and powering innovation. We pride ourselves on our extensive network of mutually beneficial partnerships, and we use our substantial influence, capital, and energy to drive towards a better future.#LMI #LI-LMI

The Position

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is seeking an experienced operations and controls professional to join our Investment Operations function as Vice President, Operational Excellence. This is a newly created, high-impact role purpose-built to assess and strengthen the health of daily operations across the full investment operations platform.

This role serves as the functions first-line lead for operational health responsible for evaluating operational risk, testing the effectiveness of the controls designed to mitigate that risk, identifying process and control gaps, and driving their remediation to closure across all operating teams: Treasury Services, Cash & Trade Operations, Derivatives Operations, Loan Operations, Alternatives Operations, Shared Services, and Investment Accounting Operations. The role reports to the Head of Investment Accounting Operations, with its function-wide mandate sponsored by the Head of Operational Strategy & Delivery.

Beyond assessment, the role owns the operational KPI and metrics framework and the operational-health reporting that informs functional governance, and partners closely with Strategy & Executions Transformation team to convert findings into durable, delivered fixes.

This is a first-line operational-excellence role embedded in the business; it coordinates with and is distinct from second-line Risk and Internal Audit, and does not provide independent assurance. The ideal candidate is a skilled collaborator who understands the downstream impact of operational decisions and can influence peer teams without direct authority. This is a high-impact individual contributor role with the opportunity to grow into a people management capacity as the function scales.

Key Responsibilities

  • Operational Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA)
    • Design and run a recurring, first-line risk and control self-assessment across all seven operating teams, producing a current-state view of where daily execution is fragile
    • Maintain a living map of operational risks, the controls intended to mitigate them, and the residual risk that remains after those controls
    • Bring an industry-aware lens to what strong operational controls look like across asset classes and lifecycle stages
  • Control Effectiveness & Gap Remediation
    • Test whether controls are operating as designed
    • Identify process and control gaps, prioritize them at the function level based on risk, and own them through to closure
    • Trace the upstream root causes of downstream breaks and not-in-good-order conditions, championing systemic, durable fixes over one-off corrections
    • Document assessment evidence
  • Metrics, KPIs & Operational-Health Reporting
    • Own the operational KPI framework and the run-state operational-health reporting that feeds functional governance forums
    • Translate operational data into a clear, decision-ready view of functional health for senior leadership
    • Align metrics and definitions consistently across teams and systems of record
  • Transformation & Product Partnership
    • Serve as the demand-side partner to Strategy & Executions Transformation team, converting diagnosed gaps into a prioritized remediation backlog
    • Coordinate with Product Owners to ensure product backlogs reflect operations requirements and priorities
    • Ensure delivered solutions close the underlying operational risk rather than addressing symptoms
    • Identify and advance automation and process-improvement opportunities, including practical application of AI tooling
  • Governance, Escalation & Second-Line Coordination
    • Run the operational-health governance routine (chaired and sponsored by the Head of OS&D), presenting current-state assessment, open gaps, and remediation status with items assigned to process owners and dates
    • Proactively raise operational risks, process concerns, and stakeholder impacts in a constructive, solutions-oriented manner
    • Coordinate with second-line Risk and Internal Audit to align scope and avoid duplication of assurance activity
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Partner Performance
    • Serve as a trusted operational partner and subject-matter expert across investment, accounting, technology, data, and treasury teams
    • Assess the operational performance of external service providers through a risk-and-control lens
    • Communicate process changes, improvement initiatives, and strategic priorities clearly to senior stakeholders
Qualifications
  • Education
    • Bachelors degree in finance, Business, Accounting, or a related field
    • Advanced degree (e.g., MBA) a plus
    • Relevant risk/controls or process-improvement certifications (e.g., Lean Six Sigma) preferred but not required
  • 10+ years of experience in investment operations, financial operations, or operational risk and controls, ideally within an asset manager, insurer, alternative investment firm, or comparable institutional investment platform
  • Demonstrated experience in operational risk assessment, control design and effectiveness testing, or RCSA-type programs
  • Strong understanding of the investment operations lifecycle across multiple asset classes including loans, derivatives, alternatives, and cash/treasury
  • Experience defining and operating metrics and KPIs and translating operational data into governance-ready reporting
  • Familiarity with loan administration and accounting systems, IBOR and ABOR environments, and how data flows across a multi-system operations infrastructure
  • Highly effective collaborator with proven experience influencing peer teams without direct authority in a matrixed organization; able to raise risks and represent stakeholder perspectives in a constructive, solutions-oriented manner
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impact for our business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

We value your hard work, integrity and commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit: https://www.libertymutualgroup.com/about-lm/careers/benefits

Job.JobTitle: Claim Professional Development Program Internship (CPDP Intern)
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $25.00 to $26.00 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Diamond Bar, CA

About this job

Internship in insurance claims at Travelers in Diamond Bar, California. Gain hands-on training in claims investigation, damage estimation, and coverage determination through structured onboarding, mentorship, and ride-alongs with experienced claim professionals.

Good fit if you are pursuing or have a Bachelor's degree, prefer business-related studies, and are authorized to work in the U.S.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards. 

Salary Range

$25.00 - $26.00

Target Openings

2

What Is the Opportunity?

Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT for this role. The Travelers Claim Intern program provides qualified candidates an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand business experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, contact clients, determine coverage, scoping of losses and completing damage estimates. We are seeking applicants who are interested about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making Claim their future career choice. Housing assistance is not provided.

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

What Will You Do?

  • Structured onboarding to Travelers systems and protocols.
  • Exposure to Personal and Business Insurance claims of basic to moderate complexity.
  • Learn and understand effective strategies for investigating, negotiating and resolving claims thoroughly, accurately and efficiently.
  • Develop knowledge of what happened, estimating damage, determining what coverages apply and helping our customers through the process through strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Observe the work of the Claim Professional through desk and 'ride-alongs' with experienced employees.

Position Summary

Supervises, trains, and monitors the activities of assigned claims adjusters and other claims personnel. Assists the Claims Leadership in the overseeing and handling of claims.

    • This position will report to Wisconsin branch office
    • This position will be supervising Field Property Adjusters in the Milwaukee area.

Duties and Responsibilities

Reviews claim correspondence and provides counsel on further action.

This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Additional Experience

Job.JobDescription:
The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth.


Are you curious about what drives employee engagement, workplace culture, and organizational success?

At Assurant, our greatest asset is our people and our culture is a distinct competitive advantage. This is more than a traditional HR internship. You'll contribute to projects that strengthen business outcomes through influencing culture, improving employee experiences, and proactively identifying and mitigating organizational risks. Along the way, you'll develop valuable skills in employee relations, workforce analytics, problem solving, stakeholder management, and strategic thinking.


At Assurant, we're transforming the way work gets done by harnessing innovative thinking, the power of AI, automation, and data-driven insights while leveraging the unique skills of our people to deliver the greatest value in the moments that matter most.


As an intern, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Work on meaningful projects focused on driving our culture and continually improving the support and experiences of our employees and leaders
  • Gain exposure to Employee Relations and HR People Partner teams
  • Analyze employee feedback and workforce data to uncover insights
  • Collaborate with experienced HR professionals and business leaders
  • Help improve processes, resources, and experiences
  • Explore emerging HR technologies, digital enablement, and AI-powered solutions
  • Present recommendations and ideas that can influence real business outcomes

You'll leave with practical experience, professional connections, and a deeper understanding of how leading organizations create great employee experiences while delivering business results.


What You'll Do

Employee Experience & Workforce Insights

  • Analyze engagement survey results, employee feedback, and workforce trends to identify themes, root causes, and opportunities.
  • Help develop presentations, dashboards, reports, and executive-ready summaries that communicate insights and recommendations.
  • Summarize survey comments and feedback trends to support People Partner priorities and action planning.
  • Research employee experience and workplace trends to inform team initiatives.

Special Projects & Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Partner with People Partners and cross-functional stakeholders on strategic and operational priorities.
  • Gather stakeholder feedback and analyze findings to identify opportunities for process improvement and stronger employee experiences.
  • Conduct research and benchmarking, then translate findings into practical recommendations.
  • Support presentations, communications, project materials, and leadership updates.
  • Bring a fresh perspective by challenging assumptions, identifying new ideas, and recommending innovative approaches.
  • Contribute to projects focused on employee relations, organizational effectiveness, digital enablement, employee experience, and continuous improvement.

Performance Management & Employee Relations Support

  • Support review of performance improvement and termination documentation for completeness, consistency, and alignment with company practices, while identifying items requiring additional People Partner review.
  • Help identify recurring documentation themes and opportunities to improve consistency and effectiveness.
  • Support maintenance of templates, resources, and job aids used by the People Partner team.
  • Summarize findings and insights related to performance management and employee relations activities to drive continual improvements.

Process Improvement & Digital Enablement

  • Support documentation and continuous improvement of People Partner processes, tools, and resources.
  • Assist with process mapping and identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce administrative effort, and improve efficiency.
  • Support development, testing, and implementation of tools, templates, and digital solutions that provide consistent guidance.
  • Help maintain centralized process documentation and knowledge resources.

Required Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, Organizational Development, or a related field. Graduating between December 2027 - May 2028
  • Demonstrated interest in HR, employee experience, or process improvement.
  • Experience using Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, or similar tools.
  • Strong curiosity, a proactive learning mindset, and a problem-solving approach.
  • Analytical skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to organize and simplify complex information.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented, and people-centered approach.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with process mapping tools, such as Visio.
  • Exposure to HR processes, employee relations, or employment practices.
  • Interest in HR technology, automation, or AI-driven solutions.
  • Experience summarizing data and creating visual insights.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $75,000 to $120,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Radnor, PA
  • Experience: 4+ years
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Senior Associate Actuarial Analyst role in assumption governance at Lincoln Financial, part of the Actuarial Development Program with rotations across business areas. Reviews and documents Life business assumptions, partners with Pricing on model inputs, and develops process improvements.

Good fit if you have passed at least 4 actuarial exams, have 1 to 4+ years of actuarial experience, know MG-ALFA, and work well independently and across teams.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina); Hartford, CT (Connecticut); Omaha, NE (Nebraska)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76818

The Role at a Glance

The Actuarial Development Program (ADP) at Lincoln Financial is an industry-leading program that demonstrates Lincoln Financial's commitment to creating highly qualified business leaders. As an ADP participant, you'll be able to explore your unique interests while developing the essential actuarial, technical, management, communication, and leadership skills you need to succeed. The Actuarial Development Program includes a series of rotations, typically every 18-24 months. For each rotation, roles are available in different business areas including Life and Annuities, Retirement and Group Protection. Experience gained will enable participants to become well-rounded actuaries with knowledge that may include Product Development, Pricing, Reinsurance, Inforce Management, Valuation, Financial Projections, Risk Management, Financial Planning & Analysis, Financial Strategy & Management, Appointed Actuary, Experience Studies, Modeling and Data Analytics & Actuarial Transformation.


ADP participants are expected to pass the Society of Actuaries' exams at a prescribed pace. The program is designed to support you as you work towards your FSA and provide the training and resources necessary to become a well-rounded actuarial leader.

Additional Program Highlights:

•Highly competitive compensation package with salary increases and bonuses upon successful exam completion
•Social and training opportunities to enhance skills, network with ADP participants and build long-lasting industry relationships
•Dedicated leaders and mentors to assist with career development
•Work with actuarial and data science software and technologies including MG-ALFA, Axis, Prophet, Dataiku, R, and Tableau
•Generous study time allowances for each exam session
•Payment and/or reimbursement of actuarial exam fees, materials, review courses, and seminars taken during the program


We're excited to bring on an Senior Associate Actuarial Analyst, Assumption Governance, to own the review and documentation of assumption proposals, approvals, implementations and impacts. This role offers a unique view into the assumptions that drive profitability across Life business, and it is a strong fit for someone who enjoys diving into the details of model inputs, taking on ad hoc projects, and collaborating across teams.

What you'll be doing

•Manage and maintain documentation of Life new business assumptions, including regular updates, version control, documentation of changes.
•Partner with the Pricing team to understand, review and refine model (MG-ALFA) input assumptions.
•Coordinate assumption updates with cross-functional teams and confirm that the latest approved assumptions are reflected in the assumptions
•Develop tools and process improvements to make assumption maintenance and validation more efficient and controlled
•Support ad hoc data analysis and projects as priorities evolve

What we're looking for

•Minimum of 4 actuarial exams passed
•1 to 4+ years of actuarial experience
•1 prior actuarial rotation
•Working knowledge of MG-ALFA
•Strong technical skills (Microsoft Office suite)
•Self-motivated with high level of integrity, strong problem-solving skills, and the capability of working independently
•Ability to quickly learn and apply new skills and information
•Collaborative, with the ability to build effective relationships across teams
•Strong written and verbal communication skills
•Experience with Tableau, SQL and Python is a plus

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through December 30th, 2026 subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

Job.JobTitle: Life Insurance Agency Development Manager (Life Sales Manager)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Manager, Insurance Sales, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
*This range represents a national range and the actual salary will depend on several factors including the scope and complexity of the role and the skills, education, training, credentials, location (State) based on ERIE's geographical differences, and experience of an applicant, as well as level of role for which the successful candidate is hired. Position may be eligible for an annual bonus payment.

At Erie Insurance, you're not just part of a Fortune 500 company; you're also a valued member of a diverse and inclusive team that includes more than 6,000 employees and over 13,000 independent agencies. Our Employees work in the Home Office complex located in Erie, PA, and in our Field Offices that span 12 states and the District of Columbia.

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That's why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.
  • Low contributions to medical and prescription premiums. We currently pay up to 97% of employees' monthly premium costs.
  • Pension. We are one of only 13 Fortune 500 companies to offer a traditional pension plan. Full-time employees are vested after five years of service.
  • 401(k) with up to 4% contribution match. The 401(k) is offered in addition to the pension.
  • Paid time off. Paid vacation, personal days, sick days, bereavement days and parental leave.
  • Career development. Including a tuition reimbursement program for higher education and industry designations.

Additional benefits that include company-paid basic life insurance; short-and long-term disability insurance; orthodontic coverage for children and adults; adoption assistance; fertility and infertility coverage; well-being programs; paid volunteer hours for service to your community; and dollar-for-dollar matching of your charitable gifts each year.

Position Summary

Life Sales Manager

ERIE Family Life is seeking a Life Sales Manager to drive life insurance and annuity growth across Central and Eastern Pennsylvania. In this highly visible field leadership role, you'll partner with independent ERIE Agents to expand life insurance production, identify cross-sell opportunities, develop agency growth strategies, and provide consultative sales coaching that helps agencies strengthen customer relationships and grow their business.

Success in This Role

Within the first year, successful Life Sales Managers will:

  • Build trusted relationships with agency partners throughout the territory
  • Increase life insurance and annuity production
  • Identify and execute agency growth opportunities
  • Conduct joint sales calls and field coaching sessions
  • Help agents develop sustainable life insurance sales strategies
  • Partner with branch leadership to drive territory performance and business growth

Territory

This territory-based position supports agencies throughout Central and Eastern Pennsylvania, including Harrisburg, Lancaster, Reading, Allentown, Bethlehem, Easton, and surrounding communities.

Candidates should reside within or near the Harrisburg or Lehigh Valley markets and be willing to travel throughout the assigned territory.

A company vehicle is provided.

Additional Opportunity

The hiring manager will also consider candidates for the Senior Life Sales Manager (F13) level. The level offered will be based on the selected candidate's experience, qualifications, and demonstrated success in life insurance sales leadership, agency development, and territory management.

Trains and guides Agents in a designated branch territory as well as additional assigned branch offices in the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products, providing assistance in the areas of production, product knowledge and application, underwriting, and agency management. Also assists Agents in examining and evaluating their current books of business for potential prospects and serves as company representative in maintaining favorable agency and Policyholder relationships. Scope: Life Sales Manager role is assigned to one branch. Sr Life Sales Manager is assigned to multiple branches.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists branch managers and district sales managers in establishing short- and long-range objectives related to life insurance and annuity sales, with emphasis on production, underwriting and Agent training.
  • Provides training and direction to ERIE Agents regarding the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products. Interacts with Agents as necessary, educating them regarding approved marketing and sales tools and techniques.
  • Educates Agents regarding the products available through Erie Family Life, including policy features and benefits. Assists Agents in reviewing their current books of business in order to identify cross selling opportunities for life insurance and annuity sales. Collaborates with Agents to identify prospecting opportunities.
  • Accompanies Agents on sales calls and assists with servicing existing customers and writing new business.
  • Serves as a liaison between the Home Office and the field. Clarifies and resolves issues, implements new programs and communicates program changes as necessary.
  • Represents the company in community relations activities as directed.
  • Develops marketing and prospecting programs to assist Agents in the sale of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Collaborates with Home Office and Branch Office marketing personnel regarding the design and promotion of incentive campaigns related to the sales of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Assists in the selection and training of newly appointed Agents, life producers and customer service representatives.
  • Handles Agency relationships and business, as a licensed life insurance Agent, according to company policy.
  • Advises appropriate Home Office personnel of competitive intelligence issues related to Agents and agency management.

The first 6 duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Capabilities

  • Values Diversity
  • Self-Development
  • Nimble Learning
  • Collaborates
  • Customer Focus
  • Cultivates Innovation
  • Instills Trust
  • Optimizes Work Processes (IC)
  • Ensures Accountability
  • Decision Quality

Qualifications

Minimum Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in insurance, sales, marketing or related field and five years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or
  • Associate's degree in insurance, sales, marketing or related field and seven years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or
  • High School diploma or GED and nine years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or

Additional Experience

  • A minimum of two years' experience in sales of life insurance.
  • The incumbent must live in the state assigned unless a change is approved by the company.
  • Frequent overnight travel required.

Designations and/or Licenses

  • Related designations, such as CIC, CFP, ChFC, or CLU, preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Lifting/Moving 0-20 lbs; Occasional (<20%)
  • Lifting/Moving 20-50 lbs; Occasional (<20%)
  • Ability to move over 50 lbs using lifting aide equipment; Occasional (<20%)
  • Driving; Frequent (50-80%)
  • Pushing/Pulling/moving objects, equipment with wheels; Occasional (<20%)
  • Manual Keying/Data Entry/inputting information/computer use; Often (20-50%)
  • Climbing/accessing heights; Rarely

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a highly motivated Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead to staff our ever-growing claims organization.

As a Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead, you will perform and deliver on long-term disability (LTD) claims assignments/projects while simultaneously leveraging and applying knowledge. You will review, investigate, and make claim determinations regarding coverage, compensability, and appropriateness assigned claims. You will provide oversight, technical information, detailed guidance and supervise the daily activities for their assigned claims area. Additionally, they will oversee and ensure the daily fair, ethical, and timely management of all claims area(s).

What you'll be doing

  • You'll manage a caseload of complex Long Term Disability claims with varied eligibility types, policy provisions, and diagnoses.
  • You'll apply policies and engage internal and external resources to ensure fair, ethical, and timely claim decisions.
  • You'll make claim-related financial decisions within company guidelines.
  • You'll use sound judgment and claims expertise to decide based on the information available.
  • You'll explain policy details, the claims process, and determinations so customers understand the outcome.
  • You'll keep inventory stable through timely risk management and efficient processing.
  • You'll resolve escalated issues and elevate to management when needed.
  • You'll research questions from the Claims team, partnering with Underwriting, Actuarial, Compliance, Account Management, and others to find answers.
  • You'll provide technical guidance on claims adjudication and coach junior team members on medical terminology, duration, functionality documentation, and workflow.
  • You'll monitor individual and team performance and act to meet or exceed standards.
  • You'll analyze reports to spot trends, then propose and develop process improvements that enhance performance and the customer experience.
  • You'll advise on how proposed process changes affect operations and system compatibility.
  • You'll mentor others and model the behaviors that build claims knowledge and strong relationships.
  • You'll contribute to departmental projects and lead workstreams as needed.

What we're looking for

Must-have experience (Required):

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's).
  • 1+ Years of Long Term Disability claims experience directly aligned to the specific responsibilities for this role.
  • Ability to communicate effectively (verbal/written).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).

Nice-to have experience (Preferred):

  • Strong mathematical skills for payment calculations.
  • Strong attention to detail.

The Senior Product Owner plays a pivotal role in driving the successful development and delivery of innovative products that meet the needs of our customers and aligns with the company's strategic goals. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Maximizes the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum team.

  • Defines and communicates product vision, overall strategy and growth opportunities to business and IT stakeholders, with minimal guidance from leadership and other Product team members.

  • Researches and analyzes market trends and user needs to develop and shape the roadmap for the product.
  • Collaborates with other Product Owners, Product Managers and shares best practices across teams to ensure alignment and consistency in ways of working within a value stream.

This position has no supervisory responsibility.

  • Experience with integrations across underwriting workbenches, PAS, billing systems, distribution/agency management, document management, and third-party data providers.
  • Experience with AI-powered or automated intake workflows (document extraction, OCR, conversational submission)
  • Data migration and reconciliation experience preferred
  • Majesco, Guidewire or comparable platform experience preferred

Certified Product Owner (CPO) required, SAFe preferred.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of the Information Security Engineer III is to design secure architectures and develop cybersecurity approaches and techniques to protect ICW Group's cloud, data, and/or AI-driven environments. This position will assist with strategic initiatives for short and long-term plans to identify and reduce the attack surface across applications and systems. This role partners closely with application, cloud, data, and analytics teams to ensure security is embedded into systems from design through production

This role supports ICW's modern data initiatives by reducing risk, strengthening security controls, and enabling secure adoption of new technologies in a highly regulated insurance environment. The engineer contributes across vulnerability management, threat detection, and incident response while providing practical security guidance that balances risk, compliance, and business needs.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Monitoring, Detection, and Incident Support

  • Monitors cloud, on-prem, and SaaS environments for security threats using SIEM, EDR, cloud-native logging, and network telemetry.
  • Assists with security incident response activities, including investigation, containment, remediation, and post-incident analysis.
  • Researches and implements methods to remediate network and application security vulnerabilities.
  • Leads and participates in security architecture controls reporting, compliance audits, monthly and ad-hoc statistics and trends, and risk-focused reports including internal and 3rd party Risk Assessments.
  • Produce risk-focused security findings and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Conducts threat hunting and root-cause analysis to identify anomalous behavior, exploitation attempts, and indicators of compromise.
  • Investigates potential data misuse, data exfiltration, and anomalous access patterns using logs, DLP, and monitoring tools.

Cloud & Generalist Security Responsibilities.

  • Prepares and analyses system security reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and trends and makes recommendations to improve security.
  • Serve as a senior technical contributor across cloud security, including IAM, logging, monitoring, detection, and secure deployment patterns.
  • Lead or contribute to vulnerability management across cloud infrastructure, applications, containers, and data platforms.
  • Participate in offensive and defensive security activities, including threat modeling, red team exercises, blue team detection improvements, and threat hunting.
  • Support incident response investigations involving cloud misconfigurations, data exposure, and/or AI-related security events.
  • Perform security architecture reviews and provide guidance to engineering teams to reduce risk while enabling business objectives.
  • Implement and improve security controls that strengthen ICW's overall security posture while supporting modern cloud and data initiatives.

Security Architecture, Standards, and Risk

  • Partners with Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Data, and Operations teams to embed security into system design and delivery.
  • Lead security reviews for new data, analytics, and/or AI initiatives, including architecture reviews and risk assessments prior to production deployment.
  • Conduct threat modeling and security design reviews for systems involving data, analytics, AI, and/or cloud services.
  • Create and maintain technical security standards and guardrails related to data protection, cloud usage, and/or AI security.
  • Partner with internal teams to remediate security findings and track remediation activities through closure.
  • Provide security guidance that balances risk reduction with delivery speed and business priorities.

Collaboration and Enablement

  • Executes technical and process changes required to adopt, maintain, and adjust InfoSec controls as required to manage the company's risks and align with industry best practices.
  • Partner with Engineering, Cloud, Data, Infrastructure, and Operations teams to embed security into system design and delivery.
  • Act as a trusted security advisor to project teams, helping them understand risk, controls, and secure design patterns.
  • Coach and mentor engineers on secure development, data handling, and cloud security best practices.
  • Work closely with project management and internal stakeholders to define and implement secure, scalable solutions.

Data and AI Security

  • Design and implement security controls to protect sensitive insurance data across AWS data platforms, analytics pipelines, and AI/ML workloads.
  • Provide security oversight for AI and LLM use cases, including model access controls, training data protection, inference security, data leakage prevention, and misuse/abuse risk.
  • Assess and mitigate risks related to AI systems, LLM usage, prompt injection, data poisoning, third-party data sources, and emerging AI threats.
  • Partner with Compliance and Governance teams to ensure data and AI controls align with NIST, NYDFS, PCI DSS, and California privacy regulations (CPRA/CCPA).
  • Contribute to the development of ICW's AI security standards, guardrails, and internal guidance as AI adoption expands across the enterprise.
  • Support Third-Party Risk (TPR) evaluations for AI vendors, SaaS platforms, data providers, and analytics tools that process or access ICW data.
  • Evaluate and onboard security tools and vendors related to data protection, cloud security posture, AI governance, and detection.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's Degree required in Engineering, Cybersecurity, Networking, or Computer Science related discipline.
  • Minimum 8 years of experience working in a security engineering related role designing secure networks, systems and application architectures or equivalent combination of education and experience required.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in AWS Cloud Security services preferred. Direct experience using advanced technologies such as Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), Firewalls, SIEM, Antivirus software, Network Packet Analyzers, content filtering, Malware analysis and forensics tools to detect intrusions.
  • Experience in cyber security role requiring knowledge of data analysis, risk assessment, risk mitigation, investigation methods, incident management concepts and practices, and policy and procedure development.
  • Experience with AWS Services such as AWS Identity & Access Management, AWS Organizations, AWS Security HuB, Guard Duty, CloudTrail, AWS CloudTrail.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Certification in GSEC, CISSP, and/or Security+ preferred. AWS Certified Security – Specialty, preferred.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Knowledge of risk assessment tools, technologies, and methodologies.
  • Knowledge of disaster recovery, computer forensic tools, technologies, and methods. Knowledge of enterprise security platforms.
  • Ability to communicate network security issues to peers and management.
  • Ability to read and use the results of mobile code, malicious code, and anti-virus software.
  • Strong understanding of endpoint security solutions to include File Integrity Monitoring and Data Loss Prevention.
  • Demonstrated experience as a lead engineer in the design, implementation and support in an enterprise IT environment.
  • Ability to combine disparate skills and thinking to craft solutions and solve complex operational problems. Ability to hypothesize on root cause of inefficiencies and then test out probable solutions against those hypotheses.
  • Must be able to read, write and speak English effectively.
  • Ability to effectively communicate/present technical information to a non-technical audience.
  • Ability to cross train and share information with team members.

We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


ABOUT ICW GROUP

ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly.

ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE

The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency.

The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready.

Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management

  • Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure.

  • Operate the intake-to-decision workflow -- apply the risk taxonomy (Tier 0 through Tier 4), move each use case through the lifecycle gates with required signoffs and triggered control-function reviews, resolve intake or escalation issues, and maintain the decision log, exception register, and escalation paths.

Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory

  • Maintain the AI policy, standard, procedure, and control library with clear owners and review cadence, coordinate rollout of the policy suite (including the prohibited-use list), keep governance templates current, support control sufficiency testing for Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and recommend process and control enhancements that improve governance performance across the function.

  • Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems.

AI Hub Ownership

  • Own and operate the AI Hub on SharePoint as the enterprise's single front door for AI serving approximately 1,300 employees -- intake, approved tools, responsible-use guidance, governance materials, learning, and metrics -- managing the content lifecycle and running it as the interface between AIGEC and the workforce.

NAIC Regulatory Compliance Coordination

  • Serve as the NAIC Response Coordinator, or lead significant portions of the response, for California DOI AI Systems Evaluation Tool inquiries, coordinate cross-functional evidence collection, maintain the artifacts serving Exhibits A through D (AI Systems Registry, model cards, AI Data Element Registry with Data Services, and the risk classification methodology), and track readiness and related policy updates as the pilot evolves.

Monitoring, Audit Readiness, and Reporting

  • Operate the governance KPI and KRI dashboard and produce reporting for AIGEC and executive leadership, assemble audit-ready evidence packs for Tier 1 systems, run regulatory scanning (NIST AI RMF, NAIC, ISO/IEC 42001, state AI laws), and route material changes into policy and control updates with operational recommendations.

Training, Awareness, and Change Management

  • Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment.

  • Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement.

  • Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains.

  • Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level

  • Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting.

  • Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions

  • Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred.

  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred.

  • Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred.

  • Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred.

  • Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

  • Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise.

  • Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function.

  • Detail Orientation: Meticulous attention to governance artifacts, compliance documentation, and registry data integrity.

  • Communication: Ability to synthesize technical, business, and regulatory information into clear, actionable materials for business owners, control functions, vendors, and executive leadership.

  • Ownership and Project Leadership: Self-directed execution across multiple concurrent governance workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

  • Adaptability: Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to establish structure and process where none exists.

  • Regulatory Awareness: Genuine interest in AI regulation and responsible AI, and in keeping ICW's posture current as expectations evolve.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is based at ICW Group's Innovation Point campus in San Diego, CA. Occasional collaboration with remote team members and external partners via Microsoft Teams may be required. This position observes standard business hours with flexibility to support cross-time-zone engagements as needed.

Job Summary

Ready to change how a Life Insurance business uses data to grow? As Director, Business Intelligence & Analytics, you will lead a team of two analysts and serve as the go-to data and analytics partner across our Life Insurance organization. You will transform how the business accesses and uses data, turning insights from distribution and sales, new business, and customer and agent experience into decisions that drive profitable growth.

Your team will own a portfolio of field-facing and operational reports and dashboards, build statistical models, and provide the analytical horsepower behind high-visibility, cross-functional initiatives. You will influence data and analytics strategy, review and approve analytics initiatives, oversee the support and evolution of existing data products, and bring innovative ideas to business leadership, then lead them through to implementation. This is a highly visible role for a builder who wants to see their work move the needle.

Essential Job Functions

In this role, you will lead the analytics engine behind our Life Insurance business. You will develop advanced, value-driven analytics solutions, from statistical models that sharpen our understanding of the application funnel, policy placement, and persistency to Power BI dashboards that give agents, field leaders, and operations teams the insights they need to act. You will own and continuously evolve a portfolio of field-facing and operational reports and dashboards so they keep pace with changing business needs.

As a trusted partner to leaders across distribution and sales, customer and agent experience, and operations, you will identify the biggest opportunities to unlock business value, translate them into clear analytics requirements and business plans, and drive them to resolution. You will apply a deep understanding of the data elements, structures, and standards common in financial services and Life Insurance, including cloud-based data storage and sharing, to balance regulatory and compliance requirements with business needs. You will consult on UAT, technical specifications, strategic planning, contract design, testing, and training, and independently lead highly complex projects with little to no guidance.

As a people leader, you will supervise, coach, and manage the performance of two analysts, deliver regular feedback, and support their professional development, fostering a high-performance culture where excellence is standard and innovation is actively encouraged. You will craft strategic plans and turn them into action for your team and for partners across three or more business domains, communicating strategy in a way that resonates with audiences new to data and analytics and helping enable enterprise priorities.

Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree or equivalent required, preferably in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Actuarial Science, Finance, Business Analytics, or a related quantitative field. Master's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or an MBA with a quantitative focus preferred. Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate or insurance industry designations (e.g., LOMA FLMI), are a plus.

Experience Requirements

7-10 years of related work experience in business intelligence, analytics, or data science required, including:

  • Building and maintaining enterprise reporting and dashboards in Power BI (or a comparable BI tool) for business and front-line audiences, including data modeling and DAX

  • Applying statistical and predictive modeling techniques (e.g., regression, segmentation, propensity or retention modeling) to solve business problems and influence decisions

  • Hands-on proficiency with SQL and experience working with data warehouses, data marts, and cloud-based data platforms across multiple source systems

  • Partnering with senior business leaders to translate ambiguous questions into analytics requirements, prioritized roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes

  • Leading complex, cross-functional analytics initiatives with IT, data science, product, and vendor partners from concept through implementation

  • Establishing data quality, governance, and reporting standards, and resolving data issues across systems

  • Communicating insights and recommendations clearly to executive and non-technical audiences

Preferred experience:

  • Insurance or financial services industry experience, ideally in Life Insurance, with familiarity with new business, underwriting, policy administration, and distribution data

  • Experience analyzing sales and distribution performance, application funnel and throughput, placement, persistency, or agent and customer experience metrics

  • Experience in a people leader or management role, including coaching and developing analysts

  • Experience supporting field-facing or agent-facing reporting in a distribution-driven organization

  • Working knowledge of Python or R and of data privacy and regulatory considerations in insurance

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

We are seeking an Attorney with jury trial experience to join our Northern California staff counsel team! Our attorneys work from home and handle in-person appearances and trials as required. We offer developmental opportunities, and a comprehensive benefits package including annual bonus potential up to 20% of the salary, generous 401k, auto allowance, PTO, medical/dental/vision, paid parental leave, and much more all without the stress of billable hours!

Job Summary

This position is responsible for representing clients in all areas of insurance defense practice, handling cases that are primarily low to moderate in complexity and exposure. Manages all phases of cases from intake to resolution.

Essential Job Functions

  • Litigates low to moderate complexity and exposure cases and performs duties necessary from intake to trial and/or settlement. This includes but is not limited to preparation of pleadings, motions, discovery, and briefs.
  • Attends hearings, conferences, interviews, mediations, arbitrations, and/or trials.
  • Proactively informs leadership of case handling opportunities and challenges encountered.
  • Consults with the Claims Department on the legal aspects of files and jurisdictional issues.
  • Performs other tasks or duties to ensure efficient case management.
  • May handle second chair trials and handle trials in cases with moderate complexity and/or exposure.
  • Provides support to senior attorneys in cases of greater complexity and/or exposure and receives developmental assignments of matters that are of high complexity and/or exposure.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Three years of insurance defense litigation and/or personal/bodily injury experience preferred. Second chair trial experience strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Special Skill Requirement

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Additional Qualification

Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Excellent written communication skills. Effective negotiation skills. Demonstrated conflict management skills. Ability to represent the company with external constituents. Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills. Demonstrated time management and priority setting skills. Ability to work within tight timeframes and meet strict deadlines. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Adept and proficient at using technology to maximize efficiency in virtual, paperless environment.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Job.JobTitle: Account Executive – Mid-Atlantic, US Accident & Health (A&H)
Job.JobDescription:
Account Executive – Mid-Atlantic, US Accident & Health (A&H)


About the position

Join us as an Account Executive to play an influential role in driving sales growth at AIG Accident & Health, a leading provider of insurance products and services focused on managing risk for both commercial and personal customers. We offer a broad range of products through a diversified, multi-channel distribution network, including one of the world's most far-reaching property casualty networks. In this role, you will report to the Head of Sales and Distribution, North America Accident & Health and be responsible for overseeing the Mid-Atlantic sales territory. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record of developing relationships with internal and external trading partners and creating a pipeline of new business opportunities aligned with the business strategy.


How you will create an impact

  • Oversee a sales territory for Accident & Health products.
  • Work with licensed producers to solicit new business opportunities.
  • Coordinate with regional underwriting to build coverage plan designs to meet customer needs.
  • Leverage extensive A&H product capabilities to offer customized coverage solutions.
  • Collaborate with internal commercial lines partners to cross-sell accident products to new and existing clients.
  • Articulate AIG's Accident & Health value proposition to external business partners to drive new business and retain renewal business.
  • Evaluate successes and challenges in territory and leverage key takeaways for effective strategy development.
  • Create and execute business plans, including a broker segmentation strategy, to achieve or exceed growth through new business, renewal retention, and increasing GPW
  • Establish effective budgets reflecting growth and diversification within the territory.
  • Engage with internal business partners to leverage relationships and strategic alignments throughout the organization.
  • Use Salesforce to develop target pipeline for new business and measure quote-to-bind ratios in the region.
  • Accurately forecast the assigned territory's monthly, quarterly, and yearly premium production for upward reporting to leadership.

What you'll need to succeed

  • Relevant sales experience is preferred – ideally you will have experience of working in the Mid-Atlantic region
  • Strong communication, presentation and team-working skills.
  • A hard-working, self-motivated energetic approach with the ability to deliver results under pressure.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain the internal and/or external sales strategy and processes to maximize the organization's profit potential
  • Promote the organization's products and services to new and current clients
  • Ensure all clients are satisfied and that the quality of the services they provide meet or exceed customer expectations
  • Liaise with clients on regular bases to understand their needs, resolve client complaints and issues, develop new business, and to provide value
  • Review current and prospective clients accounts to identify business opportunities, analyze opportunities, and promote sales growth
  • Provide reports, presentations, and recommendations on market trends, customer trends, and competitors actions
  • Handle internal and client inquiries and complaints
  • Create sales strategies, action plans and budgets
  • Research and develop new sales opportunities or new markets

Requirements

  • 5+ years insurance experience, with Accident & Health industry experience preferred.

Responsible for creating a comprehensive estimate of damages for 1st and 3rd party material damage claims leading to the proper disposition. This role is utilized as a peer mentor having mastered our processes and obtained technical expertise.

We are seeking an Auto Field Adjuster in Pasadena, CA / Glendale, CA / or East Los Angeles, CA Territory to join our team. In this field-based role, you will assess vehicle damage, prepare estimates, and guide customers through the claims process.

Interprets regulatory compliance and fair claims practices

Job Description

Director – Contracts - Reinsurance

This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our Chicago, IL or Bloomington, MN office

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Joining Aon's Reinsurance Solutions team, you will take charge of preparing, examining, and completing formal documentation that captures the terms and conditions related to treaty reinsurance arrangements. You will be motivated to continuously learn and stay current with industry expressions, conditions, trends, and regulatory changes.

Role Responsibilities

  • Support hiring, workforce planning, and talent development to ensure suitable staffing, technical knowledge, and capabilities within the department.
  • Prepare complex reinsurance contracts and review the work of supporting Contract Drafters, ensuring technical quality, accuracy, and consistency.
  • Manage and develop team of supporting Contract Drafters, offering technical mentorship, quality oversight, mentoring, feedback, and support for colleague development.
  • Participate in client, reinsurer, and broker meetings, providing wording expertise in the development and interpretation of contract language.
  • Apply deep understanding of reinsurance structures and intent to guide brokers and clients in developing and interpreting contract language covering complex coverage builds and potential loss scenarios.
  • Partner with brokers during placement negotiations to join client discussions regarding wording provisions addressing emerging risks and specific client concerns.
  • Support business growth and strengthen client advocacy through RFP participation, competitor wording reviews, and recommendations for coverage and contract improvements for new and existing clients.
  • Maintain a solid grasp of evolving insurance, reinsurance, and risk management market conditions and keep brokers and clients updated on pertinent developments.
  • Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on reinsurance contract wordings, offering mentorship and recommendations to brokers and clients.
  • Manage departmental projects and initiatives passionate about improving contract processes, capabilities, consistency, and client service.
  • Develop training materials and deliver internal technical training on reinsurance contract wording, market trends, and guidelines within the department.
  • Contribute to the Annual Global Client Training Summit by presenting to clients and preparing materials on reinsurance contract wording trends, market developments, and possible coverage or contract improvements.
  • Support multiline reinsurance business for Global and US clients.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Legal Studies, Risk Management, a related field, or equivalent years of industry experience.
  • A minimum of 8 years in insurance or reinsurance, working as a lawyer/attorney or contract/policy specialist, with preference for experience in reinsurance structures. Experience drafting and interpreting treaty wordings for domestic and global placements is preferred.
