Job.JobDescription:
At Alliant Insurance Services, we thrive on creating employee benefits solutions built on the idea that health makes growth possible. As top tier professionals dedicated to solving our clients' health and welfare insurance challenges, Alliant team members deliver an unrivaled depth of service, and our unique approach enables us to help clients stay resilient and turn change into opportunity. This position is a chance to join a dynamic, expanding company with prospects for individual and career growth.

As one of the 5 largest insurance brokerage firms in the U.S., Alliant provides property and casualty, workers' compensation, employee benefits, surety, and financial products and services to clients nationwide.

More information is available at >.

SUMMARY

Responsible for conducting analysis, pricing and risk assessment to estimate financial outcomes. Applies knowledge of mathematics, probability, statistics, and principles of finance and business to calculations in life, health, social and casualty insurance, annuities, and pensions.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provides business leadership, analytical expertise, and process oversight for significant strategic initiatives;

• Prepares and analyzes various reports to identify trends and deviations;

• Conducts analysis by qualitatively and/or quantitatively analyzing data and information, including exploratory data analysis, graphing, forecasting and modeling;

• Analyzes and documents complex data and business problems and provides recommendations based on research of performance analysis and business products for optimal business solutions;

• Develops reports, presentations and proposals for action and/or implementation plans and presents to management to assist in decision making;

• Performs quality assurance checks/peer reviews on the work of other team members/departments;

• Reviews and evaluates existing procedures and operations in assigned area; makes recommendations regarding improvements;

• Manages key actuarial projects;

• Trains or provides guidance to team members;

• Complies with agency management system data standards and data integrity (enters and maintains complete and accurate information);

• Infrequent travel required 10% - 20% of the time;

• Other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's Degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics or related quantitative field

Fifteen (15) or more years related work experience

Fellowship in the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS)

Fellowship in the Society of Actuaries (FSA)

SKILLS

Excellent verbal and written communication and presentation skills

Proven ability to apply actuarial techniques and standards to complex business problems

Excellent planning, organizational, and prioritization skills

Excellent analytical, problem solving and time management skills

Possess high level of accuracy and attention to detail

Ability to work independently and within a team and to foster teamwork

Advanced knowledge of insurance or financial principles and concepts

Proficient in Microsoft Office products; expert level in Excel

Join a hands-on maintenance team responsible for supporting facility operations, manufacturing readiness, and business growth. This role performs a wide range of facilities, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and preventative maintenance activities to ensure equipment, systems, and building infrastructure operate safely and efficiently.


What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • Perform facility-wide repairs, installations, preventative maintenance, and general upkeep activities.
  • Install, maintain, and troubleshoot electrical systems including outlets, fixtures, switches, circuits, PLCs, and CNC equipment.
  • Repair and install plumbing systems including faucets, drains, toilets, and compressed air lines.
  • Work with copper, PVC/CPVC, and PEX piping systems.
  • Conduct preventative maintenance on conveyors, pallet jacks, compactors, automated equipment, motors, and pneumatic systems.
  • Complete carpentry projects including framing, drywall repair, door and window installation or adjustment.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical and electrical issues to minimize production downtime.
  • Analyze recurring equipment failures and recommend maintenance improvements.
  • Support general facility needs including painting, signage installation, janitorial support, and seasonal maintenance.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Minimum of three years of professional trade or military experience, with prior supervisory or leadership experience preferred.
  • Hands-on experience in electrical, mechanical, and/or plumbing trades.
  • Ability to read and work from diagrams, sketches, manuals, and engineering specifications.
  • Knowledge of relay logic, ladder diagrams, motors, sensors, relays, drives, timers, solenoids, and related controls equipment.
  • Experience with PLC and CNC troubleshooting.
  • Understanding of electrical safety practices including Lock, Tag, Try (LTT), arc-flash prevention, and safe tool usage.
  • Experience performing preventative maintenance and equipment troubleshooting.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and ability to assemble racks, carts, benches, and related equipment.
  • Ability to prioritize work, manage schedules, and work independently with limited supervision.
  • Ability to make sound decisions during equipment failures or emergency situations.
  • Valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record.
  • Successful completion of a criminal background check and motor vehicle record (MVR) review.
  • Ability to qualify for and maintain authorization to drive company-owned vehicles.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Knowledge of reliability-centered maintenance, root cause failure analysis (RCFA), or failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA).
  • Experience running power lines, wiring motors, panels, transformers, and industrial equipment.

About this job

Support compliance operations for Medicare/Medicaid insurance through investigations, record management, and regulatory monitoring. Role involves coordinating audits, reviewing marketing materials, developing training programs, and identifying compliance risks.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, one or more years of compliance experience, and knowledge of insurance or financial services.

Full job description


SUMMARY

Responsible for providing support, practical management and guidance to ensure the Company's operations are conducted in compliance with ethical business practices, Company policies and legal/regulatory requirements. Advise business units and protect the Company's interests in all corporate, legal and regulatory matters.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Compliance Department Administration:

Manage carrier compliance investigations of alleged violations or rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and standard of conduct; including recording notifications, proper internal and external communication, and tracking to ensure timely responses. Identify compliance trends through monitoring internal and external reporting and assisting in the development of compliance guidelines and tools. Assist in call center oversight.

Coordinate, record, maintain and monitor compliance records, reports and analysis ensuring that all data records are complete and accurate to ensure compliance with applicable federal and state laws and regulations.

Assist with internal and external audits; and working with other departments on designated compliance matters.

Review agent-created advertisements, social media and websites; Directly provide guidance to internal and external parties. Assist with submission of marketing materials to carriers for approval and regulatory approval if necessary.

Assist Compliance Officer with administering and improving the Company's Compliance Program.

Assist with responses to alleged violations of rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and standards of conduct.

Assist with proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.

Assist with statutory and regulatory monitoring and communication of updates throughout the Company and its downstream agents.

Assist with the development and oversight of an effective compliance training program for the Company and its downstream agents, which includes appropriate training for new employees as well as ongoing training for all employees.

Assist with monitoring and coordinating the compliance activities of all business units, which includes tracking and reporting of key compliance metrics.

Assist with identifying potential areas of compliance vulnerability and risk; Assist with development and implementation of corrective action plans for resolution of problematic issues.

Special Projects: Work collaboratively with fellow staff to advance the values and mission of Senior Market Sales by serving on relevant internal and external committees; Assists with special projects/assignments as requested by members of management.

Performs other duties as assigned by management. *


QUALIFICATIONS
EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in business or a related field

One (1) or more years of compliance experience

Insurance industry or related field (financial services or marketing) experience

Carrier certification with MA/PDP


SKILLS

Working knowledge of federal, state and local laws, as well as industry regulations.

Working knowledge of insurance services industries.

Knowledge of the general industry procedures, practices and terminology.

Knowledge of systems management.

Knowledge of general office forms, processes and procedures.

Knowledge of program and project management including outcomes, quality assurance, and satisfaction measurement and interpretation.

Knowledge of supervisory techniques to accomplish instruction, motivation and training.

Skill to supervise, motivate and train.

Skill in working effectively with inbound and outbound callers/customers.

Skill in negotiating and problem solving to resolve internal and external conflicts.

Skill in the use of office equipment including computer, fax, printer, telephone system, etc.

Skill in the use of time management.

Skill in maintaining effective working relationships with all customers, employees and the general public.

Proficient computer skills (Microsoft/Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Acrobat, MS Outlook software preferred).

Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, in a constructive manner.

Ability to approach and communicate with a wide range of personalities in a professional and courteous manner. Ability to be patient under frustrating circumstances and demonstrate controlled emotional affect in difficult situations.

Ability to engage in effective interpersonal interaction, verbal communication and written communication.

Ability to maintain a high level of organization and attention to detail while remaining flexible and responsive when faced with multiple urgent requests.

Ability to read, write and communicate English effectively.

Ability to maintain all company policies, including all confidentiality and safety policies.

Ability to actively contribute to team effort.

Ability to work independently, exercise independent judgment, make and execute decisions.

Ability to develop and foster trusting relationships.

Strong verbal and written proficiencies of the English language is required and bilingual (Spanish and English) preferred.

Join a high-impact Digital Marketing team as a Performance Marketing & ABM Manager, where you will lead the strategy, execution, and optimization of enterprise demand generation initiatives that directly influence revenue growth. This role is responsible for driving awareness, engagement, qualified pipeline, and customer acquisition across multiple priority lines of business through innovative performance marketing and account-based marketing (ABM) programs.


As a strategic marketing partner and individual contributor, you will translate business objectives and sales priorities into targeted audience strategies, integrated paid media campaigns, ABM initiatives, channel experimentation, and investment plans designed to accelerate pipeline creation and increase sales velocity. Leveraging data, analytics, and market insights, you will continuously optimize campaign performance to maximize ROI and deliver measurable business outcomes.


Working cross-functionally with line-of-business marketing leaders, sales organizations, analytics teams, digital marketing peers, and external agency partners, you will play a critical role in aligning marketing efforts with revenue objectives. You will own the growth strategy and performance of paid and ABM programs while partnering with internal stakeholders on campaign execution, funnel optimization, measurement, and reporting.


The ideal candidate is a results-driven digital marketer with deep expertise in performance marketing, demand generation, audience targeting, and account-based marketing. They possess a strong analytical mindset, a passion for experimentation, and a proven ability to transform complex business goals into scalable marketing programs that drive engagement, pipeline growth, and revenue impact.


What Makes Us Different?

This role combines performance marketing, account-based marketing, innovation, and enterprise collaboration. You will help shape go-to-market strategies, evaluate emerging technologies, and influence growth initiatives across multiple lines of business.


What Will Be My Duties and Responsibilities in This Job?

  • Develop and execute digital acquisition and demand generation strategies that support business and pipeline goals.
  • Plan, launch, and optimize paid media campaigns across search, social, display, video, retargeting, and other digital channels.
  • Monitor campaign performance and make data-driven recommendations to improve results and maximize return on investment.
  • Lead account-based marketing (ABM) initiatives, including audience segmentation, account targeting, personalization, and campaign activation.
  • Leverage platforms such as Demandbase, LinkedIn, and other marketing technologies to drive engagement and pipeline growth.
  • Partner with Marketing, Sales, and cross-functional stakeholders to align target audiences, campaign objectives, and go-to-market strategies.
  • Collaborate with Marketing Operations and Analytics teams to support campaign execution, measurement, and reporting.
  • Manage media budgets, forecasts, vendor relationships, and agency partnerships to ensure efficient use of resources.
  • Evaluate marketing technologies, digital channels, and emerging advertising opportunities to drive innovation and improve performance.
  • Continuously refine marketing strategies, success metrics, and ABM capabilities to enhance business impact and support growth.

What Are the Requirements Needed for This Position?

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or related field.
  • A minimum of 7 years of experience in B2B marketing, performance marketing, ABM, demand generation, or related disciplines.
  • Experience leading complex digital campaigns from strategy through optimization.
  • Strong expertise in paid search, paid social, and display advertising.
  • Experience with Demandbase, 6sense, or similar ABM platforms.
  • Experience with Salesforce Sales Cloud; HubSpot or similar CRM platforms considered.
  • Proven project management, stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities within a matrixed enterprise environment.

What Other Skills/Experience Would Be Helpful to Have?

  • Salesforce Marketing Cloud experience.
  • Enterprise B2B marketing experience across multiple business units.
  • Agency-side marketing experience.
  • Experience with AI tools including Microsoft Copilot.
  • Experience evaluating new marketing technologies and channels.

About this job

Prepare and review complex statutory NAIC financial statements, regulatory filings, and supporting schedules for Lincoln Financial Group. Position involves statutory accounting analysis, close participation, regulatory research, and coordination of control testing, fully remote.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of financial reporting or accounting experience with statutory reporting knowledge and a bachelor's degree.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Work from Home

Work Arrangement:

Remote : Work at home employee residing outside of a commutable distance to an office location.

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76850

The Role at a Glance

As the STAT Financial Reporting Analyst you will play an important role in supporting the accuracy and integrity of the organization's statutory financial reporting. You will analyze and prepare complex statutory financial statements, regulatory filings, and supporting schedules while applying your knowledge of statutory accounting principles and NAIC requirements. You will help prepare audited financial statements. You will also research technical accounting and regulatory matters, partner with internal and external stakeholders, and help ensure reporting requirements are met accurately and effectively.

What you'll be doing

  • Prepares and/or reviews more complex quarterly and annual Statutory NAIC financial statements, supporting schedules, and other regulatory filings.
  • Reviews, analyzes, and reports on more complex statutory financial statements and supporting schedules in accordance with accounting and reporting calendars.
  • Participates in the accounting close, including the preparation and review of more complex journal entries, account reconciliations, and statutory reporting adjustments.
  • Conducts more complex financial analysis by legal entity in partnership with internal business team.
  • Identifies and researches more complex reporting issues arising from the application of statutory accounting principles, NAIC guidance, and other regulatory requirements, and assesses their applicability to assigned areas of responsibility.
  • Provides more complex support with the coordination of MAR control and regulatory testing to comply with key controls developed for the group.
  • Promotes and enhances organizational initiatives by positively influencing and supporting change management and/or departmental/enterprise initiatives within assigned area(s) of responsibility.

What we're looking for

Must-Haves

  • 3+ years of experience in financial reporting, accounting, or financial analysis that directly aligns with the specific responsibilities of this role, including statutory reporting experience
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience
  • Working knowledge of statutory accounting principles, NAIC reporting requirements, and insurance financial reporting
  • Strong analytical skills, sound judgment, and close attention to detail, with the ability to research and communicate complex reporting matters
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills, the ability to work collaboratively, and the ability to adapt quickly while meeting reporting deadlines in a changing work environment.

Nice-to-Haves

  • CPA or CPA Eligibility Certification

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through November, 30, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

What's it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

What's in it for you:

  • Clearly defined career tracks and job levels, along with associated behaviors for each of Lincoln's core values and leadership attributes

  • Leadership development and virtual training opportunities

  • PTO/parental leave

  • Competitive 401K and employee benefits

  • Free financial counseling, health coaching and employee assistance program

  • Tuition assistance program

  • Work arrangements that work for you

  • Effective productivity/technology tools and training

The pay range for this position is $75,000 - $120,000 with anticipated pay for new hires between the minimum and midpoint of the range and could vary above and below the listed range as permitted by applicable law. Pay is based on non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, education, location, licensure requirements, proficiency and qualifications required for the role. The base pay is just one component of Lincoln's total rewards package for employees. In addition, the role may be eligible for the Annual Incentive Program, which is discretionary and based on the performance of the company, business unit and individual. Other rewards may include long-term incentives, sales incentives and Lincoln's standard benefits package.

About The Company

Lincoln Financial (NYSE: LNC) helps people to confidently plan for their version of a successful future. We focus on identifying a clear path to financial security, with products including annuities, life insurance, group protection, and retirement plan services.

With our 120-year track record of expertise and integrity, millions of customers trust our solutions and service to help put their goals in reach.

Lincoln Financial Distributors, a broker-dealer, is the wholesale distribution organization of Lincoln Financial. Lincoln Financial is the marketing name for Lincoln Financial Corporation and its affiliates including The Lincoln National Life Insurance Company, Fort Wayne, IN, and Lincoln Life & Annuity Company of New York, Syracuse, NY. Leadership & Strategy

About this job

Prepares coverage opinions and manages coverage litigation strategy for complex insurance claims. Requires five years of insurance coverage experience and preferred law degree, with expertise in construction and labor law.

Good fit if you have five-plus years in insurance coverage analysis and experience with complex commercial claims or construction litigation.

Full job description

Description

Claims Coverage Counsel/Claims Coverage Administrator

Hybrid Work Schedule

Bedford, New Hampshire

Merchants Insurance Group is a leading Property and Casualty Insurer in the Northeast and is looking for an experienced Claims Coverage Counsel or Claims Coverage Administrator for our Claim Legal Team located in Bedford, New Hampshire.

We are seeking individuals with previous experience in insurance coverage analysis/determination/disposition for at least five years. While a law degree is preferred, we are also considering individuals without a law degree that have deep technical experience in significant and complex coverage scenarios to include New York construction/labor law and other commercial claims.

This position will be responsible for preparing coverage opinions and coverage position letters for claims involving complex coverage issues or disputes. This role will also assist claims professionals in the evaluation of risk transfer opportunities, priority of coverage, and tender strategies. Coverage Counsel/Coverage Administrator is responsible for assessing and directing coverage litigation strategy in conjunction with outside counsel and the claims professional, including developing and executing a plan to manage the coverage litigation through final resolution. This individual may also provide legal support to underwriting, product development and regulatory compliance programs (JD candidate only).

This position is responsible for both first- and third-party coverage review, analysis and decisions for all levels of claims, including those involved in litigation. In addition, the individual will provide claim, policy, regulatory and legal expertise, if or as appropriate, to all levels of management up to and including senior management. The role will also review all policy forms for updates and revisions, ensuring compliance with state regulations, as well as applicable statutes and case law. The position will also require training for all levels of claims staff in matters of policy interpretation, investigatory processes, regulatory compliance and good faith claims practices across multiple venues.

Merchants Insurance Group is rated A- (Excellent) with a stable outlook by A.M. Best and is consistently recognized as a top employer and high-performing organization. Recent honors include:

  • Ivans Spark Award for Innovation (2024–2025)
  • Named to Newsweek and Statista's America's Most Reliable Companies list (2025), ranked among the top 300 of 1,500 B2B organizations evaluated

We offer a hybrid work schedule, requiring two full days per week in the office, with flexibility to work remotely or in office the remaining days. This model supports collaboration while providing flexibility and work-life balance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Prepares coverage communication consistent with internal quality standards and applicable state regulations.
  • Works collaboratively with front-line claims professionals and managers to provide coverage analysis and preparation or review of coverage position letters for claims involving complex coverage issues or disputes.
  • Provides legal or coverage guidance to claim professionals handling declaratory judgment actions in which Merchants is a named party.
  • Directs outside counsel on litigation strategy.
  • Leads claim staff in training involving legal or coverage matters.
  • Provides claim legal support to underwriting and product development teams. Also assists in regulatory compliance programs by providing supplementary research regarding statutes and regulations impacting our business.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Juris Doctor degree preferred, with license in good standing
  • Minimum 5 years of insurance coverage experience and/or practicing attorney experience
  • Proficiency with Westlaw or other legal research applications CPCU highly desirable
  • Minimum 10 years of technical experience in complex coverage analysis
  • Prior leadership experience is highly desired
  • High degree of competency in insurance coverage analysis, policy construction, and legal research with exemplary writing skills.
  • Ability to transfer knowledge through formal and informal training with demonstrated excellent written and oral presentation skills.
  • Advanced written and oral communication skills with influence, initiative, and ability to communicate effectively across all levels across an insurance organization to include cross-departmental relationships.
  • Experience with construction and labor law litigation coverage issues related to risk transfer.
  • Proven demonstration of creative problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to lead and work in a cooperative manner.

What you'll be doing

  • Establishes and implements priorities, performance goals, and operating plans for the ServiceNow platform and application support function.
  • Leads a team of experienced technology professionals and/or first-level leaders, with accountability for team performance, talent development, and results.
  • Hires and retains talent and provides coaching, performance feedback, training, and stretch opportunities to build organizational capability.
  • Performs project coordination and business analysis on key strategic initiatives; writes requirements for and coordinates with technical resources to deliver and test those requirements.
  • Leads agile ceremonies and identifies maturity opportunities around ways of working.
  • Executes the strategy, product roadmap, governance model, and standards for the ServiceNow platform and related application portfolio.
  • Collaborates with technology and business leaders to identify, assess, and prioritize opportunities for digital transformation, automation, and enterprise service optimization.
  • Directs the design, implementation, support, and optimization of ServiceNow capabilities, including IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), and other applicable modules.
  • Ensures platform solutions meet complex business, technical, security, compliance, scalability, and operational requirements.
  • Provides inputs regarding platform investments, architecture, vendor strategy, risk, and business outcomes.
  • Directs the resolution of complex platform, application support, service delivery, and stakeholder escalation issues through completion.
  • Evaluates risks related to time, cost, scope, quality, security, and delivery and ensures appropriate mitigation plans are developed and implemented.
  • Provides inputs on the budget, licensing strategy, resource plan, vendor relationships, contracts, and expenses for the assigned area of responsibility.
  • Establishes performance measures and monitors platform health, delivery outcomes, service performance, and progress toward established objectives and key results.
  • Evaluates emerging ServiceNow capabilities, technologies, and industry practices and recommends opportunities to improve business value and operational efficiency.
  • Leads cross-functional teams in the delivery of complex enterprise platform initiatives and transformation programs.
  • Maintains knowledge of current and emerging trends, assesses their potential impact, and collaborates with management to incorporate relevant developments into current and future strategies.

What we're looking for

Must-Haves:

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in application architecture, enterprise platform management, application support, or technology leadership that directly aligns with the responsibilities of this position, including 3+ years of managerial, supervisory, and/or demonstrated leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated experience with ServiceNow platform administration, development, architecture, implementation, support, and/or governance in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Demonstrated experience executing technology strategies, architecture roadmaps, governance frameworks, and operating models.
  • Experience leading ServiceNow implementations or optimization efforts involving ITSM, ITOM, Customer Service Management (CSM), Human Resources Service Delivery (HRSD), or other applicable modules.
  • Experience managing technology vendors, licensing agreements, platform investments, budgets, contracts, and resource plans.
  • At least one ServiceNow Certification: Certified System Administrator, ServiceNow Certified Application Developer, or comparable ServiceNow certification.
  • ITIL Foundation certification or higher.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
  • ServiceNow Certified Technical Architect (CTA).
  • ITIL Managing Professional or Strategic Leader certification.
  • Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO) certification.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Experience leading enterprise digital transformation, automation, or platform modernization initiatives within a large, complex organization.
  • Experience establishing platform governance, operating models, and service management best practices at an enterprise scale.

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through March 1, 2027, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

Job.JobDescription:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for ten consecutive years as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this role is to develop, manage, and grow a profitable book of business within assigned line(s) of business, while serving as a senior-level underwriting and distribution partner to agents and internal stakeholders.

Senior Business Development Underwriters are responsible for underwriting more complex risks within assigned line(s) of business (e.g., Workers' Compensation or Commercial Package and its component coverages) and are expected to operate with a higher level of autonomy, authority, and judgment. In addition, this role plays a key leadership role in driving broader Commercial Lines growth by identifying cross-sell opportunities, promoting all Company products, and supporting agency and distribution strategy.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Underwriting & Portfolio Management

  • Underwrite, select, and price moderately complex to complex risks within assigned line(s) of business in accordance with Company guidelines

  • Maintain accountability for the profitability, growth, and retention of assigned portfolio

  • Evaluate detailed risk characteristics including operations, financials, management, and loss history

  • Exercise advanced underwriting judgment and authority to structure, price, and manage complex accounts

  • Utilize underwriting authority to apply appropriate pricing, credits/debits, deductibles, and alternative rating structures

  • Quote and explain complex pricing structures (e.g., retros, deductibles, large account programs) where applicable

  • Monitor portfolio performance and take proactive corrective action to achieve underwriting targets

  • Remain current on regulatory, rating, and coverage changes (e.g., WCIRB/NCCI, ISO/AAIS)

Business Development, Production & Distribution

  • Drive new business production and achieve growth objectives through proactive agency engagement, prospecting, and cross-sell execution

  • Develop, manage, and optimize a high-performing producer force aligned with Company strategy

  • Hold producers accountable for production, quality, and profitability expectations

  • Drive profitable sales across all Commercial Lines products, including increasing penetration of existing products and supporting new product introductions

  • Actively identify and lead cross-sell opportunities, partnering across underwriting teams to deliver total account solutions

  • Prospect, prequalify, and appoint new producers with strong alignment to target business segments

  • Set and manage production goals and performance expectations with key agency partners

  • Maintain deep knowledge of assigned territory, including competitor positioning and market dynamics

  • Influence and provide input on distribution strategy, product positioning, and market opportunities

Producer & Relationship Management

  • Serve as a lead Company representative with key and strategic agency partners

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships through regular agency engagement, presentations, and strategic planning

  • Lead complex account and pricing discussions with agents and insureds

  • Provide underwriting and distribution guidance to agents, including structuring solutions for more complex risks

  • Deliver high levels of responsiveness, service, and professionalism in all interactions

  • Present agency performance insights, growth opportunities, and strategic recommendations to internal leadership and agency partners

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Mentor and support the development of Business Development Underwriters and junior staff

  • Provide guidance on underwriting approach, agency management, and deal structure

  • Participate in training, onboarding, and knowledge sharing across the team

  • Contribute to special projects, product initiatives, and process improvements as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but is expected to mentor, influence, and provide guidance to junior team members.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Minimum 5 years underwriting experience required; 7+ years preferred, with demonstrated experience handling more complex risks and agency relationships.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Current driver's license required.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Demonstrated success in building and managing high-value agency relationships and driving profitable growth

  • Proven ability to underwrite complex risks and apply advanced underwriting judgment

  • Strong business development, negotiation, and relationship management skills

  • Ability to balance advanced underwriting discipline within assigned line(s) of business with production and cross-sell expectations across Commercial Lines

  • Ability to evaluate submissions, financials, and loss data to support complex decision-making

  • Advanced knowledge of Commercial Lines products, including Workers' Compensation and/or Commercial Package and its component coverages

  • Ability to mentor, coach, and influence others

  • Strong analytical, communication, and presentation skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

  • Role requires 50%-75% travel to meet with clients, attend industry events, and develop new business opportunities.

  • Travel is usually limited to automobile but occasional air travel is required.

  • Requires regular visits to outside locations such as producer's offices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment. Requires the ability to work 20-30% of time from home.

This description is a general statement of essential job functions and responsibilities. The position may include other duties as assigned.

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.

WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference

  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging

  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match

  • Bonus potential for all positions

  • Paid Time Off

  • Want to continue learning? We'll support you 100%


ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

Company Details

Berkley Surety is a highly professional, service-oriented surety underwriting management company, providing a full spectrum of bonds for contract, environmental, and commercial surety accounts through multiple distribution channels in both the United States and Canada. We write on behalf of W. R. Berkley Corporation member company Berkley Insurance Company, which has an A.M. Best rating of A+ (Superior). We pride ourselves on building strong relationships with our agents. We highly value the insight and expertise our agency partners bring to the table which helps us provide timely and predictable surety solutions.

Company URL: www.berkleysurety.com

Responsibilities

Serves as lead underwriter for assigned field offices as front line for either the commercial or contract departments or both. Underwrites new and renewal business with limited supervision. Supports the Head of Underwriting in balancing the needs to achieve budgeted financial results (premium volume, loss ratio, premium collections and expense management including commissions) with effective price management through sound underwriting practices in an effort to produce profitable results. Serve as lead in Book of Business reviews and assist Head of Underwriting in portfolio management. Positively interacts and collaborates with the field underwriters in assigned territory as well as other critical internal/external business associates.

Key Functions/Duties of Position: Describe the overall job responsibilities (including any decision-making authority) for this position.

  • Provide approvals, with conditions as necessary, or declinations within prescribed authority limits in a timely and understandable manner consistent with BSG guidelines and goals. Make recommendations to Head of Underwriting on a course of action for approval or declination as well as overall policy positions and underwriting guidelines.
  • Review and underwrite new and renewal business from assigned field offices in the primary line of business Analyze submitted data, determine and obtain additional information when needed. Make decisions on approvals/declinations within prescribed authority limits. On accounts or bond requests over authority limits provide recommendations on course of action in a concise and timely manner.
  • Effectively communicates recommendations and decisions with confidence, clear communication, good listening skills, professionalism, and empathy with the goal to be a trusted adviser and valued partner to all parties.
  • Plans and executes regular travel to develop and enhance new and existing producer and account relationships. Visits new and existing accounts; prepares and shares meeting agendas, obtains follow up documentation, evaluates the accounts for appropriate action.
  • Interact and collaborate with assigned field offices, Home Office colleagues, reinsurers and other critical business associates. Maintain and manage workflow, including effective communications, with assigned field office meeting all company standards and expectations.
  • Participate in BSG senior management decisions as respects developing or improving underwriting procedures, guidelines and policy.
  • Effectively evaluates bond forms and other relevant documents in an effort to assess risk.
  • Keeps Head of Underwriting apprised of issues of importance to BSG.
  • Submit Special Acceptance requests to reinsurers for large capacity accounts.
  • Develop and train other team members such as Sr. Underwriters, Underwriters, Associates Underwriters and Trainees as appropriate.

Qualifications

  • Position involves a high degree of analytical and communication skills with the capacity to communicate this knowledge and expertise to others within BSG.
  • Is considered and expert in their ability to read, analyze, discuss and interpret financial statements, bond forms, supporting documents, and government regulations and reach appropriate risk assessment conclusions.
  • Provides well developed reasons for approvals/declinations as well as recommendations in support of new and existing accounts and specific bond needs over granted authority limits.
  • Communicate difficult decisions/positions in the face of counter positions.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills with the ability to write clear and effective reports and business correspondence so that others will clearly understand the content and the intent.
  • Ability to solve practical problems and appropriately deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.
  • Organize and adjust workflow to adapt to periods of high activity and demands with the ability to work independently and in a team environment
  • Self-motivation and an out-going orientation with strong customer focus
  • Provide coaching, mentoring and leadership to others.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in the use of automation tools provided by BSG (i.e. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Lotus Notes, U/W System, etc.)

Education Requirement:

  • Minimum 4-year degree or related industry experience
  • Business/Finance/Accounting Majors preferred, but not required
  • 10 years of Surety industry or related experience required
  • Prior experience in a branch or field office management is suggested.

About this job

Assistant Underwriter at WR Berkley's Berkley Southwest division in Little Rock, performing underwriting analysis on renewal accounts and endorsements within assigned authority. The role involves evaluating risks, processing paperwork, and serving as the first point of contact for agents regarding account questions and service issues.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, strong communication skills, and experience in commercial rating or underwriting roles.

Full job description

Company Details

2025 Business Insurance Best Places to Work winner, Berkley Southwest offers commercial property and casualty products and services through independent agents in Arizona, Arkansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas. We maintain a strong local presence in each of our markets, keeping underwriting and support close to the customer.

Now more than ever, financial strength is critical to a successful, long term insurance relationship. Berkley Southwest is a member company of W. R. Berkley Corporation, a Fortune 500 company, whose insurance company subsidiaries are rated A+ (Superior) by A.M. Best. #LI-LD1 #LI-HYBRID

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

Contributes to Company financial objectives in partnership with their Underwriting and Sales account teams. Responsibilities include monitoring renewal pipeline, underwriting renewal business, and processing endorsements within established authority and in consideration of risk, appetite, and pricing guidelines.

Key Functions/Duties of Position: Describe the overall job responsibilities (including any decision-making authority) for this position.

  • Performs underwriting analysis on low complexity renewal accounts and endorsements within assigned authority by evaluating exposures, financial stability, historical loss data, and potential hazards. Refers renewals outside of authority to the Underwriter or Manager.
  • Applies recommended pricing to underwritten accounts and discusses significant rate changes with the Underwriter and Regional Sales Director to determine the best approach for agent communication.
  • Completes cursory review of new business submissions for acceptability when requested. Gathers key underwriting reports and required information to support risk evaluation.
  • Serves as the account team's first point of contact with agents regarding missing information, service issues, billing questions, and general inquiries.
  • Orders and reviews loss control reports based on underwriting guidelines or Underwriter request. Follows up on open recommendations.
  • Completes required regulatory and internal filings accurately and timely.
  • Reviews premium audit changes and requests updates to exposures as directed.
  • Evaluates incoming account correspondence and determines appropriate action—autonomously within authority or by referral to Underwriter or leadership.
  • Establishes and maintains regular communication channels with underwriting, sales, and support teams. Stays informed on relevant account developments and industry trends.
  • Participates in process improvement initiatives, including automation and data integration efforts, to enhance underwriting efficiency and accuracy.
  • Assists in onboarding and training of new team members.
  • Communicates and interacts with agents in a professional and responsive manner.
  • Other duties and projects as assigned.

Education Requirement

  • Bachelor's degree in related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
  • Commercial rating experience or experience in underwriting role preferred.
  • Advanced insurance education is desired, such as Associate in General Insurance, Kaplan Insurance courses, CPCU etc.

Qualifications

  • Verbal and written communication skills are necessary to interact professionally with all internal and external contacts. Ability to articulate clearly, concisely, and deliver difficult messages thoughtfully.
  • Solid organizational skills with the ability to handle multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Strong computer skills with knowledge of MS Excel and Word.
  • Able to thrive in a fast-paced environment.
  • Learning agility – willing and able to learn from experiences and new situations.
  • Ability to project a warm and friendly manner in all business contacts and maintain a professional relationship with co-workers, agency contacts, and the general public.
  • Aligns and practices our C.A.R.I.N.G. Values (Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Integrity, Nurturing Growth, Generosity)

Sponsorship Details

Sponsorship not Offered for this Role

Company Details

Berkley Mid-Atlantic Group (BMAG) is a property and casualty insurance provider serving the Mid-Atlantic. We are a member of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the largest commercial lines property and casualty insurance holding companies in the United States. With the resources of a large Fortune 500® corporation and the ability to operate with the closeness and flexibility of a small company, we exclusively work with select independent agents to insure the future of business.

Our culture is one that empowers employees to question the status quo and seek innovative ways to continue to exceed the expectations of our customers. We practice collaboration, creativity, and teamwork on a daily basis, with a commitment to innovation and high performance.

Company URL: https://www.wrbmag.com/

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

Lead the enterprise actuarial, analytics, and portfolio intelligence agenda so that pricing, reserving, capital, reinsurance, planning, and growth decisions consistently improve risk-adjusted returns. The Chief Actuarial Officer translates complex risk into clear choices, builds trusted decision systems, and develops the next generation of actuarial and analytical leadership.

Reporting to the President, the Chief Actuarial Officer is a member of the executive leadership team and the senior actuarial voice for the operating unit. The role owns the integrity and strategic application of actuarial work across pricing, reserving, forecasting, portfolio management, capital and reinsurance support, regulatory matters, and data-enabled decision making. The leader partners closely with the President, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Claims Officer, distribution leaders, and corporate actuarial stakeholders.

Over the five-year horizon, success requires moving beyond production of actuarial indications and reports toward an integrated decision-intelligence model. The Chief Actuarial Officer will establish governed, explainable, repeatable analytics; accelerate feedback loops; identify emerging risk early; and enable leaders to act with confidence while preserving actuarial standards, sound judgment, and appropriate human oversight.

Enterprise Strategy and Executive Decision Support

  • Serve as a strategic partner to the President and executive team, connecting actuarial insight to operating strategy, growth priorities, geographic expansion, product appetite, expense management, and risk-adjusted return objectives.
  • Frame choices through scenarios, ranges, sensitivities, trade-offs, and leading indicators rather than relying only on point estimates or historical summaries.
  • Own the actuarial narrative for quarterly results, annual operating plans, reforecasts, and corporate reviews, with clear explanations of performance drivers and corrective actions.
  • Create a multi-year actuarial and analytics roadmap aligned with enterprise priorities, technology capabilities, talent needs, and governance expectations.

Pricing, Portfolio Steering, and Product Economics

  • Lead pricing adequacy, rate-level, trend, loss-cost, retention, mix, and new-business analyses across Small Commercial and Middle Market package products, Commercial Auto, Workers Compensation, Umbrella, and other assigned lines.
  • Build portfolio steering capabilities that connect indicated need, achieved rate, underwriting action, exposure change, retention, claims emergence, and profitability at actionable segment levels.
  • Partner with underwriting and distribution leadership to define profitable growth guardrails, market and segment priorities, and measurable action plans.
  • Provide actuarial leadership for product development, coverage changes, filings, and experimentation, including disciplined test design, monitoring, and post-implementation evaluation.
  • Advance risk segmentation and price optimization practices while protecting fairness, explainability, regulatory compliance, and sound underwriting judgment.

Reserving, Financial Insight, and Prospective Risk

  • Own the operating unit reserving process and recommendations, including methods, assumptions, diagnostics, documentation, peer review readiness, and communication of uncertainty.
  • Connect reserve analysis with claims operations, underwriting actions, social and economic inflation, legal environment changes, catastrophe activity, and shifts in exposure or mix.
  • Develop prospective views of loss emergence and profitability using actual-versus-expected diagnostics, early-warning indicators, scenario analysis, and stress testing.
  • Partner with Finance on premium, loss, expense, cash-flow, and earnings forecasts; annual planning; and explanations of material variances.
  • Maintain readiness for auditors, regulators, rating agencies, corporate actuarial reviews, and other authorized oversight.

Capital, Reinsurance, Catastrophe, and Emerging Risk

  • Provide actuarial insight for capital allocation, risk appetite, volatility, accumulation, and return-on-equity decisions at line, segment, product, and portfolio levels.
  • Partner on ceded reinsurance strategy, structure evaluation, renewal analytics, exposure data quality, and assessment of retained volatility.
  • Advance catastrophe and climate-related risk analysis appropriate to the portfolio, including geographic concentration, hazard change, model uncertainty, and mitigation opportunities.
  • Establish a repeatable emerging-risk process covering cyber, autonomous and connected technologies, supply-chain disruption, litigation and social inflation, economic regime shifts, and other material exposures.
  • Translate stress and scenario results into practical underwriting, claims, product, reinsurance, and growth recommendations.

Data, AI, Decision Systems, and Model Governance

  • Own the actuarial data and analytics strategy in partnership with technology, data, underwriting, claims, finance, compliance, and corporate stakeholders.
  • Create governed data products and a consistent source of truth for pricing, reserving, plan, actual-versus-expected, rate and retention, exposure, and portfolio performance reporting.
  • Sponsor responsible use of predictive analytics, machine learning, generative AI, and automation where they improve speed, quality, insight, or scalability.
  • Implement model inventory, ownership, validation, documentation, change control, performance monitoring, bias and fairness review, explainability, access controls, and human-judgment standards proportionate to model risk.
  • Ensure automated outputs are reproducible, auditable, secure, and appropriately reviewed before they influence material decisions.
  • Modernize workflows to shorten decision cycles and redirect actuarial capacity from manual production toward interpretation, challenge, and action.

Qualifications

Required

  • Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS).
  • Bachelor's degree in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, economics, data science, finance, or another relevant quantitative field, or equivalent experience.
  • Significant progressive property and casualty actuarial experience, including leadership of pricing and reserving work and senior-level influence on business decisions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading teams, developing talent, managing change, and partnering across underwriting, claims, finance, technology, compliance, and distribution.
  • Ability to communicate complex analysis, uncertainty, and strategic choices clearly to executive and nontechnical audiences.
  • Working knowledge of applicable actuarial standards, insurance regulation, rate filing considerations, financial reporting, and model governance.

Preferred

  • Membership in the American Academy of Actuaries (MAAA).
  • Experience with commercial package, Commercial Auto, Workers Compensation, Umbrella, Small Commercial, or Middle Market portfolios.
  • Experience with reinsurance, catastrophe modeling, capital analysis, portfolio optimization, and emerging risks.
  • Fluency with modern actuarial and analytical ecosystems such as SQL, Python or R, visualization tools, cloud data platforms, and governed AI-enabled workflows.
  • Experience modernizing actuarial processes, implementing model governance, or building enterprise decision-support capabilities.

Leadership Competencies

  • Strategic enterprise thinking: Connects actuarial evidence to long-term competitive advantage, capital deployment, and operating priorities.
  • Commercial and underwriting acumen: Understands how product, appetite, distribution, claims, expense, and price interact to create sustainable returns.
  • Quality decision making: Balances rigor and speed; distinguishes what is known, uncertain, assumed, and actionable.
  • Influence and communication: Creates clarity, earns trust, constructively challenges, and turns analysis into commitment and action.
  • Technology and AI stewardship: Recognizes high-value use cases and establishes proportionate governance, controls, and human oversight.
  • Talent multiplication: Builds successors, broadens capabilities, and creates an environment where diverse perspectives improve decisions.
  • Execution and accountability: Sets priorities, simplifies work, assigns ownership, monitors outcomes, and closes the loop.

About this job

Senior Analyst in Investment Accounting at AIG responsible for accounting and reporting on over $95 billion in invested assets. Manages monthly and quarterly accounting close for international entities, prepares investment disclosures for regulatory filings, and coordinates with business units on new investment transactions.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of investment accounting experience, know GAAP and investment products, and can work with Excel and multiple teams.

Full job description

Who we are

AIG, Inc. is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world's most far-reaching property casualty networks. AIG, Inc. (“AIG”) offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network. Customers value AIG's strong capital position, extensive risk management and claims experience and its ability to be a market leader in critical lines of the insurance business.


Corporate Finance - Investment Accounting

The Investment Accounting group at AIG is responsible for the accounting and reporting for AIG's Invested Assets of over $95 billion a comprised primarily of fixed maturity securities and includes private equity, hedge funds, commercial/residential loans and equity securities. In addition, AIG's derivative portfolio consists primarily of foreign exchange derivatives but also includes interest rate and other derivative instruments.


The Investment Accounting group's specific responsibilities include reconciliation of transactional data from various sub-ledgers to the general ledger and ultimately AIG's financial statements as well as all related external reporting for investments (10Q/K, Financial Supplement, STAT Audited Financials, Investment NAIC reporting and various government regulatory reports). AIG has multiple legal entities around the globe.


The team is also responsible for establishing the accounting for new transactions or new investment products, implementation of new GAAP and STAT accounting standards as it relates to invested assets, the implementation of new accounting systems as it relates to invested assets, and management of the risks, controls and AIG audit as it relates to investments and supporting Investment FP&A.


Responsibilities

  • Execute and manage accounting processes related to the monthly and quarterly accounting close to ensure accuracy of AIG's invested assets data of certain international entities
  • Support the preparation of certain Investment disclosures for AIG 10Q/K and Financial Supplement, including as appropriate the Investment, Lending, Fair Value, VIE Footnotes and Investment MD&A
  • Assist with the implementation of process improvements and new systems, in coordination with other areas of the department/organization
  • Point of contact and support for the various business unit and corporate controllers
  • Coordinate with various areas in the organization to develop an understanding of new investment transactions and to provide guidance/support that ensures the accounting results from these investments are accurately recorded in the AIG ledgers
  • Perform ad-hoc analytical requests

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance
  • At least 3 years' experience in accounting and reporting for investment products
  • Understanding of investment products and accounting treatment for fixed maturity, equity, cash equivalent and alternative investments
  • Working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principle (GAAP) and the recording of investments-related journal entries
  • Experience with foreign currency remeasurement and translation
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience performing investment data analysis including commentary
  • High level of competency using Microsoft Excel including pivot tables and formulas to create/manage investment data and perform analysis
  • Ability to work collaboratively with teams in multiple locations
  • Ability to balance multiple projects at once, to prioritize appropriately, and to approach the work with a sense of urgency and strong attention to detail to produce high quality results in a time sensitive environment
  • Team-player mindset geared towards process improvements and the implementation of accounting controls to ensure consistency and data quality of the team's financial output
  • High level of motivation and initiative, ability to work independently, including strong organizational skills
  • Comfort level working within a dynamic and complex organizational structure
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to maintain relationships at all levels within the organization
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff, peers, and other external and internal audiences
  • Computer proficiency with a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, database experience a plus

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced Tax and Treasury Technology Leader to develop and implement the worldwide technology strategy and roadmap for tax and treasury systems, data, integrations, and digital capabilities. The person in this position brings expertise across direct and indirect tax, tax provision and compliance! Also transfer pricing, cash and liquidity management, payments, banking connectivity, debt and investments, foreign exchange, data and analytics, Agentic AI, and workflow automation. Translate priorities into secure, resilient, well-governed, and data-driven technology solutions.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world! As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Serve as the senior technology leader responsible for both tax functions and treasury management, owning the strategy, architecture, roadmap, delivery, and operational health of the global technology ecosystem.

Be responsible for the portfolio of technologies, including tax provision and reporting: Global tax provision, effective tax rate, deferred tax, tax accounting, disclosure, and close-support solutions. Direct tax compliance: Corporate income tax, withholding tax, statutory reporting, return preparation, filing, and jurisdictional compliance platforms. Indirect tax: VAT, GST, sales and use tax, determination, calculation, invoicing, reporting, reconciliation, and e-filing technologies. Transfer pricing: Intercompany policy, calculation, documentation, operational transfer pricing, and country-by-country reporting solutions.

Oversee treasury management: Cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, bank account administration, payments, collections, in-house banking, netting, and reconciliation platforms. Financial risk and capital markets: Foreign exchange, interest rate and commodity risk, hedging, debt, investments, guarantees, and associated accounting and valuation capabilities.

The person in this role will be responsible for banking connectivity and payments: Bank portals, host-to-host connections, APIs, SWIFT connectivity, payment factories, file transmission, fraud controls, and payment status monitoring. Information analysis, computational insights, and artificial intelligence: Financial and liquidity data products, governed data models, dashboards, predictive insights, scenario modeling, intelligent automation, and Agentic AI capabilities

Ensure end-to-end process integrity and data consistency across tax determination, provision, compliance, statutory reporting, payments, cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, bank reconciliation, hedging, debt, and investment processes.

Partner closely with senior Tax, Treasury, Finance, Accounting, Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Data, Cybersecurity, and Technology leaders to align platform capabilities with business priorities and regulatory obligations.

Define and maintain the platform governance model for the technology solutions supporting Tax and Treasury functions, including demand intake, prioritization, architecture, security, change control, release management, access governance, and communication.

Take charge of the IT service model across application support, incident and problem management, monitoring, batch and interface operations, disaster recovery, business continuity, vendor support, and service-level performance. Oversee evaluation, adoption, and rollout of new platform features and releases; perform impact assessments and guide configuration, integration, controls, testing, deployment, and hypercare.

Drive adoption and support for new capabilities, ensuring teams are equipped to use systems, data, analytics, and AI effectively in day-to-day operations.

Champion data quality, lineage, standardization, retention, security, and controls across the landscape; establish clear ownership and collaborate with Data, Risk, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance teams.

Complete the AI strategy related to Tax and Treasury, prioritizing responsible use cases such as anomaly detection, reconciliation support, cash forecasting, scenario analysis, document intelligence, research assistance, workflow orchestration, and control monitoring.

Ensure effective integrations and data flows between Tax and Treasury platforms and adjacent ecosystems, including ERP, HR and payroll, procurement, billing, banking networks, market data, consolidation, regulatory reporting, and enterprise data platforms.

This role goes well beyond maintaining current tools. You will:

  • AI-enabled automation and advanced analytics for cash forecasting, tax data preparation, reconciliations, exception management, regulatory change analysis, and aiding decision-making
  • Real-time and API-enabled banking, payment, and data connectivity, with resilient security and control frameworks

  • Your work will directly support tax compliance, liquidity, financial risk management, payment integrity, operational resilience, and better enterprise decisions through technology, data, AI, and process excellence.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

Extensive experience, typically 7+ years, leading Tax, Treasury, Finance, or corporate technology portfolios in a global, matrixed organization.

  • Deep hands-on and strategic experience with:
  • Tax provision, tax accounting, direct tax compliance, indirect tax, transfer pricing, and statutory reporting technologies
  • Treasury management systems supporting cash, liquidity, payments, bank account management, debt, investments, foreign exchange, hedging, and reconciliation
  • Bank connectivity and payment technologies, including SWIFT, host-to-host, APIs, payment files, bank portals, and fraud-control capabilities
  • ERP, consolidation, sub ledger, payroll, procurement, billing, market data, data platform, and regulatory integrations that support Tax and Treasury processes
  • Data architecture, master and reference data, data lineage, reporting, analytics, and data product operating models
  • AI, machine learning, workflow automation, document intelligence, and agentic solutions, with responsible AI and governance controls
  • Proven success leading complex, multi-year transformations, global deployments, process standardization, platform rationalization, and operating model change across Tax and Treasury.
  • Experience establishing reliable application support and service management for time critical close, filing, payment, cash, and market-facing processes.
  • Experience driving adoption of AI, automation, and analytics in Tax and Treasury while maintaining appropriate human review, security, auditability, and regulatory compliance.
  • Solid background partnering with senior business collaborators to translate Tax/Treasury strategies, risks, controls, and performance measures into technology roadmaps and investment priorities.

Leadership & collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing, global teams across business, technology, data, architecture, delivery, and operations skills. Excellent collaborator management and interpersonal abilities, with the ability to work with senior leaders in Tax, Treasury, Finance, Accounting, Risk, Compliance, Audit, Data, and Technology.

Experience managing portfolio prioritization, budgeting, capacity, resource planning, and delivery across concurrent programs, enhancements, regulatory commitments, and operational needs.

Strong vendor and partner management skills, including contracts, performance, service levels, product roadmaps, security requirements, implementation accountability, and risk allocation.

Strategic problem solver who can connect Tax and Treasury technology, data, controls, and AI capabilities to outcomes such as compliance, liquidity visibility, risk reduction, payment integrity, operational resilience, and improved efficiency.

Demonstrated experience identifying and implementing automation, AI/ML, advanced analytics, and agentic workflows in controlled financial processes. Ability to define a governed data strategy that improves data quality, accessibility, lineage, reuse, and decision support across jurisdictions and business divisions.

Comfortable operating in a matrixed, global environment, balancing enterprise standardization with local tax, banking, legal, regulatory, and market requirements.

Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Business, or a related field.

An advanced degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Tax, Information Systems, Data, or a related field, or equivalent experience, is preferred.

Job Description

Partnering closely with Finance, Operations, Technology, and regional collaborators, this role will lead major PSA initiatives from discovery through implementation, stabilization, and ongoing support in a global, matrixed environment!

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world!

As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

  • Implement the vision, roadmap, governance, and lifecycle management of Workday PSA, aligning platform capabilities with global finance, order-to-cash, project delivery, and operational priorities.
  • Serve as the enterprise design authority for Workday PSA. Lead solution architecture across Projects, Project Billing, Customer Contracts, Customer Accounts, Time Tracking, Expenses, Revenue Management, Accounts Receivable, and Collections.
  • Lead technical solutioning for major PSA initiatives from discovery and process design through configuration, testing, deployment, hypercare, and transition to steady state support.
  • Translate complex business requirements into scalable Workday configurations, business processes, security designs, integrations, and operating procedures.
  • Architect end-to-end professional services processes that support: Project, contract, customer, and worktag setup. Time and expense capture, approval, and corrections.
  • Billing schedules, billable transactions, invoice creation, adjustments, and special handling
  • Revenue schedules, revenue recognition, intercompany activity, and accounting alignment
  • Accounts receivable, cash application, collections, write-offs, and customer account management
  • Utilization, project performance, margin, operational, and financial reporting
  • Define architectural standards and guardrails for configuration, business processes, calculated fields, custom validations, reporting, security, and data governance.
  • Partner with Workday Financials and HCM architects to ensure PSA designs align with the broader Workday platform, enterprise architecture, chart of accounts, organizational structures, worker data, and time entry requirements.
  • Architect and oversee integrations between Workday PSA and adjacent platforms, including CRM, contract lifecycle management, ERP, tax, banking, data warehouses, reporting, payroll, and other enterprise applications.
  • Own data integrity and control design across customer, contract, project, worker, time, billing, revenue, invoice, and receivables data, with clear reconciliation and auditability.
  • Support the Workday security build, including security groups, domain and business process policies, role assignments, access controls, and separation of responsibilities.
  • Lead reporting and analytics architecture using Workday report writing, calculated fields, dashboards, worksheets, and downstream data platforms to support operational and executive decision making.
  • Evaluate Workday releases and new PSA capabilities, assess business and technical impacts, oversee regression testing, and guide adoption decisions.
  • Provide support for complex production issues, root-cause analysis, defect resolution, and business critical support while strengthening preventive controls.
