The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a PPLI Client Experience Specialist to support the Retail Solutions business in a work from home environment.

Background Details
As a PPLI Client Experience Specialist, you will manage the end-to-end administration of the Private Placement Life Insurance (PPLI) policy life cycle, including new business and case management, forms management, policy issuance, policy delivery, post-issue transactions, incoming requests and inquiries, and the death claim process. Serving as a key point of contact for PPLI Sales, Underwriting, Product, specialty brokers, and other business partners, you will guide stakeholders through case requirements, status updates, and next steps while ensuring new business submissions are accurate, complete, and compliant.

In partnership with Underwriting and Product teams, you will support case approvals, policy issuance, IDF implementation, planning, and funding activities. You will also support operational functions across PPLI and Executive Benefits products (COLI, BOLI, and ICOLI) by processing premium payments, renewals, fund transfers, and related transactions. Additionally, you will maintain PPLI forms and coordinate regulatory updates with Compliance, Legal, and State Filing teams, resolve service and reporting issues, identify operational risks and process improvement opportunities, take the lead on defining workflows and maintaining procedures and reporting, and contribute to departmental initiatives that enhance efficiency, service delivery, and business outcomes.

This is a collaborative, fast-paced role where priorities can change quickly, and success depends on building strong relationships with sophisticated brokers and quickly learning complex life insurance products and investment options. If this sounds like a role for you, please read on!

What you'll be doing

  • You will own the end-to-end PPLI policy life cycle, from new business and case management and policy issuance through all post-issue transaction processing and incoming requests and inquiries, to the death claim process, while building and maintaining strong, trusted relationships with sophisticated brokers, distribution partners, underwriters, and key internal stakeholders.
  • You will serve as a primary point of contact for PPLI Sales, Underwriting, Product, specialty brokers, and other partners, providing clear, proactive guidance on case requirements, status, and next steps.
  • You will review new business submissions for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established requirements and resolve routine discrepancies before advancing cases.
  • You will collaborate with Underwriting to support case approval and complete policy issuance activities within the new business platform. You will also coordinate with Product and other partners to support IDF implementation, planning, funding, and related case activities.\
  • You will maintain PPLI forms and coordinate updates with Compliance, Legal, and State Filing to support timely and accurate regulatory submissions.
  • You will perform assigned PPLI post-issue and Executive Benefits operational activities, including premium payments, renewals, fund transfers, and related transactions.
  • You will research and resolve challenging but well-defined service, transaction, and reporting issues using established procedures, reports, and available resources, escalating exceptions as appropriate.
  • You will identify case-level risks, financial implications, process gaps, or service concerns and communicate findings and recommend next steps to appropriate partners.
  • You will lead process improvement by identifying efficiencies, defining workflows, maintaining and updating procedures, and producing reporting, while also contributing to team projects and supporting the implementation of departmental and enterprise changes.
  • You will stay flexible and collaborative in a fast-paced, changing environment, reprioritizing and pivoting quickly as case needs and business priorities shift.

What we're looking for

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's)
  • 1+ Years of experience in a client-, broker-, or partner-facing role in a service, operations, or case management environment; life insurance new business/case management experience is a plus but not required
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and collaboration skills, with a proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships with sophisticated brokers
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and multitask while maintaining strict attention to detail, and comfort working in a fast-paced environment where priorities change quickly
  • Ability to evaluate information and data trends, solve challenging but non-complex problems, apply sound judgment to draw conclusions and act effectively in situations with limited standardization.
  • Interest in process and continuous improvement, with the ability to define workflows, document procedures, and create reporting
  • Ability to learn complex life insurance products and related investment options quickly
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through November 30, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

What's it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

Job.JobTitle: Assistant General Counsel, Bad Faith Litigation
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $171,000 to $212,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: New York, NY

About this job

Assistant General Counsel managing bad faith and extra-contractual litigation for AIG's insurance claims organization. Requires 7+ years of law firm litigation experience, J.D., and state bar admission to handle an active docket and advise claim handlers.

Good fit if you have litigation experience with depositions, motions, and strong writing skills, and want to work in insurance claims management.

Full job description

Who we are:

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide financial security.

Get to know the business:

AIG's Global Legal, Compliance, Regulatory and Government Affairs (GLCR) department is comprised of attorneys and other professionals providing high-quality advisory and transactional support with integrity and objectivity across all parts of the organization. The team ensures an operating environment that minimizes legal, regulatory and reputational risks, complies with all laws and regulations, and enforces AIG policies and procedures.

This is a global, diverse and award-winning team that has been recognized for its leadership and innovative solutions. You will also be eligible to participate in AIG's award-winning pro bono program.

AIG's GLCR department is looking for an experienced attorney to serve as an Assistant General Counsel managing bad faith litigation and providing advice to AIG's claims organization in the New York office.  

Specific Responsibilities Include:

The primary purpose of the position is to manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra-contractual matters arising from the handling of claims under casualty, financial lines, property and specialty policies issued to commercial and personal lines insureds. The attorney will also be responsible for providing timely advice to claim handlers in order to avoid and/or mitigate extra-contractual exposures.

  • Manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra contractual matters;
  • Develop resolution strategies and make recommendations to senior management;
  • Direct and supervise outside counsel with respect to the implementation of litigation strategies;
  • Ensure that high-quality written work product is filed on behalf of the AIG member insurance companies;
  • Collaborate with business partners in the claims organization on strategic decisions and provide timely advice to claim handlers to avoid and/or mitigate bad faith exposure;
  • Prepare and conduct regularly scheduled training presentations to claim handlers.
  • On occasion and as necessary, travel for mediations, trials;

Education / Experience:

  • Attorney with at least 7+ years of law firm litigation experience strongly preferred;
  • J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials;
  • Admitted to practice in at least one state;
  • Litigation experience should include preparing witnesses for, taking, and defending depositions, as well as drafting and arguing dispositive motions;
  • Trial experience very useful but not required
  • In-house experience with another insurer is also useful but not required.

To succeed in this position, the successful candidate must possess the following skills:

  • Strong initiative and work ethic;
  • Focused attention to detail and honed analytical skills;
  • Superior oral and written communication skills;
  • Strong interpersonal skills;
  • Ability to be a self-starter and work independently;
  • Flexibility and a willingness to adapt to changing needs of the organization and/or business clients;
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment;
  • Ability to deliver creative and well-reasoned plans to resolve challenges and to execute on such plans;
  • Ability to thrive in an environment where coordination and teamwork is a priority while also being committed to individual accountability and results;
  • Willingness to be mentored and trained to meet the needs of the organization; and
  • Sound legal and business judgment.

At AIG, we have a 100-year legacy of working to make the world a better place. And that begins with our employees. We're proud to offer a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most – your health care, savings, financial protection, and wellbeing. Through a wide variety of programs and initiatives, we invest in each employee, seeking to ensure that our people are not only respected as individuals, but also truly valued for their unique perspectives.

In addition, we're proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits

At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike.

Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters

At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what's most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world's most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.

SUMMARY

The Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Specialist supports the execution of the organization's search engine optimization strategy to increase online visibility, drive qualified organic traffic, and improve overall website performance. Reporting to Director of SEO this role is hands-on and focused on Search and AI discoverability while creating a positive user and client experience across the website. The SEO partners with the PR team on SEO-related media outreach and link building efforts, as well as the broader marketing team to ensure SEO best practices are consistently applied, while contributing insights that inform strategy and drive measurable growth.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Conduct keyword research, competitor analysis, and site audits to identify opportunities for new content or additional SEO/AEO optimization.

Implement on-page optimizations including title tags, meta descriptions, header tags, internal linking, and schema markup.

Develop content optimization efforts across landing pages, blogs, and multimedia assets to improve visibility and engagement.

Research, write and optimize clear, user-focused website copy and though leadership for B2B audiences. Use keyword and performance data, along with an understanding of ICPs/personas and the buyer journey, to address audience needs at each stage and improve visibility in traditional search and AI engines.

Partner with subject matter experts to develop accurate, useful content, translating their expertise into clear copy aligned with audience needs, search intent, and business goals.

Assist in the creation and management of SEO and Search Engine Marketing (SEM) campaigns across platforms.

Track, measure, and report on SEO KPIs such as rankings, traffic, engagement, and conversions.

Surface actionable insights to the Director based on trend analysis.

Utilize tools such as GA4, GSC, BrightEdge to monitor performance and surface insights.

Maintain dashboards and reporting accuracy across SEO and paid channels.

Stay current on search engine algorithm updates, SEO trends, and emerging tools.

Experiment with new tactics, including generative AI-driven search and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), under the guidance of the Director of SEO.

Contribute ideas to improve processes, tools, and outcomes for SEO initiatives.

Partner with manager and broader marketing team to ensure SEO is integrated into all digital projects.

Support campaign planning, execution, and reporting to align with business goals.

Assist in testing landing page templates, modules, and content variations to optimize user experience and search performance.

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field , or equivalent combination of education and experience

Three (3) or more years of experience in SEO or digital marketing with a proven track record of improving website rankings and traffic.

Three (3) or more years of content writing experience, preferably in a B2B environment

SKILLS

Knowledge of on-page optimization (title tags, meta descriptions, internal linking, schema markup)

Proficiency with SEO tools such as Google Search Console, Google Analytics (GA4), BrightEdge, SEMrush, Ahrefs, Moz or equivalent

Knowledge of technical SEO (site speed, mobile optimization, crawlability, Core Web Vitals)

Detail-oriented and able to manage multiple projects simultaneously

Strong written and verbal communication skills

Job.JobTitle: Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as the Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

As the North America Head of Financial Lines Technical Claims you will report to the North America Head of Financial Lines Claims, and be responsible for technical oversight of Financial Lines Claims in North America. You will be responsible for driving Claims technical excellence and be a recognized subject matter expert within and outside of the Claims function in the relevant business lines. You will collaborate directly with senior claims, underwriting, actuarial, legal and compliance leaders to ensure effective development and management of strategic objectives and policies for those lines of business, and be responsible for leading the development of clear and effective strategies for resolving high complexity and severity claims, for identifying claim and coverage trends, and for driving technical excellence and internal business partner communication within specific business lines. You are also responsible for setting strategic vision for the approach to and resolution of these claims, driving claims consistency by product, partnering with underwriting on trends and exposures and working with actuarial to develop a robust and consistent approach to claims exposure assessment and reserving.

  • Providing oversight of complex, high severity claims across D&O, E&O/MPL, Fiduciary, Fidelity, Financial Institutions, Employment Practices Liability products, focusing on overall claims consistency, thought leadership, best practices, lessons learned and technical trainings across all regions and products in North America.
  • Monitoring of, and escalation/referral for guidance, direction and authority on, matters involving high severity and/or complex coverage issues and matters involving high profile insureds or events or of significant impact.
  • Active involvement in highest severity or high profile claims, at the direction of senior claims management, including direct involvement in negotiation of settlements with Insureds and Claimants, based on sensitivity, severity, complexity or age of matter, as necessary.
  • Assisting the Head of Financial Lines Claims with the effective management and implementation of strategic claim objectives and policies for a line of business, in accordance with the company's strategic plans. ·
  • Claims trend and legal development identification, analysis and reporting, including regular LOB reports for senior claims management and internal business partners and similar LOB-specific reporting; coordination with IT/claims data functions to ensure necessary/correct data views.
  • Providing oversight and management of systemic and quasi-systemic claim issues that cross all lines of business; generating periodic reports and updates regarding exposures to senior claims, actuarial and underwriting management.
  • Reviewing, developing and/or delivering technical claims training content; developing a formalized “lessons learned” capability fit for purpose for Financial Lines to ensure claim insights are communicated consistently with stakeholders in Underwriting and Actuarial.
  • Communication of, education and training regarding existing or developing coverage issues to ensure accuracy and consistency of position/approach.

What you'll need to succeed:

  • Extensive knowledge in several diverse disciplines or recognized professional fields, i.e. commercial insurance policy coverage and controlling laws, litigation management governance/control and comprehensive understanding of critical issues in other related areas.
  • Advanced communication skills which are critical to building consensus across areas of influence (external and/or internal relationships), team, and/or matrix environment.
  • Superior leadership and management skills demonstrating integrity and professionalism.
  • Proven ability to drive results by identifying and resolving significant problems within scope of responsibility.
  • Extensive knowledge of the insurance industry, its products and services.
  • 15+ of related work experience with commercial or Risk Management claims including technical claim handling, coverage interpretation, and claim/litigation.
  • The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor's Degree with a Master's Degree or JD preferred.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you.


For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $250,000- $315,000. In addition, the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Job Description

Posting Description

Surety Account Manager, Processor Team Lead

Summary

The Surety Account Manager is responsible for managing client relationships, overseeing surety account service activities, and providing leadership and direction to the Surety Processing team. This role serves as the primary point of contact for clients, carriers, and internal stakeholders while ensuring the accurate and timely issuance, renewal, and servicing of surety bonds. The Surety Account Manager drives operational excellence through workflow management, quality control, staff development, and process improvement while delivering exceptional client service and maintaining strong carrier relationships.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients, surety carriers, producers, and internal business partners.
  • Participate in client meetings and provide consultative support regarding bond programs, renewals, and service needs.
  • Lead the review of surety proposals, bond documentation, renewal information, and carrier source documents for accuracy and completeness.
  • Oversee the day-to-day operations of the Surety Processing team, including workflow distribution, prioritization, and quality assurance.
  • Provide guidance, training, and mentorship to surety processors to support performance, productivity, and professional development.
  • Monitor departmental service standards and ensure timely completion of bond issuance, renewals, endorsements, cancellations, and reinstatements.
  • Manage and maintain client records, bond schedules, policy information, and supporting documentation within agency management systems and carrier portals.
  • Review and approve bond requests, renewal processing, invoices, finance agreements, and related surety transactions.
  • Coordinate the issuance of new and renewal bonds, including bid, performance, payment, maintenance, and miscellaneous bonds.
  • Track bond renewals and ensure all required documentation and billing information is processed accurately and within established service timelines.
  • Address client service issues, billing inquiries, and bond-related concerns while collaborating with carriers and internal departments as needed.
  • Assist with process development, workflow enhancements, and operational efficiency initiatives to improve overall team performance.
  • Maintain compliance with agency procedures, carrier requirements, and regulatory guidelines.
  • Support special projects and departmental initiatives as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of surety bonds, bond administration processes, and surety industry practices.
  • Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to motivate, coach, and develop team members.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong client relationship management and customer service skills.
  • Ability to make sound independent decisions and exercise professional judgment.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with clients, carriers, producers, and internal teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Experience working with agency management systems and carrier platforms preferred.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities, processes, and technology.

Education and Experience

  • Associate's degree or equivalent experience required; Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • 3+ years of insurance industry experience, including surety account management, surety operations, or related client service experience.
  • Previous leadership, supervisory, or team lead experience preferred.
  • Experience managing bond issuance, renewals, and surety servicing activities preferred.

Certificates, Licenses, and Registration

  • Property & Casualty Insurance License required or obtainable within 30 days of hire.
  • Surety-specific industry designations or advanced insurance certifications are a plus.

What we Offer:

We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $75,000.00 – $85,000.00. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives.

The Central Reserving team is seeking a highly analytical and innovative professional to help advance our reserving capabilities through the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and advanced analytics. This role will be responsible for developing tools and models that identify and quantify key drivers of claims outcomes, uncover insights into loss development behavior, and enhance reserving accuracy across multiple lines of business.

In addition, this role will support the analysis, determination, and reporting of reserves for Extra-Contractual Obligations (ECO) and Corporate-Level Unallocated Loss Expense (ULE).

The successful candidate will partner with reserving actuaries, claims professionals, data scientists, and business leaders to transform complex datasets into actionable insights, modern analytical tools, and next-generation reserving methodologies.

This position offers a unique opportunity to influence the future of actuarial reserving by combining traditional actuarial expertise with cutting-edge AI and advanced analytics capabilities.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support the quarterly process of determining the appropriate amount of IBNR to be booked across assigned reserving segments, including Extra-Contractual Obligations (ECO) and Corporate-Level Unallocated Loss Expense (ULE).
  • Analyze information to determine, document, and communicate the adequacy of loss and loss expense reserves.
  • Develop and apply advanced analytics, predictive modeling, and AI-based tools to identify and quantify key drivers of claims outcomes, improve reserve estimates, and generate business insights into loss development behavior.
  • Research, develop, and enhance reserving methodologies and models to improve reserve accuracy and support actuarial transformation initiatives.
  • Analyze and monitor loss development trends, claims emergence patterns, and relevant industry, regulatory, and operational changes, and effectively communicate findings to management.
  • Partner with Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) to analyze reserve risk for use in capital modeling purposes.
  • Assist with quarterly financial and regulatory reporting (quarter close) and provide data and exhibits for annual statement reporting, including ECO and ULE reporting requirements.
  • Collaborate with Claims, Finance, Pricing, Data Science, and Technology teams to improve data quality, streamline processes, and achieve reserving modernization objectives.
  • Work effectively both independently and as part of a team to achieve the organization's financial, strategic, and operational objectives.

Qualifications:

  • BS in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related area
  • ACAS or FCAS
  • 4 or more years of experience in reserving and/or pricing
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Work well both independently and as part of a team
  • Proficiency in Excel, SQL, SAS, Python, R, or other programming languages preferred
  • Strong business and collaboration skills and responsive to service needs and operational demands
  • Effective time management skill
  • Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Strong work ethic

Job Description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Claims Specialist to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims


Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair, and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

Picture yourself building a successful career at AIG working alongside other talented, highly motivated individuals committed to reaching our goal of becoming the world's leading insurance provider. We believe that our success depends on building a world class team. If you would like to be a part of our team, we invite you to consider putting your talents to work with the AIG Claims department.


We are seeking an experienced Casualty Claims Adjuster to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and resolve Commercial Auto Liability and Commercial General Liability claims. The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in liability analysis, injury evaluation, coverage interpretation, and litigation management, with the ability to independently handle a moderate to complex caseload from initial notice through resolution. This role requires sound judgment, strong analytical skills, and the ability to balance customer service, financial stewardship, and technical claim expertise. The adjuster will work closely with insureds, claimants, attorneys, brokers, and internal business partners to deliver timely, fair, and compliant claim outcomes. You'll be responsible for:


Claim Investigation, Evaluation and Negotiation

  • Conduct prompt, thorough investigations to determine coverage, liability, damages, and compensability.
  • Gather and evaluate evidence, including statements, police reports, medical records, expert reports, and other relevant documentation.
  • Analyze coverage issues and prepare reservation of rights, denial, and other coverage correspondence as appropriate.
  • Evaluate bodily injury, property damage, and exposure-related claims to determine appropriate resolution strategies.
  • Independently negotiate settlements within established authority levels.
  • Develop and execute proactive claim resolution strategies that achieve timely and cost-effective outcomes.
  • Identify and mitigate claim exposure through effective investigation, evaluation, and negotiation.
  • Ensure accurate claim documentation supporting all decisions and actions taken throughout the life of the claim.

Litigation Management

  • Manage litigated files and coordinate with defense counsel to develop case strategies.
  • Review pleadings, discovery responses, deposition summaries, and legal evaluations.
  • Monitor litigation budgets and legal expenses to ensure efficient claim handling.
  • Participate in mediations, settlement conferences, and other dispute resolution proceedings as necessary.

Financial and Regulatory Stewardship

  • Establish and maintain accurate indemnity and expense reserves with documented rationale.
  • Continuously evaluate reserve adequacy throughout the life cycle of the claim.
  • Ensure compliance with company guidelines, statutory requirements, and regulatory standards across all applicable jurisdictions.
  • Maintain diary and workload management systems to effectively prioritize and resolve assigned inventory.

Customer and Stakeholder Management

  • Deliver exceptional customer service through professional, timely, and empathetic communication.
  • Build strong working relationships with insureds, brokers, claimants, attorneys, and internal stakeholders.
  • Communicate claim status, strategy, and exposure effectively to management and business partners.

What you'll need to succeed:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 4 years + Commercial Auto Liability and/or Commercial General Liability claims handling experience.
  • Demonstrated experience handling bodily injury claims involving moderate to significant exposure.
  • Experience interpreting policy coverage and drafting coverage position letters, reservation of rights letters, and denial letters.
  • Experience managing both litigated and non-litigated claims.
  • Excellent analytical, investigative, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Active Property & Casualty Adjuster License preferred; must obtain required state licensing within six months of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Litigation management experience.
  • Multi-state claims handling experience.
  • Experience handling serious bodily injury claims.
  • Professional designations such as AIC, CPCU, ARM, or SCLA.
  • Prior experience with commercial insurance carriers handling middle-market or large commercial accounts.

Actuarial Associate
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Actuarial Associate to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Actuarial

Our Actuaries are on the front lines, quantifying risk, pricing insurance and reserving losses for AIG's major insurance operating companies, globally. We collaborate with Finance, Claims, Operations, Marketing and Risk Management, among other functions. As an AIG actuary, you will be challenged and encouraged to reach your greatest potential to help improve how we predict, manage and mitigate risk.

How you will create an impact

We are seeking an actuary with industry expertise to support the Pricing function within our Lexington Excess Casualty segment. The position involves profitability analysis/ deep dive, large accounts pricing review, monthly business KPI reporting, assisting with annual budget and setting portfolio strategy. They will partner with other actuaries in implementing best practices, analytical techniques and assessing the impact of loss trends and claims emergence.

  • Support development of pricing models and rate indications using actuarial and statistical techniques
  • Prepare, validate, and reconcile data used in pricing analyses
  • Assist in pricing analyses, rate proposals, and supporting documentation for business partners
  • Support implementation of rating changes in systems, including testing and validation
  • Monitor loss trends and portfolio performance metrics and flag notable changes
  • Assist with research of market trends, competitor behavior, and external factors affecting pricing
  • Produce recurring reports supporting portfolio monitoring and pricing decisions
  • Document methodologies, assumptions, and outputs used in pricing analyses

What you'll need to succeed

  • BS in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related area
  • Completion of one or more actuarial exams
  • Foundational knowledge of pricing methodologies (rate adequacy, segmentation, trend)
  • Ability to support pricing analyses using structured data under guidance
  • Familiarity with pricing data, validation, and tools
  • Basic understanding of governance and the business impact of pricing decisions
  • Ability to keep manager and immediate team informed on progress, issues, and results

Full job description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as an Underwriting Specialist in our new Contract Extra division and play a key role in launching and growing this exciting new initiative within Western World. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

For more than 50 years, Western World has provided wholesale distribution partners with innovative non-admitted insurance solutions. Combined with the strength and capabilities of Lexington Insurance, Western World offers a broad suite of E&S products that help agents and address complex risks ranging from Main Street businesses to sophisticated middle market accounts.


This is a unique opportunity for a highly experienced E&S casualty underwriter to help shape the future of a growing business segment while serving as a technical casualty expert and mentor to others within the organization.


How you will create an impact

  • Underwrite and manage a profitable portfolio of casualty & package business, including new and renewal submissions.
  • Analyze exposures, loss history, financial information, and underwriting data to make sound risk selection and pricing decisions.
  • Negotiate terms, conditions, pricing, and coverage structures with wholesale partners.
  • Maintain underwriting authority while ensuring compliance with company guidelines, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as the casualty subject matter expert for the division, providing guidance and technical support to less experienced underwriters.
  • Partner with leadership to drive casualty growth initiatives and execute business strategies within targeted segments and industries.
  • Help identify trends in production, retention, rate achievement, and loss performance, recommending actions to improve portfolio results.
  • Build and strengthen relationships with key agency partners through regular engagement, joint business planning, and agency visits.
  • Mentor and develop less experienced underwriters through coaching, training, and sharing of underwriting best practices.
  • Monitor marketplace conditions, competitive activity, and emerging casualty exposures to identify growth opportunities and potential risks.
  • Conduct agency visits and represent Western World at industry events and marketing functions


What you'll need to succeed


  • Minimum of 7+ years of E&S Casualty underwriting experience, including experience handling middle market and larger accounts.
  • Strong technical expertise in casualty underwriting, including General Liability, Products liability and Excess Liability. Some property experience is a plus.
  • Proven ability to evaluate complex risks and make sound underwriting decisions.
  • Proven ability to mentor less experienced underwriters
  • Strong negotiation, communication, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience underwriting package business, including working knowledge of commercial property coverages and exposures.
  • Existing relationships within the wholesale brokerage community.
  • CPCU, AU, ARM, ASLI, or other relevant professional designations.
  • Experience working within delegated underwriting authority environments and the E&S marketplace.

About this job

Handle complex Directors & Officers Liability claims and related management liability exposures for AIG's Financial Lines Claims team. Independently negotiate multi-million dollar claims, oversee investigation strategy, and manage litigation budgets with authority over case disposition.

Good fit if you have 6+ years of complex claims or litigation experience, strong negotiation skills, and expertise in claims management and litigation control.

Full job description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Complex Claims Director – Management Liability to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

As Complex Claims Director for Management Liability, you will be responsible for handling all aspects of our highest severity D&O claims with opportunity to handle high exposure Employment Practices Liability and Fiduciary Liability claims and you will have the unique opportunity to work with some of the industry's top talent in Financial Lines Claims. You are respected for your deep technical expertise and/or ability to oversee programs and processes. You have balanced the needs of multiple stakeholders, making sound decisions using data, analysis, experience and judgment, along with the appropriate risk mindset. Ultimately, you take ownership for key outcomes. This position requires:

  • Determining the scope and extent of available coverage.
  • The investigation, evaluation and disposition of new and existing Directors & Officers Liability claims including possibly Employment Practices Liability and Fiduciary Liability claims.
  • Preparation and execution of investigation strategies which identify critical issues effecting liability, causation and damages and assessment of risk transfer and contribution opportunities.
  • Clear and concise communication and contact with internal and external customers, including insureds, brokers and underwriters, to provide guidance and manage expectations.
  • Proper documentation of exposure evaluation and resolution strategy.
  • Frequently present to senior management of claim disposition recommendations.
  • Obtain the appropriate authority to independently negotiate multi-million dollar claims with the top plaintiff attorneys nationwide. Document evaluation, thought process, and strategy. Utilize ADR as appropriate and necessary.
  • Effectively strategize and budget litigation of each claim through discussions with counsel, vendors and insureds. Establish with defense and coverage counsel clear ground rules in order to maintain financial control of budget and expenses.
  • 10% travel.

What you will need to succeed

  • 6+ years of experience handling complex insurance claims, litigation or other related experience; management liability claims experience highly preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills (verbal/written) and strong negotiation skills.
  • Advanced experience and capabilities in litigation claims management including ADR and mediation process.
  • Experience attending and controlling cases: pre-suit, litigated, post-trial, at mediations, settlement conferences, etc.
  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent required. JD highly preferred. Multi-state adjuster licenses preferred.
  • Motivation and interest in the potential for an upwardly mobile career path.

Ready to make a bigger impact? We look forward to reviewing your application.

Support delivery of strategic initiatives across AIG's global account portfolio, including program launches and growth initiatives. This role coordinates across multiple functions and markets to translate business strategies into executable plans.

Good fit if you have 3-5 years in account management or program delivery, strong organizational skills, and preferably insurance or multi-market experience.

Full job description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Global Account Manager to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


The Global Account Manager is responsible for supporting the delivery of strategic initiatives across the global account portfolio. Reporting to the AVP, Global Account Manager, this role is responsible for meeting our client commitments, managing key components of new program launches, and supporting growth initiatives.

This role sits within account management but operates across functions, driving alignment, accountability, and progress across complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives. This role ensures that strategic priorities and client commitments are translated into clear, executable plans and delivered successfully across the organization.

We are seeking an individual who can operate independently, bring structure to ambiguity, and effectively coordinate across teams, while also developing the materials and analysis needed to support decision-making.


How You Will Create an Impact

  • Partner directly with the Global Account Manager to support execution of key account initiatives, including program launches, customer experience, expansions, and operational changes across multiple markets
  • Translate business development strategies and client commitments into clear action plans with defined owners, timelines, and dependencies
  • Track progress, identify risks, and proactively drive resolution of issues
  • Have a strong understanding of the different regulatory market requirements
  • Experience building business cases, summaries, and structured reporting
  • Serve as the central point of coordination across legal, underwriting, claims, finance, product, and IT to align on priorities and deliverables
  • Ensure teams are coordinated and informed, with clear expectations and timelines
  • Escalate and help resolve blockers impacting delivery
  • Communicate with client counterparts to maintain alignment on timing and deliverables
  • Bring structure to how initiatives are tracked and executed across the account (timelines, trackers, dependencies)
  • Maintain documentation and working files to support transparency and continuity across initiatives
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes and ways of working
  • Learn pricing and P&Ls to ensure track efficiencies and measure post launch success
  • Support preparation for internal and client-facing updates, including QBRs and executive readouts
  • Track KPIs and understand how we measure success across our different programs

What You'll Need to Succeed


  • 3-5 years of experience in account management, operations, program delivery, or similar roles within complex environments
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Ability to operate independently and drive progress without constant direction
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills
  • Experience in insurance, warranty, or service contract programs is preferred
  • Experience supporting global or multi-market initiatives is preferred

Quick facts

  • Pay: $112,000 to $140,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Wilton, CT
  • Experience: 7+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Manager role overseeing accounting and reporting for AIG's $95 billion invested assets portfolio, including fixed maturity securities, derivatives, and alternative investments. Responsibilities include monthly and quarterly close processes, investment disclosures for regulatory filings, and implementation of accounting improvements across global entities.

Good fit if you have 7+ years accounting experience with investment products, strong GAAP and statutory reporting knowledge, and expertise in fixed maturity and equity accounting.

Full job description

Who we are

AIG, Inc. is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world's most far-reaching property casualty networks. AIG, Inc. (“AIG”) offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network. Customers value AIG's strong capital position, extensive risk management and claims experience and its ability to be a market leader in critical lines of the insurance business.

Corporate Finance - Investment Accounting

The Investment Accounting group at AIG is responsible for the accounting and reporting for AIG's Invested Assets of over $95 billion a comprised primarily of fixed maturity securities and includes private equity, hedge funds, commercial/residential loans and equity securities. In addition, AIG's derivative portfolio consists primarily of foreign exchange derivatives but also includes interest rate and other derivative instruments.

The Investment Accounting group's specific responsibilities include reconciliation of transactional data from various sub-ledgers to the general ledger and ultimately AIG's financial statements as well as all related external reporting for investments (10Q/K, Financial Supplement, STAT Audited Financials, Investment NAIC reporting and various government regulatory reports). AIG has multiple legal entities around the globe.

The team is also responsible for establishing the accounting for new transactions or new investment products, implementation of new GAAP and STAT accounting standards as it relates to invested assets, the implementation of new accounting systems as it relates to invested assets, and management of the risks, controls and AIG audit as it relates to investments and supporting Investment FP&A.

Responsibilities

  • Execute and manage accounting processes related to the monthly and quarterly accounting close to ensure accuracy of AIG's invested assets data across all entities
  • Support the review and preparation of certain Investment disclosures for AIG 10Q/K and Financial Supplement, including as appropriate the Investment, Lending, Fair Value, VIE Footnotes and Investment MD&A
  • Support the review and preparation of NAIC statutory reporting and other regulatory reporting requirements
  • Lead the implementation of process improvements, in coordination with other areas of the department/organization
  • Key point of contact and support for the various business unit and corporate controllers
  • Coordinate with various areas in the organization to develop an understanding of new investment transactions and to provide guidance/support that ensures the accounting results from these investments are accurately recorded in the AIG ledgers
  • Perform ad-hoc analytical requests

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance
  • 7+ years' experience in accounting and reporting for investment products
  • Strong understanding of investment products and accounting treatment for fixed maturity, equity, and other investment products
  • Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principle (GAAP) and the recording of investments-related journal entries
  • Strong knowledge of statutory reporting gained in part by preparation of statutory reporting schedules
  • Experience with foreign currency remeasurement and translation
  • Excellent analytical skills, including experience performing investment data analysis including commentary
  • Experience reviewing work papers supporting disclosures
  • High level of competency using Microsoft Excel including pivot tables and formulas to create/manage investment data, review investment data and perform analysis
  • Ability to work collaboratively with teams in multiple locations
  • Ability to balance multiple projects at once, to prioritize appropriately, and to approach the work with a sense of urgency and strong attention to detail to produce high quality results in a time sensitive environment
  • Team-player mindset geared towards process improvements and the implementation of accounting controls to ensure consistency and data quality of the team's financial output
  • High level of motivation and initiative, ability to work independently, including strong organizational skills
  • Comfort level working within a dynamic and complex organizational structure
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to maintain relationships at all levels within the organization
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff, peers, senior management and other external and internal audiences
  • Computer proficiency with a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, database experience a plus
  • Experience with PAM/Aladdin a plus

For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $112,000-$140,000. For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $110,000-$138,000. The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. Quick facts

  • Pay: $112,000 to $138,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: New York, NY

About this job

Lead AIG's greenhouse gas inventory, carbon accounting program, and sustainability performance tracking. Manage data governance, cross-functional partnerships, and external reporting while translating climate strategy into business insights.

Good fit if you have five years of corporate sustainability experience, strong GHG accounting knowledge, and project management skills.

Full job description

Sustainability Manager, Carbon Accounting and Performance

Purpose: The Sustainability Manager will lead the company's greenhouse gas inventory and carbon accounting program for AIG's operations, ensuring accurate data, strong governance, regulatory alignment, and readiness for external reporting and assurance. The role will also track sustainability performance, support climate strategy, manage cross-functional programs, and translate technical topics into clear business insights and stakeholder communications. The ideal candidate brings strong sustainability and GHG expertise, analytical and project management skills, and the ability to collaborate effectively across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

GHG Inventory Governance & Operations Oversight – 50%

  • Own the annual operations GHG emissions inventory, including methodology, boundaries, assumptions and emissions factors and maintain a transparent, consistent and well-documented Inventory Management Plan that is ready for external reporting and assurance.
  • Manage the company's carbon accounting platform vendor, including system performance, data quality, enhancements and issue resolution.
  • Partner with the Operations lead and Sustainability Controller to establish clear roles, requirements, timelines, review protocols and documentation standards.
  • Partner with the Operations lead, sustainability data providers and third-party vendors to ensure timely, accurate and complete data collection and reporting.
  • Review and validate inventory results, including data quality, reasonableness, year-over-year changes and significant assumptions.
  • Oversee tracking, monitoring and reporting of GHG emissions regulatory requirements across legal entities and review legal entity GHG reporting for consistency and alignment with Group.
  • Partner with the Sustainability Controller to support GHG reporting controls, documentation, audit evidence and external assurance.
  • Monitor evolving GHG accounting standards and reporting expectations, assess their implications and improve the efficiency, consistency and governance of carbon accounting processes.

Sustainability Performance Management – 20%

  • Build cross-functional partnerships to align sustainability priorities, targets and performance measurement with business objectives.
  • Develop dashboards, scorecards and other tools to track sustainability performance and support reporting, communications and decision-making.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of sustainability programs against business goals, stakeholder expectations and relevant industry benchmarks.
  • Apply credible frameworks, emissions pathways and industry methodologies to support the company's climate strategy and net zero commitments.
  • Provide subject-matter expertise to Sustainability Working Groups and help business and functional teams identify opportunities to advance sustainability and decarbonization priorities and integrate sustainability in business decision-making processes.
  • Monitor emerging sustainability developments, industry practices and stakeholder expectations to inform strategy and performance benchmarks.

Engagement and Program Delivery – 20%

  • Manage the development and execution of the company's sustainability engagement strategy.
  • Guide and support Sustainability Working Groups, business champions and the Employee Sustainability Network in advancing shared priorities.
  • Support the identification and management of external partnerships with industry groups, NGOs, academic institutions and other organizations aligned with the sustainability strategy.
  • Translate sustainability strategy and technical topics into clear, business-relevant messages, recommendations and actions.
  • Develop events, thought leadership, sponsorships and engagement initiatives that strengthen the Sustainability Office's visibility and support stakeholder expectations.
  • Measure the reach and impact of sustainability engagement activities and recommend improvements.
  • Manage cross-functional projects from planning through delivery, coordinating contributors, timelines, risks, deliverables and senior-management updates.

Additional Responsibilities – 10%

  • Develop clear presentations, disclosures and other materials that communicate sustainability priorities, performance and progress internally and externally (e.g., leadership meetings, CDP Climate Change Questionnaire, Ecovadis, content for annual sustainability report, ad-hoc requests)
  • Lead research and analysis on priority topics, including materiality, climate and GHG reporting, and present actionable insights to senior stakeholders.
  • Promote the Sustainability Office's visibility across the enterprise.
  • Support additional sustainability priorities and special projects as business needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of five years of corporate sustainability experience.
  • Strong knowledge of GHG emissions accounting, methodologies and reporting requirements, and decarbonization strategies including renewable energy procurement.
  • Familiarity with evolving sustainability regulations and disclosure frameworks and standards, such as the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Science-based Target Initiative Standards (SBTi), RE 100.
  • Demonstrated project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt plans and deliver high-quality work on time.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex information and present clear, actionable insights to senior management and executive audiences.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex technical topics for diverse stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to build relationships and collaborate effectively across business lines, functions and stakeholder groups.
  • Experience with ESG data providers (e.g., MSCI, ISS, CDP, Sustainalytics, Ecovadis) and carbon accounting and management software.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint and Teams.
  • Experience with Watershed (or similar carbon accounting platform) and Workiva strongly preferred
  • Experience improving processes, supporting change and working independently with sound judgment and initiative.
  • Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience in insurance or financial services a plus

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Sustainability or Environmental-related field, Business or other discipline that aligns with corporate sustainability initiatives preferred. A master's degree in a similar field is desired.

About this job

Account Coordinator supporting AIG's US captive insurance management operations in Burlington, Vermont. Role focuses on financial reporting, regulatory compliance, and client service for a portfolio of captive insurance companies.

Good fit if you have accounting experience, strong Excel skills, attention to detail, and can work independently to meet filing deadlines.

Full job description

Who we are

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks, and provide for retirement security.

Get to know the business

AIG Insurance Management Services is seeking to hire a captive insurance professional to support our US captive management operations. This position is expected to focus on financial reporting, customer service, and continuing AIG's strong reputation in the captive management marketplace. The ability to report on results in a timely manner with accuracy is a must.

About the role

What you need to know:

As an Account Coordinator this position will manage a small portfolio of captive insurance companies while supporting colleagues that are managing large and complex captive insurance companies. This position will be the primary contact for all captive operations which includes financial statement preparation and regulatory compliance on behalf of captive owners.

This role interacts with and ensures strong relationships with clients, regulators, captive directors, and key service providers. Our team cares about providing good customer service, being responsive, and working in a positive environment.

Performance Objectives include:

    • Client Management: Responsibilities include being the clients' primary contact, preparation of financial statements, and ensuring captives are compliant with all regulatory requirements which includes various filings for each client accurately and with specified deadlines.
    • Non-Routine Client Management: Perform special requests for clients, which may include tasks such as business plan changes, preparing financial proformas, or analyzing new agreements. Keep reviewer informed and involved early on with any non-routine changes as well as ask for guidance when needed.
    • Communication/Relationships: Responsible for the day-to-day client and service providers' communications for matters relating to captive business operations and insurance programs. This position must liaison with several professionals, including domicile regulators, auditors, actuaries, tax advisors, bankers, and legal advisors.

What we're looking for:

    • Accounting experience with attention to detail.
    • Either hold or working towards an associate's or bachelor's degree in accounting, business, or related field preferred.
    • Excellent Excel skills.
    • Previous experience working within a team environment to meet filing deadlines.
    • Excellent organizational skills.
    • Ability to think through and complete tasks independently.
    • Ability to make contributions on special projects as needed.
    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
    • A growth mentality with willingness to accept feedback.

Ready to win together? We would love to hear from you.

Full job description

​Underwriting Specialist, Accident and Health

Join us as an Underwriting Specialist to make more of your specialist expertise and experience.


Make your mark in Underwriting

AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


The role will work closely with Sales, Claims and Operations, Finance, Legal, Risk and Compliance to help achieve strategic initiatives, which will ensure long-term growth of profits for Accident and Health.


How you will create an impact

  • This role is your opportunity to drive profitable growth in Accident & Health by working on creative solutions for complex risks. Using your proven relationship building skills, you will be responsible for underwriting a range of new and renewal business in both Corporate and Specialty Markets business.
  • As a member of the team, you will set a high standard of customer service to brokers and clients – providing an example for junior colleagues to follow. You will also provide guidance, mentoring and training to less-experienced underwriters – and support them in building their broker network.

Underwriting / Portfolio Management

  • Responsible for underwriting new and renewal business of both Corporate and Specialty Markets, including negotiating pricing, terms, and conditions.
  • Monitor the adherence to underwriting requirements and guidelines for assigned book of business.
  • Maintain underwriting discipline by adhering to underwriting guidelines, directives, and delegated authority limits.
  • Review portfolio analytics and provide leadership in decision making on required actions.
  • Develop strong, long-term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business.
  • Assist manager & underwriters in collaborating with Distribution, Business & Product Leaders, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers.
  • Identify the need for and manage special underwriting projects as needed.
  • Foster a culture that promotes collaboration, innovation, diversity, equity and inclusion

What you will need to succeed

  • Minimum of 8+ years of experience with Accident & Health products with proven technical underwriting skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategies to grow profitability and production growth.
  • Strong customer service ethic, with a sound understanding of the business processes.
  • Excellent communication (oral and written) and influencing skills and proven ability to collaborate and work across multiple areas of the organization.
  • Demonstrated planning, execution, and negotiation skills.
  • Self-motivated and able to set strategic direction.
  • Able to work in a team to lead and contribute so that AIG meets its strategic goals.
  • Knowledge of country regulatory and compliance requirements.
  • Strong presentation, prioritization, and time management.
  • Proven ability to motivate and gain commitment and trust from market and colleagues.
  • Knowledge of market segmentation, portfolio management, acquisition, and multiple distribution systems.
  • Ability to multi-task and handle divisional objectives as requested and handles multiple priorities often under tight deadlines.
  • Strong sense of responsibility for one's actions and work.

About this job

Handle complex marine claims including Motor Truck Cargo, Vehicle Physical Damage, and Commercial Property. Work with brokers, experts, and legal representatives to investigate claims and identify fraud while maintaining AIG's quality standards.

Good fit if you have marine claims knowledge, experience in negotiation or mediation, and strong communication and problem-solving skills.

Full job description

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Marine Complex Claims Adjuster to play your part in that transformation. It's an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

As a Major Loss Adjuster, you will be focused on handling all aspects of Motor Truck Cargo, Vehicle Physical Damage, Car Hauler Liability, Commercial Property, Contractors Equipment, and Warehouse legal Liability claims. This role is an ideal opportunity to develop your expertise in handling and investigating complex claims. You will deal with genuine claims through a proactive, best practice approach, in line with AIGs quality standards – you will actively promote and demonstrate the principles of ‘Treating Customers Fairly' in claims handling. Additional responsibilities include:

  • You will proactively identify and review suspect/fraudulent claims on a consistent basis – dealing with such claims in line with our clear guidelines.
  • Your work will involve regular contact with internal stakeholders and brokers, (medical) experts, clients' lawyers, victims or their legal representatives. We want you to build effective relationships with internal and external customers, while acting as a point of referral.
  • You will have the opportunity to grow your experience by providing support to Team Managers and deputizing in their absence. For example, you will assist with monitoring market/industry practices in claims handling.
  • Use the claims experience you gain to help improve our products in collaboration with colleagues in underwriting.

What you'll need to succeed

  • Knowledge of legal / regulatory and litigation / procedural requirements for marine claims.
  • Specialist knowledge of marine technical claims topics is preferred.
  • At least some experience in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.
  • Policy language skills enabling accurate and consistent policy wording interpretation.
  • Lateral thinking and the ability to problem solve and develop new ideas to improve working practices.
  • Strong communication, time management, administrative and report-writing skills.

Ready to accelerate your career? We would love to hear from you.

The Senior Underwriter will contribute to the growth of the business by underwriting Inland Marine products under general direction, issuing quotes and policies while ensuring standards and compliance guidelines are met. The position is responsible for underwriting large accounts and building relationships with clients and brokers. Other responsibilities include:

  • Evaluating, prioritizing and selecting submissions to be underwritten
  • Delivering strategic account reviews and preparing associated file documentation
  • Adhering to underwriting guidelines and discipline
  • Assisting management with the implementation of profit center strategic initiatives and providing technical underwriting and marketing support on other projects
  • Assisting regional manager and product leaders in developing existing and establishing new broker relationships
  • Collaborating with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business to target business development opportunities
  • Working with management, brokers, clients, and other partners on deal structure, contract terms and conditions on a portfolio of more complex risks
  • Representing AIG at client and broker functions
  • Contributing to the development of less experienced staff
  • Participating in special underwriting projects as needed
  • Providing superior customer service to brokers and clients (internal & external)

What you'll need to succeed

  • Understanding of Inland Marine Insurance and associated risks including fundamentals of loss trends, loss triangles, and ratemaking etc. with a focus on Transportation and Logistic risks
  • Must be detail-oriented, possess analytical, critical thinking and problem solving skills, and be able to make decisions based on level of authority
  • Effective in dynamic environment, adaptable, comfortable with ambiguity, working at pace and prioritizing multiple tasks
  • Strong communication skills (written and verbal), collaboration, building trust with wide range of colleagues and clients
  • Financial acumen, appetite for learning about the industry, negotiating skills and a focus on writing profitable business
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience; Commercial Insurance Company, Agency or Brokerage experience preferred; Inland Marine experience preferred

About this job

Design and implement global wireless network architectures for an enterprise, focusing on Wi-Fi 6/6E standards, RF engineering, security, and performance optimization. Lead wireless standards definition, conduct site surveys, and integrate automation and AI-driven monitoring across multi-vendor environments.

Good fit if you have 10+ years designing large-scale enterprise wireless networks, deep RF and WLAN expertise, and strong security and automation knowledge.

Full job description

About the role


The Wireless Network Engineer is a technical leader in wireless networking, responsible for designing and implementing global wireless network architectures that align with industry best practices, organizational needs, ensuring high performance, scalability and security. We are seeking a highly skilled Wireless Network Engineer with expertise in wireless network infrastructures to define and enforce wireless standards, including RF design principles, authentication frameworks, encryption protocols, security, compliance and robust performance. This is a key role in defining enterprise-wide wireless standards, ensuring high performance and seamless user experience.


Responsibilities


  • Lead engineer responsible for designing and developing scalable and highly available wireless network architectures that align with enterprise goals, industry standards and best practices.
  • Define and enforce wireless standards, including RF planning principles, authentication frameworks, encryption protocols, compliance, and performance optimization.
  • Develop and maintain standardized wireless configurations that ensure consistent operation and interoperability in multi-vendor environments.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert in Wi-Fi technologies, particularly IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6/6E) and 802.11ac standards.
  • Coordinate and conduct predictive modeling and site surveys to ensure optimal RF coverage, signal integrity, and client density planning.
  • Implement AI-driven insights and machine learning-based analytics to proactively monitor user experiences, identify anomalies, and accelerate issue resolution.
  • Integrate self-healing capabilities into the wireless network to enable automatic remediation of common performance and connectivity issues.
  • Utilize intent-based networking principles to align wireless configurations with user needs and business intent, reducing manual intervention.
  • Drive the use of automation platforms for configuration management, policy enforcement, and streamlined operational workflows.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, security, and application teams to ensure wireless solutions support current and future business initiatives.
  • Continuously evaluate emerging technologies and provide strategic guidance on adoption and integration to support innovation and efficiency.
  • Evaluate emerging wireless technologies and trends, providing guidance to stakeholders on adoption strategies and their potential impact.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align wireless strategies with enterprise network architecture, security, and digital initiatives.
  • Ensure network security through robust wireless encryption protocols, authentication mechanisms, and compliance with regulatory standards.
  • Articulate design rationale, flexibly adapt solutions, and iterate designs when required.
  • Work closely with senior management, network engineering and operations teams.
  • Act as an escalation engineer for high severity network related production issues, work with engineers and various vendors to identify tactical and strategic solutions.

Requirements


  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, or related field, such as Computer Science or Information Technology or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of proven experience designing, deploying, and managing large-scale wireless enterprise networks, project delivery with focus on user experience, performance optimization and scalability.
  • Extensive experience in wireless network engineering, design, and optimization in enterprise environments.
  • Deep understanding of RF engineering principles and WLAN technologies, including Wi-Fi 6/6E and 802.11ac standards.
  • Strong background in wireless network security, including authentication, encryption, and compliance frameworks.
  • Proficient in the use of site survey and RF planning tools for predictive and real-time analysis.
  • Experience with multi-vendor wireless ecosystems and interoperability planning.
  • Familiarity with automation frameworks and proactive network management practices.
  • Hands-on experience in large-scale wireless deployments across campus, retail, or high-density environments.
  • Knowledge of location-based services, BLE technologies, and mobile engagement strategies.
  • Experience analyzing, gathering, and auditing large-scale and complex data sets to uncover new trends and patterns that influence architecture direction.
  • Proven experience recommending network improvements, including cost/benefit analysis, to meet changing business requirements.
  • Prior experience planning large-scale projects through vendor comparison and cost studies.
  • Sharp troubleshooting faculties, deductive reasoning, and careful attention to detail.
  • Independent and self-directed work ethic when participating in a collaborative environment.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Dedicated commitment to service availability and quality user experience.
  • Must be results driven with a strong sense of urgency.

Nice to Have

  • Demonstrated ability to utilize AI-driven tools for network visibility, root cause analysis, and performance metrics is nice to have
  • Industry certifications on Wireless Networking is preferred.

If your compensation expectations are above the posted range, we still encourage you to apply - your unique background matters to us.
